cleared.check: Monad interpreter refactor from v0.16.5 to v0.16.7 (StackTop one-past stack pointer): DUPn, SWAPn, push, pop, pop_for_overwrite, top_two, check_requirements stack size, call_runtime argument pointers and result slot, the runtime context stack pointer and size, and the initial pointer in execute.cpp.
cleared.result: Old code held a pointer to the top word with the empty stack at bottom minus one; new code holds a pointer one past the top with operator[](i) = *(ptr + i - 1). Old *(top - N) equals new top[-N], old top + 1 equals new next_slot(), old top - bottom equals new next_slot() - bottom (bottom moved by one with the pointer), so every changed expression names the same word. A new vector set, stackedge.py, runs DUPn and SWAPn for n = 1 to 16 at the needed depth and one short, pushes to depths 1,014 to 1,025 followed by DUP1, DUP16 and SWAP16, and memory, hashing and copy runtime calls at stack depth 0 to 1,019: 117 of 117 cases equal the model and Ethereum on Monad and on MegaETH, failures included. The PoolManager uses DUP and SWAP up to 16 in every function, so this is the path every eth_call on the 0.16.7 fleet takes.

cleared.check: Monad countl_zero of category/core/runtime/uint256.hpp, rewritten between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 to a loop without early exit; bit_width uses it, and the emitter uses bit_width for MULMOD with a power of two modulus (modop_optimized) and for EXP with a power of two base.
cleared.result: The new loop keeps the value from the most significant nonzero word: 192 - 64 i + clz(word i), and 256 for zero. A transcription agrees with 256 minus the bit length on 200,007 inputs that include every word boundary. The interpreter uses it only for CLZ (opcode 0x1e), which the PoolManager bytecode does not contain; the compiled MULMOD by 2^96 and 2^128 sites of src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48 reach it through bit_width at compile time only.

cleared.check: Correction and extension of the cycle 12 clearance that the only emitter change from v0.16.5 to v0.16.7 is the constant-by-variable shift. Four more compiled-path changes exist. (1) touch_memory, used by every compiled MLOAD and MSTORE with a non-literal offset, skips the bounds and expansion check when the same stack element already passed it for at least the same size.
cleared.result: Safe as read. The size is recorded on the StackElem object (virtual_stack.hpp lines 216-227 and 279). Every StackElem is constructed fresh by placement new with touched_memory_size_ zero (rc_ptr.hpp line 64, virtual_stack.cpp lines 90-94 and 346-361), and every operation that produces a new value returns a new element: release_general_reg, release_avx_reg and alloc_or_release_* move the register into a new_stack_elem (virtual_stack.cpp lines 821-856, emitter.cpp lines 1161-1233); operations that return an input unchanged (x - 0, x & ~0, shift by 0) return the same value. A cached element therefore always holds the value that was checked, memory never shrinks within a frame, and the data pointer is reloaded from the context on each access, so a reallocation by expansion is followed. Literal offsets, such as mload(0) in src/types/Currency.sol:68, are never cached. The cached path is taken for example by mstore(fmp, 0) at src/types/Currency.sol:77 after mstore(fmp, selector) at line 60.

cleared.check: (2) Monad v0.16.7 write_to_final_stack_offsets, which writes the virtual stack back at the end of every compiled basic block: dependency counts moved from an unordered_map keyed by heap address to an array indexed by each element's lowest stack index, elements are visited in stack index order, and stack words that were stored from general registers are loaded word by word into an AVX register (mov_words_to_ymm).
cleared.result: The algorithm is the same topological write with cycle breaking; only the order in which dependency-free elements are taken changes, and the result does not depend on that order. blockexit.py models the code as written on 200,000 random block-exit states (elements in any mix of stack slot, general register, AVX register and literal, one to three stack indices each): both the stack index order and a shuffled order standing for v0.16.5 leave every final stack index with its element's value, and a planted fault that ignores dependencies is caught in 9,479 of 20,000 cases. mov_words_to_ymm puts word 0 and 1 in the low half and 2 and 3 in the high half, matching the little endian slot layout of stack_offset_to_mem256 (emitter.cpp lines 109-116). The scratch register it uses is free at allocation and distinct from the init register and from every element register. The array index stays in range under the invariant v0.16.5 already needed (an element at a slot in [min_delta, top] has its lowest index there). Every JUMP and JUMPI of the PoolManager, among them the TickBitmap and BitMath branches, passes through this code.

cleared.check: (3) Monad v0.16.7 block_prologue stack bound check, changed from 'min_delta < -1024 or max_delta > 1024' to 'max_delta - min_delta > 1024' before the two runtime checks, and (4) MSTORE8 of a value held in a stack slot and the branchless CLZ.
cleared.result: With min_delta at most 0 and max_delta at least 0, every block the new static test rejects is one whose two runtime checks (size at least -min_delta and size at most 1024 - max_delta) no stack size passes, and the old static test is implied by the new one, so both versions fail exactly the same stack sizes and an exceptional halt consumes all gas either way. MSTORE8 now reads four bytes of the little endian slot and stores the low byte, the same byte as before. The PoolManager bytecode has no MSTORE8 (0x53) and no CLZ (0x1e) by linear disassembly of build/PoolManager.json.

This covers storage, balances and nonces, not logs or receipts.

cleared.check: MegaETH mega-evm (main branch; state/cleared.json records Rex6 active on mainnet since 25 August 2026): the handlers it replaces and whether any changes a value, a success flag, return data or gas left for the PoolManager's operands.
cleared.result: From MINI_REX on, all 256 table entries are rebuilt (instructions.rs lines 859-916 and following). Arithmetic, comparison, shift, KECCAK256, CALLDATA*, RETURNDATA*, MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE are the revm handler inside compute_gas_ext, which only records compute gas. SSTORE and LOG gain storage gas and data-size limits (storage_gas_ext, additional_limit_ext). CALL, STATICCALL, DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE go through forward_gas_ext, which caps the gas given to the callee at 98/100 of what remains instead of 63/64 (lines 1064-1180), and from Rex4 through volatile_data_ext, which reverts a call to the block beneficiary only when the calling frame has disabled volatile access and caps later compute gas after an oracle or beneficiary access (lines 40-140, 405-445). SELFBALANCE gains the same beneficiary guard. Measured with a callee that returns GAS: a hook or token called from the PoolManager address gets 97.87 percent of the parent's gas on MegaETH against 98.31 percent on 19 other networks (raw/fwdgas.json). The PoolManager keeps more gas after each callee returns, so its own revert wrapping cannot run short; a callee gets about 0.44 percent less, which changes gas only. The PoolManager never touches the beneficiary and never disables volatile access, so the guard cannot fire on its own calls, and an attacker cannot set that flag in a victim's frame (F-018 records the hook author case).

cleared.check: Callee gas: can an ordinary account make a precompile, predeploy or system contract that burns forwarded gas the recipient of a take or native payout, the hook or a currency inside a transaction that a victim sends through a normal router on an honest pool (lead L-684).
cleared.result: No on all 21 networks, on the text of the code. The PoolManager makes outbound calls at four places only: the native payout and the token transfer of src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, whose target is the currency of the take and whose recipient is the `to` argument chosen by the caller of take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297); the balanceOf staticcall of sync at src/types/Currency.sol:94, whose currency the caller chooses (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288); the hook call of src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, whose target is key.hooks, part of the PoolKey that the pool id hashes (src/PoolManager.sol:132, 151); and the unlock callback to msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:110). In a victim's swap or removal on an honest pool, the currencies and the hook are fixed by the pool and the recipient and the callback target are fixed by the victim's router and calldata. No storage that a third party can write steers any of these targets. A gas-burning address can therefore appear only in a transaction the attacker builds, where it costs the attacker gas and reverts the attacker's own unlock. Where a hook address is a special address, the low 14 bits decide which callbacks run: HyperEVM 0x0800 to 0x0813 all set BEFORE_ADD_LIQUIDITY (Hooks.sol:32), so no deposit can enter such a pool; Monad 0x1000 sets AFTER_INITIALIZE (Hooks.sol:30), so the pool cannot be created; Arc 0x1800..00 has no flag bits and is never called. Gas forwarding is 63/64 everywhere except MegaETH (98/100), so after a callee burns its gas the PoolManager keeps at least 1/64 to revert. A victim's swap or removal therefore cannot be made to fail or to cost far more on any of the 21 networks through callee gas.

cleared.check: Whether the PoolManager-only replay can fail: the reference interpreter was given a planted MULMOD fault (result off by one when the modulus is 2^256-1, the modulus FullMath.mulDiv uses) and run on 15 matched MegaETH swaps.
cleared.result: All 15 became unmatched, so a wrong 512 bit product on the swap path shows in the frame, log and storage comparisons. The deployed PoolManager runtime on 143, 4326 and 999 equals the build of this checkout byte for byte except the 20 bytes of the immutable address (eth_getCode, 24,009 bytes each), so the program counters of the build's jump map apply to the deployed code.

cleared.check: Whole-transaction replays (every contract, not only the PoolManager) of the first 270 Monad and MegaETH transactions, to see whether the narrower PoolManager-only method hides anything.
cleared.result: Mismatches in the whole-transaction replay traced to the reference interpreter having no gas: a router frame that is given zero gas, and an aggregator that prices the trade with GAS, GASPRICE and BASEFEE. In every such case the PoolManager frames and storage matched once the outside frames were taken from the call tree, which is why the PoolManager-only method was used. This is a limit of the tool, not a difference of the networks.

cleared.check: Lead L-682: which routines ruint 1.20.0 uses on the kona mips64 target for 64 by 64 to 128 bit products and 128 by 64 divisions, and whether the opcode vectors pass through them.
cleared.result: ruint 1.20.0 divides with MG10 reciprocals (reciprocal_mg10 by table and 64 bit products, div_2x1_mg10, div_3x2_mg10, Knuth div_nxm), so no u128 division and no compiler-builtins call (__udivti3, __umodti3, __multi3) occurs: the linked object of the handlers references none, products are DMULTU and DMULT with MFHI and MFLO, and the only divisions are three DDIVU for one-limb operands. The big-endian path of pu128::get (lib.rs:107-118) joins limbs in the right order. Compiled with rustc 1.97.0 for kona's target spec and run in a Cannon-semantics emulator, all 85,544 targeted and 96,876 battery vectors and the pool math checks match; planted faults (MOVN on bit 0, 5 bit DSLLV mask, a DMULTU high word error) give 624, 895 and 1,797 mismatches on 4,278 sampled targeted vectors.

cleared.check: Lead L-683 for Celo: respected game type, implementation, program and who may prove or challenge.
cleared.result: eth_call on Ethereum at block 26,487,021: OptimismPortal 0xc5c5D157 version 5.1.1 and AnchorStateRegistry 0x8fe58d21 both return respectedGameType 42. DisputeGameFactory 0xFbAC1621 gameImpls(42) = 0x1736c101, an OP Succinct fault dispute game version 2.1.0 with aggregationVkey 0x006e44fd...4850, rangeVkeyCommitment 0x543e17e8...1746, SP1 verifier 0x3b604117 and access manager 0x2c4e8f33. proposers(0) and challengers(0) are false, so proposing and challenging are allowlisted; FALLBACK_TIMEOUT is 1,209,600 s, after which proposals open. An ordinary account cannot turn a divergence of the SP1 program into a challenge of an honest root; it could at most propose after 14 days of proposer silence. Which op-succinct release and integer library the range vkey belongs to was not determined.

Its newer AnchorStateRegistry 0xaa45411f (version 3.8.0) returns respectedGameType 1961; gameImpls(1961) = 0x43f4cd26, OP Succinct fault dispute game 2.0.0 with aggregationVkey 0x00be73c0...5902, rangeVkeyCommitment 0x584fd7b9...129c, challenge window 3,600 s, prove window 604,800 s, access manager 0xb0998d01. proposers(0) and challengers(0) are false and FALLBACK_TIMEOUT is 31,536,000,000 s, so proposer and challenger are allowlisted for practical purposes, as L2BEAT states (one proposer, one challenger). cleared.check: Lead L-677: which go-ethereum commit nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f runs, and whether its jump destination cache and opcode handlers differ from 0e44603.
cleared.result: Not readable. raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for OffchainLabs/nitro at b72783f and for v3.13 branch and tag names, and nitro v3.12.4 carries .private-submodules.conf, which rewrites the go-ethereum and wasmer submodules to their private variants when the repository is built privately, so the rc.9 build most likely uses a private go-ethereum. The newest public pin is v3.12.4 at go-ethereum 0e44603 (GitHub tree page), the commit cycles 9 to 12 read; the fork's public master (461e517) is older and differs only by value-versus-pointer operands in the arithmetic handlers. In 0e44603 the jump destination cache is keyed by the hash from StateDB.GetCodeHash of the resolved address and is filled at SetCallCode (evm.go:348-551, contract.go:93-110), so entries describe the bytes of that hash and a reorg or redelegation changes the hash, not the entry. The opcode answers of the rc.9 endpoints were tested by earlier cycles and match.

cleared.check: KECCAK256 and keccak caching in the Base range program on the zkVM.
cleared.result: In the range program lock alloy-primitives 1.6.1 depends on sha3 0.11.0 and keccak 0.2.0 from the registry, and no crate depends on tiny-keccak or fixed-cache; the sp1-patches entries target tiny-keccak 2.0.2 and sha3 0.10.8, so they do not apply to the hash behind KECCAK256. The opcode therefore runs portable Rust code in the zkVM and no keccak cache is linked. This costs cycles and does not change results; keccak 0.2.0 on RISC-V was not run here.

cleared.check: For each of the 21 networks: could an opcode the PoolManager runs give another result in the build that settles state than on the node, and could an ordinary account use it.
cleared.result: No on all 21 as far as tested. Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM settle on the client that produces blocks (no separate proof build; covered by OPCODES.md checks 1 to 4). OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink: kona-client 1.9.0 on MIPS64, permissionless games, no divergence in the compiled handlers or the prestate scan (this unit). World Chain: op-program 1.9.0 on MIPS64, permissioned, no divergence (cycle 12). Zora and Soneium: no proof program, operator only (cycle 12). Base: SP1 range program on RV64IM, permissionless challenges, no divergence (this unit). Celo and X Layer: OP Succinct with allowlisted challengers, program arithmetic not identified, unknown but not usable by an ordinary account. Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium: wasm replay settled in cycle 12; the go-ethereum of the rc.9 nodes is private and unknown, endpoint answers match.

cleared.check: Swap events with amount0 = amount1 = 0 and price, tick and liquidity unchanged, which the step formulas cannot produce
cleared.result: 451 such events across the windows. PoolManager.swap rejects amountSpecified == 0 (src/PoolManager.sol:193), and a nonzero amount always moves the price or spends the amount (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-437, src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:63-105). The only path to a zero swap is a hook with BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA_FLAG whose specified delta cancels the amount (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:266-277), after which Pool.swap returns ZERO_DELTA without touching state (src/libraries/Pool.sol:320). Every such event whose pool key was found has a hook address with bit 3 set; the rest are on pools whose key no public source gave, and they fit only that path. The event is correct and moves no funds.

The protocol fee of a new pool is zero in this build: initialize sets no protocol fee (src/libraries/Pool.sol:105-106).

cleared.check: Event semantics for pools with hooks that return deltas: the Swap event carries the pool delta of Pool.swap, computed from amountToSwap after the beforeSwap delta, before afterSwap adjusts the caller delta
cleared.result: src/PoolManager.sol:202-250 emits delta.amount0(), delta.amount1() of pool.swap(params) with amountSpecified = amountToSwap, so a hook delta changes the specified amount the loop starts from and never the arithmetic the event reports. The replay therefore needs no special case for return-delta hooks: it derives the specified amount from the event, and all swaps on return-delta hook pools in the windows match. Hook and token behaviour was not swept (owner instruction).

cleared.result: No. memory.go and stack.go are byte identical to upstream go-ethereum v1.17.4. Free clears the whole used length before the buffer returns to the pool, and Resize only reslices into capacity that was zero when allocated.

cleared.check: Interpreter loop of the fork against upstream v1.17.4: does the multi-gas change alter an error path?

cleared.check: Step 2 planted fault: MULMOD(a, b, 2^256 - 1) returns one more than the true remainder, on every call (FAULT=mm1) or only when a*b >= 2^256 (FAULT=mm1big).
cleared.result: mm1: 0 of 614,687 v4 pairs and 0 of 49,726 v3 pairs match, because the 1e6 and Q96 denominators then take the 512 bit branch with a wrong high word. mm1big: unmatched v4 pairs rise from 2,414 to 3,167 and v3 from 5,905 to 7,723, and the full-loop replay of the newest 40,000 blocks goes from 0 to 78 unmatched. The fault is caught only for even denominators. With an odd denominator, twos is 1 and add(div(sub(0, twos), twos), 1) is 0 (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:59-75), so prod1 drops out and the result is prod0 times the inverse modulo 2^256, which is exact whenever the quotient fits. oddden.py confirms this on 400,000 inputs: 0 wrong results for 200,129 odd denominators and 199,871 of 199,871 wrong for even ones. A fault in the high word for an odd denominator therefore cannot change a PoolManager amount unless it moves prod1 between zero and nonzero or across the require at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:30.

cleared.result: The constant denominator at pcs 22330-22377 is 2^128, so this copy computes feesOwed. prod1 is nonzero only when the fee growth delta times liquidity is at least 2^256, which makes feesOwed at least 2^128. cleared.check: Whether the PoolManager's own storage, its transient storage, or the balanceOf staticcall of sync can read a stale word from the reth execution cache branch for a destroyed account without code
cleared.result: The branch is taken only for accounts whose info at the start of the block had the empty code hash and that the block destroyed. The PoolManager has had code since deployment and cannot be destroyed under EIP-6780, so its account is never on the branch and insert_storage replaces each of its written words after every block. Transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14) lives in the EVM journal and is not in the execution cache. The balanceOf read of sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364, src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) reads the token's storage, which can be stale only for a token created in the block that destroyed its address. The account cache entry of a branch account is removed, so its code hash and balance are read fresh, and code is looked up by code hash.

cleared.check: Which accounts can reach the stale branch, including EIP-7702 delegated accounts, accounts emptied under EIP-161, and the contracts a victim pool depends on
cleared.result: Reachable: an address created and self-destructed in one transaction, an account without code that a creation landed on and that self-destructed in the same transaction, and an empty account removed under EIP-161, each re-created later in the same block. All of them carry code deployed in that block. An EIP-7702 delegated account has a non-empty code hash, so a destroyed one would take the clear-everything branch, and it cannot be destroyed because it was not created in the transaction and its nonce is above zero; after its delegation is cleared it keeps storage and a nonce and still cannot be destroyed or created over. Tokens, hooks, routers, PositionManager and Permit2 already used by a pool had code before any such block and cannot be destroyed; a proxy runs its implementation with the proxy's own storage. A victim pool can therefore depend on a branch account only by choosing a token or hook made in that pattern, which is an attacker-made contract (actor pool-creator).

cleared.check: Other caches in front of state on reth based clients, looking for an index that is not the full content or address
cleared.result: The execution cache indexes code by code hash, accounts by full address and storage by (full address, full slot); clear() keeps the code cache because its mapping cannot change. The precompile cache is per precompile address, indexed by the full input bytes, returns an entry only when the stored spec matches and the call has at least the recorded gas, stores only successful outputs that consumed no state gas, and is applied only through map_cacheable_precompiles, which skips precompiles marked stateful; Celo's transfer precompile is built with .stateful() (alloy-celo-evm lib.rs line 125). The payload builder's CachedReads is indexed by address and slot, is pre-filled from a committed block and used only for a job whose parent is that block hash, and falls through to the database for slots it lacks. Base's txpool prewarm keeps its own CachedReads and starts a fresh one for each head. The sparse trie cache feeds only state root computation. The src/ code calls no precompile.

cleared.check: On Monad every served receipt, log and trace comes from RPC nodes that interpret (F-130). Do those nodes check their execution against what the validators agreed on, so that mined results stand for validators that may run compiled code? (lead L-737)
cleared.result: Own reading of monad-bft at tag v0.16.7 (commit 670b8ce5). A proposal for block N carries delayed_execution_results, the full Ethereum header of block N-D (monad-consensus-types/src/block.rs line 92; EthHeader wraps the alloy Header, monad-eth-types, so it holds state root, receipts root, logs bloom and gas used). EthBlockPolicy::check_coherency reads the header the node's own execution wrote to its triedb (monad-eth-block-policy/src/lib.rs lines 1182-1196 and 1271-1290; monad-triedb-utils/src/lib.rs lines 124-154 and 314-342) and returns ExecutionResultMismatch when the two differ. The block tree then leaves the block incoherent and counts rx_bad_state_root (monad-blocktree/src/blocktree.rs lines 280-308). A block that is not coherent is never committed: get_high_committable_qc skips it (blocktree.rs line 369), try_commit returns early (monad-consensus-state/src/lib.rs lines 1459-1467) and prune asserts coherency (blocktree.rs lines 153 and 169). Only newly coherent blocks are handed to execution (lib.rs lines 1542-1558). A node that is not in the validator set runs the same consensus state; only its votes, timeouts and proposals are filtered out (monad-state/src/consensus.rs lines 591-637). So a full node, tracing or not, whose execution of block N-D gave a different state root, receipts root, logs bloom or gas used than the header the validator quorum certified stops committing at block N. rpc.monad.xyz follows the finalized tip, so its interpreter results equal the quorum's for every block it serves, receipts and logs included. If validators run compiled code, its state root, receipts root, logs bloom and gas used have therefore agreed with the interpreter on every mined block, including the 129,567 swaps through the 512 bit branch of FullMath.mulDiv found in cycle 14. What stays without evidence is input that no mined transaction has used.

cleared.check: Do bor v2.11.2 and the unreleased develop branch change the interpreter, the integer library or state handling compared with the builds already tested?
cleared.result: 17 core/vm and core/state files are byte-identical between v2.11.1 and v2.11.2. develop is identical to v2.12.0-beta in 14 core/vm files and in parallel_statedb.go, blockchain.go and worker.go. Every tag and branch pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. The opcode handlers call SDiv, SMod, Exp, AddMod and MulMod with the result aliasing the last operand (instructions.go lines 60, 74, 81, 196 and 202). The library writes the result only after the computation, so the aliasing is harmless. The only correctness fix in a recent release, v1.3.1's DivMod aliasing fix, is a function the interpreter does not call.

cleared.check: Lead L-750: the cache that --precompile-cache adds in bor v2.12.0-beta. What is its key, and can a STATICCALL from sync(X) get a cached result for a different input or a different precompile?
cleared.result: The flag adds the extended keccak store, keyed by string(data) (shared_cache.go lines 160-245), and gives the builder and the serial importer the ecrecover cache. The ecrecover cache serves only address 0x01 with input of at most 128 bytes. Its key is the input right-padded to 128 bytes, which is the padding ecrecover applies anyway. It is skipped when the precompile set is overridden. Gas is charged from RequiredGas on a hit, and the stored and returned slices are clones (evm.go lines 53-116). No other precompile is cached. A sync(0x01) gets the same bytes as an uncached call, and balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) parses them the same way.

cleared.check: Can an ordinary account use Salvador, which gives five accounts code at block 98,688,600, against other users' funds in the PoolManager?

cleared.check: Does the libevm pin of avalanchego master (a335c2ecf4df) or uint256 v1.2.4 change an opcode result for the PoolManager?

cleared.check: T14 configurable accounts as unlock callers, as hooks and as take recipients
cleared.result: A configurable account has the one-byte marker as code. When the PoolManager calls it (unlockCallback at PoolManager.sol:110 or a hook call at Hooks.sol:131-136), the 0xef instruction runs the shim, which answers only isValidSignature, onERC721Received and empty input and reverts otherwise. So unlock from such an account reverts and a pool naming it as hook cannot initialize. A TIP-20 take to it is an ordinary balance credit. The shim writes no state and makes no calls, so nothing reaches other users' funds. Addresses are hashes of a configuration, so one cannot be placed at an existing contract's address.

cleared.check: Whether the T15 zone portal call made inside a PoolManager transfer can re-enter the PoolManager or change the debited amount

The portal is a canonical runtime that derives the token from msg.sender and does not call the PoolManager. A revert only fails the caller's own take.

cleared.result: Window: HyperEVM blocks 50,165,552 to 52,165,551 on the archive client https://rpc.purroofgroup.com, 3,268,303 v3 style Swap logs, 131,330 Mint and 221,319 Burn logs (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-closed-producers-2.work/raw/logs999.jsonl). Pools were identified from their own getters (factory, token0, token1, fee, tickSpacing) and kept only when factory.getPool(token0, token1, fee) or getPool(token0, token1, tickSpacing) returned the pool, which is what a PoolCreated log would establish; the PoolCreated log scan over 52 million blocks was started and abandoned as too slow. 431 pools of 14 factories pass, holding 2,258,337 swaps (69 percent). The largest factories are 0xff7b3e8c00e57ea31477c32a5b52a58eea47b072 (1,115,904 swaps), 0x07e60782535752be279929e2dffdd136db2e6b45 (495,284), 0xb1c0fa0b789320044a6f623cfe5ebda9562602e3 (278,022) and 0x32b9da73215255d50d84feb51540b75acc1324c2 (220,491). Stage A, without RPC: 1,686,939 swaps equal one v3 swap step to the unit from the price, tick and liquidity of the pool's previous log, 35,596 of them through the 512 bit branch of mulDiv or mulDivRoundingUp. No swap reached the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and no logged amount is at or above 2^160. 2,995 swaps end exactly on the price of a tick that is a multiple of the spacing. Stage B, with eth_call at the parent block for slot0, liquidity, the tick bitmap and liquidityNet, and the block's Mint and Burn logs applied in order: all 2,995 end-on-tick groups and random samples of 3,000 groups with a 512 bit step and 25,000 groups that may need one inside a multi-step swap (two random draws, which can overlap), 30,995 groups in all. 33,760 swaps reproduce price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to the unit, 19,015 of them through the 512 bit branch (65,309 mulDiv calls with a product of 512 bits), 7,359 with several steps. 22,032 needed the pool's real fee, which differs from fee() on dynamic fee pools and was found by search: one free parameter is fitted per swap and price, tick, liquidity and both amounts must then all match; most fees found are multiples of 100 pips between 0 and 4,000, and a few are other values such as 10,562. 4 did not reproduce: 0x47a2f2ff4d1e218bba017d19222073eaa07b5740289dcca39cd3c88a2ddae25c (block 50,624,670); 0x5a64629ddf197c4e3c2addd942cf25e0a55d7d0b4b659d56249adb3f9b471458 (block 51,255,107); 0xd144959f18fd332b6c3c8111486b41111e44e91ca82d1cc28ffd01b848df7eca (block 51,371,005); 0x3d3c51a3d7ee8bbd78940198e2850863299c7c9a20ff4d913a9d16251678cef0 (block 51,370,051). Each is explained by the collector: the pool also emitted a liquidity event with topic 0xd78218c0d304e8893cb3200abe394bbc8d5b7804d9c51f236df9fdcf481d02d3 (a Mint variant with ticks in topics 2 and 3) that the collector does not read, and with that event applied the liquidity before the swap equals the logged liquidity in every case (chkmis.py; for 0x47a2f2ff, 3,174,629,732,523,735,714,636 + 6,417,522,110,843,946,721,988 = 9,592,151,843,367,682,436,624, the logged value). Planted faults: MULMOD one too high on 512 bit products made 131 of 137 swaps fail, and getSqrtPriceAtTick one unit high on multiples of 10 made 117 of 121 fail, so the comparison sees both classes. cleared.check: L-732. Which reth revision do the public MegaETH locks name, and does its execution cache keep stale storage for an account that was destroyed and re-created without code in one block?
cleared.result: mega-reth itself is not public (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-reth/main/Cargo.toml returns 404) and the public RPC reports mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc; reth has no v2.2.3 tag (the execution cache file at that tag returns 404). mega-evm v1.7.4's Cargo.toml says it is built against reth v2.3.0 (revm 40.0.3, alloy-evm 0.36.0), and the stateless-validator lock at e1618ed7 pins reth tag v2.3.0 at commit 9384bc53d8c0c77e59cac83fdaaf3b372c6d2216. The execution cache at v2.2.0 and at v2.3.0 (identical to 9384bc53) still has the branch that reth pull request 28148 fixes: when an account was destroyed and its original info had no code, insert_state removes the account from the cache and continues, so a re-created account's new storage is never written to the cache and a value read earlier stays (cached_state.rs lines 904-923 at v2.3.0, 863-882 at v2.2.0). The pull request changes that to remove only when the account has no current info. Whether the MegaETH sequencer reads through this cache cannot be read. The branch only touches an address that held no code at the start of the block and was destroyed and re-created inside it, so it cannot reach the PoolManager's storage or a token or hook that an existing pool already uses; a contract the attacker re-creates is its own, which is at most pool-creator level, and a stale read on the sequencer would publish state that the stateless validator rejects, which is operator level.

Binary search of eth_getTransactionCount on the archive client puts its first transaction in block 37,597,803 (2026-06-12 03:59:16 UTC): system transaction 0x2a36e3161a6271d7bcf0145928660f63fd5a5c0839fdcd2400b081107b991385 (0x01f391a92efbdff628ea8b24a09adaa08a215fca6f7b38cb3db7bbb8ed378b61 on the archive client), USDC transfer(0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24, 2,000,000,000) with gas price 0, next to a system transaction from 0x2000000000000000000000000000000000000000 to that linked contract. This is the AQAv2 rebalance: the Hyperliquid documentation says the treasury deployer designates the treasury address, AQAv2 is activated by validator vote after both deployers stake 500k HYPE and send authorization transactions from their staking accounts, and the linked HyperEVM contract then rebalances with the treasury address in a 9:1 ratio. The address was therefore designated by a staked deployer and activated by validator vote; it is not a contract that HyperCore picked without a record. For the PoolManager to be named the same way, a treasury deployer staking 500k HYPE and a validator vote would be needed, so F-020 stays at operator level.

cleared.check: Can the evm2 JIT crates be built here so that their own differential tests run on the PoolManager runtime?
cleared.result: No. The LLVM backend needs LLVM 23 (crates/jit/README.md), and the machine has LLVM 18.1.3 (llvm-config --version). The workspace Cargo.toml patches the ark crates from a git repository on github.com, which this environment cannot clone, and codeload.github.com returned 403 for source archives of both revisions. The review therefore worked from source: 58 files of crates/jit (codegen, builtins, backend, llvm, runtime, context) were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at 66687c18 and at 35aa3280 by following module declarations (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/crawl.py, copies in research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/r66 and r35), plus crates/evm2 at 66687c18. Between the two revisions 8 of the 58 files differ. In codegen the only change is block_analysis.rs lines 2249-2250, which gives opcodes flagged UNKNOWN no stack inputs, and a test. peephole.rs, const_fold.rs, translate/mod.rs, memory_sections.rs and sections.rs are byte-identical.

cleared.check: Which PoolManager opcodes the JIT sends to builtins that wrap the interpreter's own arithmetic, and whether those builtins match the interpreter.
cleared.result: The runtime (24,009 bytes, no metadata trailer) contains 112 distinct opcodes (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/census.json). DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP with an unknown exponent are calls to builtins (translate/mod.rs 776-803). The builtins call ruint wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, add_mod, mul_mod and pow, and evm2's i256_div and i256_mod (builtins/src/lib.rs 112-160). These are the same functions the interpreter uses, linked natively into the same binary at the same ruint version (builtins are resolved by address, builtins/src/ir.rs 1-40). The rev! macro reads the operands top first and writes the result into the lowest slot, which is the specified order. So MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 at FullMath.sol:24 and with a pool denominator at FullMath.sol:48, SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 and FullMath.sol:112 runs the code that the 185,529 vectors already tested through the interpreter. KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, LOG and the calls are builtins as well (lib.rs 162-575, 762-875) and were read: CALLDATALOAD past the end pads with zeros through evm2 read_word_padded, RETURNDATACOPY fails before charging gas when offset plus length exceeds the return data, MCOPY expands memory to max(dst, src) plus length, KECCAK256 of length 0 touches no memory, TSTORE fails in a static frame and TLOAD does not.

cleared.check: Inline lowering of SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO and the JUMPI condition, transcribed with LLVM poison semantics.
cleared.result: No mismatch. SIGNEXTEND is select(ext < 31, (x << (248 - 8ext)) >>s (248 - 8ext), x), BYTE is select(i < 32, (v >> (248 - 8i)) & 0xff, 0), and the shifts select 0, or for SAR the sign fill, when the count exceeds 255; the poisoned shift result is only in the unselected arm (translate/mod.rs 685-691, 804-875). Comparisons are i256 icmp, ISZERO is icmp eq 0, and JUMPI branches on icmp ne of the whole word (line 1050). jitmodel.py runs these on 631,353 vectors (the battery and targeted sets, every pair of 196 edge values for every index and count, all 256 powers of two and their negations as divisors and moduli) and makes 1,068,620 checks against the specification without a mismatch or undefined operation. Planted faults are caught: BYTE guard < 33 (367 mismatches), shift guard > 256 (1,659), SAR default without the sign (2,746), SIGNEXTEND guard < 30 (31). A SIGNEXTEND guard of < 32 gives no mismatch because index 31 shifts by 0, so that mutation is equivalent. This covers the SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SDIV and SMOD of TickBitmap.compress and position (TickBitmap.sol:20-38, 54-67).

cleared.check: Every peephole rule in peephole.rs, with most care for MULMOD with the constant moduli 2^96, 2^128 and 2^256-1, SDIV and SMOD by -1 and -2^255, EXP with a constant base or exponent, and the inline EXP gas.
cleared.result: No mismatch. A power of two modulus 2^k lowers MULMOD to (a*b mod 2^256) & (2^k - 1) and ADDMOD to (a+b mod 2^256) & (2^k - 1), which is exact because 2^k divides 2^256 (peephole.rs 161-213). This is the path for MULMOD by 2^128 at pc 22378 and by 2^96 at pc 22639, which a PUSH in the same block supplies (census.json). 2^256-1 and 1,000,000 are not powers of two and go to the ruint builtin. SDIV by -1 negates, by -2^255 returns x == -2^255, and by other signed powers of two uses LLVM sdiv, whose only undefined case is excluded; SMOD by 0, 1 or -1 is 0 and by other signed powers of two uses srem, which keeps the dividend's sign (53-160). EXP with a power of two base 2^k is select(e < ceil(256/k), 1 << ke, 0) and charges (263 - clz(e)) / 8 bytes of gas, which equals the specified byte length for every exponent tested (215-305). The PoolManager's own constant operands are a dividend of -887272 or 887272 for SDIV and SMOD (pc 7400-7443) and a dividend of 0xd76453e0 for DIV (BitMath.sol:45), which no rule matches, so they use the builtins. Planting a mask of 2^k instead of 2^k - 1 gives 14,252 mismatches.

cleared.check: Constant folding and range folding in the bytecode analysis (const_fold.rs), including folded constants that are stored in place of an executed instruction (translate/mod.rs 633-656).
cleared.result: No unsound rule. try_const_fold calls ruint and evm2 i256 for the arithmetic and writes its own rules only for DIV and MOD by zero, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE and the three shifts (const_fold.rs 113-168); these were transcribed and match on all vectors. try_range_fold (213-389) gives a range below 2^31 that must hold every result when at least one input is a range or an unknown value. 60,000 random abstract inputs (ranges, inline constants, large constants including the BitMath byte table words, and unknown values) were each tested on sampled concrete values: 657,425 cases, none outside the range. Planting a range one smaller for MOD gives 30 failures. EXP folds only when its exponent is constant, so its gas stays static (bytecode/mod.rs 751-767).

cleared.check: Edge refinement after a JUMPI in block_analysis.rs: the DUP, LT and GT patterns with ISZERO chains that bound a stack value on one edge, and at_most.
cleared.result: Sound. branch() (block_analysis.rs 1943-2017) recognises PUSH-target JUMPI after a DUP or a DUP and PUSH compared with LT or GT in either order, with any number of ISZEROs, and bounds the original value by c - 1 or c on the edge where the test says so. 38,465 random stacks, depths, constants and patterns were executed concretely and the bound held on every taken edge; a planted bound of c - 2 fails 20 times. at_most (160-168) keeps an infeasible edge's value unchanged and never widens a constant. Ranges only hold values below 2^31.

cleared.check: Dynamic JUMP and JUMPI through the dispatch table, jump target conversion, and multi-target jumps that switch on the low 64 bits.
cleared.result: No mismatch. A dynamic target saturates to 2^64-1 when it does not fit in 64 bits (u256_to_u64_saturating, translate/mod.rs 2269-2277), and the table holds every valid JUMPDEST of the code (2102-2172). jumptable.py transcribes the rank table and finds that each of the 24,030 tested pcs (0 to max_pc + 64, 2^40 and 2^64-1) dispatches to its own JUMPDEST when it is one of the 610 valid ones and to the invalid jump block otherwise; shifting the bitmap by one plants 1,220 errors. A multi-target jump truncates to 64 bits only when the analysis committed every value: constant sets hold only valid targets, ranges are below 2^31, an enumerated invalid constant must fit in 64 bits (fits_switch_case, 1938-1941), and an unknown operand marks the state failed (1686-1742), so no value of 2^64 or more can alias a valid pc.

cleared.check: Memory expansion in compiled code: MLOAD and MSTORE inline checks, the per-section cache of checked ranges, the memory section analysis that skips checks, and mresize.
cleared.result: Correct as read. build_ensure_memory (translate/mod.rs 1858-1920) saturates offsets at 2^63-1, and mresize calls resize_evm with length 0, which still grows memory to the offset (evm2 memory.rs 101-114). A later access is exempt only if its base equals an earlier checked base and its constant addend is at least the earlier one, so its offset cannot exceed 2^64 and its end lies below memory already allocated. memory_sections.rs propagates a lower bound on memory size that is the minimum over predecessors (join_state 285-297) and only counts constant accesses that always expand memory; MCOPY counts max(dst, src) (bytecode/mod.rs 790-806). Checks are skipped only where that bound covers the exact required size.

cleared.check: Gas charged per section against per-instruction charging, and stack checks at section entry: can compiled code return a different result from a call or decide a branch differently?
cleared.result: No. Gas sections end at every branching instruction and at every instruction whose host effect depends on the remaining gas: calls, creates, SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, EXTCODE*, SELFDESTRUCT and host-table opcodes (sections.rs 229-256, bytecode/mod.rs 1214-1240). The static gas of the section is charged at its head, so a frame that runs out of gas inside a section halts at its head instead of a few instructions later, with the same exceptional halt, all frame gas consumed and every effect reverted. GAS returns the remaining gas plus the gas owed by later instructions of its section (translate/mod.rs 1143-1153, sections.rs 109-141), which is the specified value. Sections without a check carry the deficit as negative remaining gas until a signed check before any builtin that charges or reads gas. Stack bounds are checked at the head of a stack section and never ahead of a host-effect instruction. At 35aa3280 the SSTORE builtin skips a cold load when the remaining gas is below the full cold cost, as the interpreter at that revision does; the SLOAD builtin is unchanged and uses the additional cold cost like the interpreter (evm2 host.rs 14-31 at both revisions).

cleared.check: How a node decides to compile a contract, whether compiled and interpreted frames mix in one transaction, and what happens to a block when they disagree.
cleared.result: evm2 compiles a code hash after 8 lookups (jit_hot_threshold) when the code is at most 24 KiB, 24,576 bytes (runtime/config.rs 17, 280-290, 368-377). The PoolManager's deployed code is 24,009 bytes on Ethereum and on Tempo (eth_getCode, queried 2026-11-25), so it is eligible even under evm2's default, and reth v2.11.0 removes the limit (max-bytecode-len default 0) and keeps the threshold of 8. The decision is per frame: run_supported looks up the code hash and spec, runs the compiled function if it is resident and otherwise returns None so that the interpreter runs the frame (runtime/src/evm2_evm.rs 59-104). Compilation runs in background workers, so one transaction can run the PoolManager frame compiled and a hook or token frame interpreted, or the reverse. On Ethereum, a reth node whose compiled code disagreed with the specification would compute a different state root and fork itself off, while geth and the other clients decide the canonical chain (F-129). Tempo has one client; its release binary is built without the JIT feature (cleared in cycle 14), so no Tempo validator runs this code.

cleared.check: Whether an ordinary account can reach compiled code on the networks.json endpoints through eth_call or switch it on.
cleared.result: No. The Ethereum endpoint reports reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc, rpc_modules lists rpc, net, web3, txpool, debug, eth and trace, and reth_jit returns Method not found (queried 2026-11-25). Tempo reports tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 and refuses rpc_modules. Only an operator can enable the JIT, so the actor for any JIT fault is operator.

cleared.check: Does any of the other 19 networks run the evm2 JIT?
cleared.result: No. web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-25 (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/clientversions.json): OP Mainnet op-reth v2.8.1, Unichain, Ink and Soneium op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, Base reth v2.5.2 base v1.5.6, Zora conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, Worldchain world-chain v2.8.2, Celo reth v2.2.0, X Layer reth v2.3.0. op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and v2.8.1 build on revm 43 and op-revm with no evm2 dependency (rust/Cargo.toml of those tags), and reth v2.2.0, v2.3.0, v2.5.2 and v2.8.2 have no evm2 entry in their manifests. Arbitrum One and Elysium run Nitro, Polygon bor, BNB Smart Chain geth, Avalanche avalanchego, Arc its revm based node, and Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM their own executors, which earlier cycles read separately. Robinhood Chain answered 429 to this query and runs Nitro by earlier cycles.

cleared.check: Task 2 (lead L-726): is the PoolManager compiled at all by Monad's x86 emitter. Method: the emitter was built from downloaded source (category-labs/monad v0.16.7 and v0.16.5 category/vm and category/core from cdn.jsdelivr.net, asmjit at commit 9eb6edbf711ceb25346ee40bae68b40a4505cdf5 from raw.githubusercontent.com, evmc master of category-labs/evmc with the fork's four struct fields added by hand), the runtime symbols it only references were stubbed, and native::compile was run with the production CompilerConfig on the build of this checkout and on the code read with eth_getCode from 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e at https://rpc.monad.xyz (24,009 bytes, sha256 prefix 288b97729c9e4f34; it differs from build/PoolManager.json only in the 20 immutable bytes at offset 13606, which hold the PoolManager address).

The size check compares Emitter::estimate_size() (text size + 32 per pending CALLDATALOAD handler + read-only data + 4 x bytecode size, emitter.cpp 1020-1030) with max_code_size(10,240, 24,009) = 10,240 + 32 x 24,009 = 778,528 bytes (x86.hpp 53-65, types.hpp CompilerConfig max_code_size_offset = 10 x 1024, x86.cpp 308-315 and 468-479). The built emitter prints 285,084 bytes for the deployed code and 285,059 for the build with a zero immutable under v0.16.7, and 284,482 and 284,425 under v0.16.5, for MonadTraits MONAD_EIGHT, NINE and TEN alike, and returns an entry point (error_code NoError). The asmjit commit is the vcpkg pin of 2025-05-08, not the submodule pin of the release, which could not be read without the GitHub API; a different asmjit could move the estimate by a few percent at most, and the margin is a factor of 2.7.

cleared.check: Task 3 (lead L-725): which execution mode Monad validators run by default and after how much interpreted gas the PoolManager is compiled.
cleared.result: The execution daemon builds vm::VM vm{trace_calls ? InterpreterOnly : Dual} (cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7, line 479 at v0.16.5), so a node runs Dual unless it is started with --trace_calls. The published full node instructions recommend --trace_calls only for archive and RPC nodes, and the validator installation page says nothing about execution flags. The docs list monad 0.16.5 for mainnet and 0.16.7 for testnet. In Dual mode VM::execute_raw (vm.cpp 140-191, identical in v0.16.5 and v0.16.7) runs a contract in the interpreter and starts asynchronous compilation once the gas the interpreter has spent on that code hash, summed over all executions, reaches max_code_size(10,240, code size), which is 778,528 gas for the 24,009 byte PoolManager; when the node's code cache is not yet warm it compiles at once. A validator that follows the published setup therefore runs the PoolManager as native code after its first few transactions, and RPC nodes with --trace_calls interpret it.

cleared.check: Task 1: the compiled code of the never-mined paths against Monad's interpreter. A harness (harness.cpp) links Monad's real interpreter (interpreter::execute), the real emitter (native::compile) and the real runtime library from v0.16.7, with one in-memory host that keeps storage, transient storage, warm sets, logs and balances and reverts them per frame. Every transaction runs twice from the same state, once interpreted and once as native code, with MonadTraits MONAD_TEN, and the harness compares every call result (status, gas left, return bytes), all storage and transient storage, balances and logs. Users and an ERC20 are host-level accounts; inside unlockCallback a user runs a script of PoolManager calls and can read its own delta through exttload and pay it, mint it, or clear it exactly. Paths: clear of an exact credit (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319), transferFrom and burn through an allowance or an operator (src/ERC6909.sol:35-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22), approve and setOperator (src/ERC6909.sol:50-64), donate (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480), the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52), the amount above 2^160 branch of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97), and take, mint, clear and swap amounts drawn from edge sets around 2^64, 2^96, 2^127, 2^128, 2^159 to 2^161, 2^255 and 2^256 - 1.
cleared.result: No difference. 20,000 mixed scenarios (629,823 transactions and 676,709 calls inside unlocks) and nine per-path batteries of 100,000 calls each (approve, transferFrom, burn, clear, donate, fallback, amount above 2^160, take, swap; 291,020 transactions) give identical results in the interpreter and in native code, gas left included. The v0.16.5 build gives the same on 5,450 scenarios. The only raw difference is the status class of an exceptional halt: native code reports EVMC_FAILURE where the interpreter reports EVMC_OUT_OF_GAS, both with zero gas left; a receipt and a calling frame see only failure, so the harness compares halts as one class. A trace build of the interpreter records coverage: every instruction of clear (17 of 17), transferFrom (60 of 60), approve, setOperator, _burnFrom (37 of 37), Pool.donate (42 of 42), UnsafeMath.simpleMulDiv (35 of 35) and the fallback at SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 (12 of 12) ran; 7,505 of 10,418 PoolManager instructions ran in total. Two planted emitter faults are caught: SUB without borrow propagation (emitter.cpp 2481) makes 200 of 200 mixed and 90 of 90 battery scenarios differ, and an off-by-one in LT with a literal left operand (emitter.cpp 4029) makes 111 of 200 mixed and 48 of 90 battery scenarios differ.

cleared.check: Task 1: the exact basic blocks of each path and the emitter routines chosen for them. The emitter's own assembly log (CompilerConfig asm_log_path, with a comment for every EVM instruction and block) was written for the deployed code (pm.asm, 48,691 lines) and cut into the blocks that hold an instruction of each path (blocks/*.asm, blocks/summary.json, blocks/routines.json).
cleared.result: The paths occupy 85 blocks with 940 EVM instructions and 3,264 x86 instructions: clear 5 blocks (0xde6 to 0xe31), transferFrom 11, approve 1 (0x2518), setOperator 1 (0x20c1), _burnFrom 7, Pool.donate 8, the fallback 3 (0x5d5d, 0x5d6c, 0x5d71), getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp 15, getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown 13, simpleMulDiv 6. Of the EVM instructions, 624 emit no code (PUSH, DUP, SWAP and POP live in the virtual stack), 163 call runtime routines (DIV and MOD of variable operands, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, KECCAK256, LOG, CALL, memory growth), 112 use AVX moves for block-exit spills and wide literals, 52 are four-limb GPR arithmetic or comparisons (cmp or sub followed by sbb, add followed by adc), and the rest are shifts, setcc after fused ISZERO pairs, and branches. A comparison feeding JUMPI stays in CPU flags, and a dynamic JUMP checks the target below 24,009 with the three upper limbs zero and then goes through a jump table over every byte offset (fallback block 0x5d71). The comparison of whole transactions above runs exactly these instruction sequences on all their entries, so a Python model of each routine was not needed; the comparison is with Monad's interpreter, which cycles 1 to 14 matched to the specification on 185,529 vectors and the mined replays, and not with pyevm.py.

cleared.check: Whether the overflow fallback at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 and the amount above 2^160 branches at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 can decide the outcome of a swap that succeeds, which would make a compiled-only fault there reach funds.
cleared.result: They cannot. The fallback runs only on an exact-input step that stops short of its target (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:74-82) with amountRemainingLessFee times the current price sqrtC at or above 2^256 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:41-43), so the input is at least 2^256 / sqrtC. Inside one step the token1 output equals input times sqrtC times sqrtN / 2^192, where sqrtN is the price at which the step stops, so the output is at least 2^64 times sqrtN. A zeroForOne step searches for its target inside the current bitmap word (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:94-104, src/libraries/Pool.sol:348), and word 0 begins at compressed tick 0. A step that starts at a positive tick therefore never has a target below tick 0, where the price is 2^96, so sqrtN is at least 2^96 and the output is at least 2^160, which reverts in the toInt128 of src/libraries/Pool.sol:455 or :459. A step that starts at or below tick 0 has sqrtC of at most about 2^96, so the input is at least 2^160 and reverts the same way. The price limit can only move the target closer. The verifier of this cycle supplied this argument; the bound on liquidity alone does not exclude the fallback. The harness agrees: all 100,000 fallback calls and all 100,000 calls above 2^160 reverted with 0x93dafdf1 in both engines. Branch :105 (exact output above 2^160) needs more than 2^160 of output and was never reached, as cycle 12 found (jumpmap neverReached). A wrong result in these blocks could only change which error a reverting frame returns.

cleared.check: Whether any of the other 20 networks runs EVM bytecode through a compiler like Monad's.
cleared.result: No other network in networks.json runs Monad's emitter. The reth JIT (evm2 with reth_jit) was read in cycle 14 and is off on the public endpoints, and Stylus compiles WASM, not EVM bytecode (OPCODES.md, cycle 14 ethereum-reference and arbitrum-family). cleared.check: Task 1, jump pairs 9042/9048 (unlockCallback CALL, PoolManager.sol:110) and 15088/15094 (balanceOf STATICCALL, Currency.sol:94). Sides: 9048 falls through to 9049 with the result left at its default 0 and skips the decoding of the returned bytes; 15094 falls through to 15095 and returns the default 0 balance without decoding. Condition for the untaken side: the success word is zero at 9048 (or 15094) while it was nonzero at 9042 (or 15088).
cleared.result: Unreachable on every network for any value a CALL or STATICCALL can push. The disassembly of the build reads CALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI at 9035-9042 and PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x241a, JUMPI at 9043-9048, and STATICCALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI, PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x3afa, JUMPI at 15081-15094. Both JUMPIs of a pair test the same stack word: the first leaves through 0x24c2 (9410: RETURNDATACOPY of all return data and REVERT) when the word is zero, the second runs only when it is nonzero and then jumps. No network can make one word both zero and nonzero, so a CALL that returns 2, or any other nonzero word, still takes the decode side. The decode side checks return data size (9263-9272 for unlockCallback, 15104-15108 for balanceOf, both require at least 32 bytes) and reverts otherwise. callsem.py, rerun this session on all 21 networks, returned 50 of 50 specified words, including the success flags of calls that revert, fail a static write or carry value.

cleared.check: Task 1, pc 15021 (Currency.sol:91-92). Sides: taken goes to the balanceOf STATICCALL at 15026, fallthrough runs SELFBALANCE at 15023. Condition for the untaken side: the currency word masked to 160 bits is zero inside balanceOfSelf.
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. balanceOfSelf has two callers, sync (PoolManager.sol:281-285) and _settle (PoolManager.sol:353-359), and each tests isAddressZero on the same currency value first and takes another branch for address(0). The condition is AND and JUMPI on a value from calldata or transient storage; it reads no environment opcode, so no chain property enters. SELFBALANCE stays dead code, and no network difference in SELFBALANCE (for example a native balance mirrored elsewhere, F-008 on Polygon or the USDC faces on Arc) can reach the settlement arithmetic through it.

cleared.check: Task 1, pc 16370 (Hooks.sol:137). Sides: fallthrough computes bytes4(data) from a hook calldata shorter than 4 bytes; taken uses the first 4 bytes. Condition: mload(data) < 4.
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. data is always an abi.encodeCall of an IHooks selector with at least one argument (Hooks.sol:180, 190, 202, 204, 225, 237, 256, 300, 323, 333), so its length is at least 36 bytes. The length is written by the compiler's encoder in memory and does not depend on any opcode result outside MLOAD and LT, which the opcode battery covers.

cleared.check: Task 1, ABI decoder bounds at pcs 1378, 2396, 3087, 5298, 10926 and 11947. Sides: revert to 816 when calldata is shorter than the head of a second static struct. Condition: CALLDATASIZE minus 4 is less than the head of the second struct while an earlier JUMPI of the same function (for example 1327 before 1378) passed with a larger bound.
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. Both tests compare CALLDATASIZE, a single value per frame, against two constants, and the earlier test uses the larger one. A network cannot return two CALLDATASIZE values in one frame. pmdiff4 (malformed calldata on a third of 10,773 calls) matched the reference on all 21 networks in cycle 12.

cleared.check: Task 1, Panic 0x41 at pcs 5583, 11761, 11789, 11817 and 19089. Sides: Panic 0x41 when a memory struct allocation moves the free memory pointer above 2^64 - 1 or below its old value. Condition: the free memory pointer exceeds about 2^64 before the allocation. The one input from outside that moves the pointer before these allocations is hook return data, because callHook advances the pointer by returndatasize rounded up plus 32 (Hooks.sol:142-148).
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. Reaching 2^64 needs return data of about 2^64 bytes, which no transaction gas cap allows: the largest simulated call gas any endpoint grants is about 150 million on Monad (OPCODES.md check 2), while 2^64 bytes of memory cost far more than 2^100 gas under the quadratic rule. cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks under specified opcode results, and a revert in any case. Rechecked by hand: getSqrtPriceAtTick receives ticks bounded by checkTicks (Pool.sol:94-98) or by the clamp at Pool.sol:351-356; a step amount is at most about 2^192 (liquidity below 2^128 times a price below 2^160, over prices of at least 2^32), so the int256 casts and the loop sum stay below 2^255; computeSwapStep with liquidity 0 computes a zero amount to the target and always reaches it (SwapMath.sol:63-99), so getNextSqrtPriceFrom* never sees liquidity 0, and those functions test liquidity before the mulmod in any case; an exact output step that stops short has amount times price below liquidity times 2^96 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:59-71), so neither PriceOverflow nor the toUint160 cast can fire. Each condition is a relation among ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MULMOD, SHL, SHR, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, ISZERO and AND results, so a network could make one true only by returning a word the specification does not give. The 185,529 battery vectors and the 2,000 or so scripts on the build show no such word on any of the 21 networks, and these sides would only turn a success into a revert, which takes no funds.

cleared.check: Task 2, transient storage cleared at the end of the transaction and rolled back on revert (Lock.sol:12-26, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41, CurrencyReserves.sol:28-31).
cleared.result: The source needs end-of-transaction clearing for two slots only. unlock always ends by writing false to the lock slot (PoolManager.sol:113) or reverts, and it reverts unless NonzeroDeltaCount is zero (PoolManager.sol:112). _accountDelta increments the count only when a delta goes from zero to nonzero and decrements it only when a nonzero delta returns to zero (PoolManager.sol:368-378), so a zero count means every delta slot is zero. What outlives a completed unlock is the synced currency and reserves, which is F-071 for a shared transaction. The property whose failure would hand funds to an ordinary account is rollback on revert: a lock flag or a credit written in a frame that reverts must disappear. callsem.py, rerun this session, gave the specified words for the transient write after a reverted write, a static write, a nested write and two failures on all 21 networks. The special contexts were cleared in earlier cycles and are not repeated: Tempo type 0x76 batches, HyperEVM system transactions, Nitro retryables and deposits, OP Stack deposits, MegaETH mini-blocks, Monad, Polygon and BNB Smart Chain parallel execution with re-execution (bor resets transient storage per transaction and per re-execution; Monad drops a failed frame's copy, state3/state.cpp 126-181), Celo fee debit and credit calls and ERC-4337 or EIP-7702 bundles (state/cleared.json). Within one shared transaction the lock and the deltas cannot pass from one party to the next for the reason above.

In every case the settle that follows in the same transaction credits 0, because the returned word does not change inside the transaction. A zero take of these addresses fails with ERC20TransferFailed (0x90bfb865) where the returned word is not 1, and succeeds where the callee has no code or is a real token. The precompiles that charge for their input (0x05 to 0x11 and several system contracts) consume the forwarded gas, and the whole script fails, which is the caller's own loss. initialize succeeds with the codeless hook 0x100, and with 0x10 on Avalanche and HyperEVM, because those flag combinations call no hook at initialize. cleared.check: Task 2, dirty upper bits that assembly in src/ cleans or assumes clean: masks in Currency.sol:61, CurrencyDelta.sol:12-13, CurrencyReserves.sol:29, CustomRevert.sol:25, 43, 64-65, 75-76, 97-100, 115, SqrtPriceMath.sol:62, 110, 137-138, 166-167, 198, 217, SwapMath.sol:31-33, LiquidityMath.sol:12 and the signextend calls of TickBitmap.sol:20-21, 38, 54-55 and CustomRevert.sol:34, 53-54; and the places that use a word unmasked: Lock.isUnlocked (Lock.sol:25), ParseBytes (ParseBytes.sol:12, 19, 26) and Position.calculatePositionKey (Position.sol:54-66).
cleared.result: No case depends on a network. Values from calldata pass the ABI decoder, which rejects dirty high bits (set C3, sync of an address word with bits above 160 set, reverts on the reference and on the six networks of set C). The lock slot is only ever written with true or false (Lock.sol:13, 19). ParseBytes returns full words that the compiler cleans to bytes4, uint24 or int256 where they are used, and each read follows a length check (Hooks.sol:152, 166, 259). In the position key the upper bytes of each mstore are overwritten by the next store or lie outside the hashed range [0x0c, 0x46), so dirty ticks or owner bits cannot change the key. AND, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL and SHR are in the battery on all 21 networks.

cleared.check: Task 3, the assembly that writes memory without moving the free memory pointer: CustomRevert (exits at once), Hooks.callHook (allocates from returndatasize, Hooks.sol:140-149), Currency.transfer (calldata at the free pointer, output to 0..32, then zeroes 0x60 bytes, Currency.sol:55-80), Extsload and Exttload (do-while loops, Extsload.sol:18-63, Exttload.sol:18-38), ParseBytes and Position.calculatePositionKey. Edge inputs: hook return data of 31 to 1,048,576 bytes, a reverting hook with 0, 1, 31, 32, 33 and 32,768 bytes of data, extsload(start, n) for n = 0, 1, 2, 2^251, 2^251 + 1, 2^251 + 2, 2^256 - 2 and 2^256 - 1, the array forms with length words 0, 1, 2^251, 2^251 + 1, 2^64 - 1 and 2^64, and a dirty address word in sync.
cleared.result: Each block assumes only that memory above the free pointer is scratch it may overwrite and that RETURNDATASIZE gives the length the callee returned. Currency.transfer trusts mload(0) only when return data is longer than 31 bytes and fails on 1 to 31 bytes; Yul evaluates the call before the or() term, which the bytecode does. The extsload loops run once even for n = 0 and then return the 64 byte header. For n = 2^256 - 1 the shifted length wraps and the function returns 32 bytes, for n = 2^256 - 2 it returns 0 bytes, and 2^251 returns a header with length 2^251 and no elements; all are view calls that cannot move funds. The array forms with a length of 2^64 or 2^251 are refused by the ABI decoder. The wrapped error for a reverting hook grows by 32 bytes per word of data, 228 bytes for empty data. All 39 scripts gave the reference interpreter's bytes on Ethereum, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Monad, Tempo and HyperEVM in the earlier attempt, and again this session on Arbitrum One (Nitro, go-ethereum fork), Monad (C++ interpreter) and Tempo (evm2).

cleared.check: Monad main, EIP-8024 and SLOTNUM: can the new opcodes or their immediates change the jump destination map or the execution of the deployed PoolManager?
cleared.result: No. The opcodes are gated on Amsterdam, which only MONAD_NEXT selects, and mainnet's revision function ends at MONAD_TEN. The interpreter's jump analysis has no EIP-8024 case, because an allowed immediate is never 0x5b or a PUSH. The compiler consumes an immediate only when it is allowed and otherwise ends the block as invalid, so 0x5b after 0xe6 to 0xe8 stays a JUMPDEST. A linear scan of the 24,009 byte runtime finds no 0x4b, 0xe6, 0xe7 or 0xe8 outside push data, so no PoolManager instruction changes meaning.

cleared.check: Monad main, generic 256 bit division and modular arithmetic that DIV, MOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD call (udivrem, addmod, mulmod), read against v0.16.7 for the paths FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and 48) and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp use.
cleared.result: Equivalent as read. udivrem now forms the remainder from the n significant divisor words. After Knuth division the normalised remainder is below the normalised divisor, so the words at n and above are zero, and v0.16.7 read the same zeros. The short path zero fills the remainder and copies min(M, N) words, which also removes an over-read when M is less than N. addmod's fast path returns the same value through one variable. mulmod's wide_mul is truncating_mul of width M+N. Not run, because the library could not be built here.

cleared.check: Monad main, the new per-block cache of literal memory ends in the x86 emitter (touched_memory_end_): can a compiled MLOAD or MSTORE skip a needed memory expansion?
cleared.result: No, as read. Memory never shrinks inside a frame. The cache is reset at the start of every block except a fall-through continuation, which a debug assertion requires to have no jump entry, and it only skips the check for literal offsets whose end is at or below one already expanded. The data pointer is reloaded from the context on every use.

cleared.check: F-133 and lead L-778: which code path puts a storage word of an address without code into the reth execution cache before a block destroys and recreates that address, on op-reth v2.8.1 and v2.8.2 (ethereum-optimism/reth op-v2.6.0-2), conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, world-chain v2.8.2 and base v1.5.6 (base/reth 9e380dd).
cleared.result: None on the default paths. Since Cancun an account is destroyed only in the transaction that created it, so a destroyed account whose original info has no code was created in that block. A storage read of such an address goes to the cache only through State::storage when the account status leaves storage unknown, and revm 42.0.0 returns zero without a read for LoadedNotExisting, InMemoryChange and the Destroyed states (states/account_status.rs lines 58-67, states/state.rs lines 270-300) and for an account created in the transaction (revm-context-interface account.rs lines 172-211). Access list entries only mark slots warm. The only reth path that reads storage slots outside execution is the block access list prewarm (prewarm.rs lines 342-431), which mod.rs lines 359-368 select only when the payload carries a block access list, and OP Stack and Base blocks carry none. The cache entries that the old branch fails to update therefore never exist, the next read misses and goes to the state overlay, and followers cannot be stalled this way. No path reaches the PoolManager in any case: it has code and no SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364 read balances of contracts that already have code). A block access list fork would need a new node release, and base main (base/reth 2b20e42) and op-reth develop (op-v2.7.0-2) already write the recreated account's storage.

cleared.check: Lead L-731: the arithmetic opcode handlers of the respected kona-client prestate itself, run in the Cannon MIPS64 emulator.
cleared.result: Twenty handlers were located in the image and run on every battery and targeted vector of their opcode, with no mismatch: ADD, SUB, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, EXP, ADDMOD, MULMOD, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, BYTE, AND, OR, XOR, SHL, SHR and SAR. The comparison can fail: a DIV handler run as if it were GT or EQ gave 790 and 773 wrong words. The rules that settle withdrawals on OP Mainnet, Unichain and Ink therefore compute the mulmod of src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and :48, the sdiv and smod of src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26 and the byte lookup of src/libraries/BitMath.sol:22 as the specification says. MUL, SIGNEXTEND and EQ were not located and stay with the cycle 13 rebuild.

cleared.check: Upcoming fork, Lagoon, judged from the develop source on 2026-11-25: can a native take (P1), a token take (P2), a sync (P3) or a hook call (P5) aimed at SuperchainETHBridge or ETHLiquidity move value that the caller does not owe.
cleared.result: No. SuperchainETHBridge has no receive or fallback, so a value call with empty calldata from take(address(0), ...) reverts, and sendETH needs its own selector. ETHLiquidity has no receive or fallback; burn and mint revert unless the caller is the bridge, and fund needs its selector. relayETH and refundETH deliver ETH by a self-destructing SafeSend, so ETH sent to the PoolManager raises its balance without msg.value; _settle credits native payments only from msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354) and the PoolManager has no receive function, so such ETH is credited to nobody and cannot be taken.

cleared.check: Lead L-771: does the Base B20 stablecoin precompile or a BNB Smart Chain Jenner CAS20 token redirect a transfer by a pattern in the recipient address, or call another contract during a transfer, as Tempo T15 zone deposit addresses do?
cleared.result: No on both. Base answers reth/v2.5.2 base/v1.5.6. In v1.5.6 the B20 V3 transfer resolves the recipient with B20CreditRecipientStrategy::ExcludingZeroAndSelf, which returns the address unchanged and only rejects zero and the token itself (credit_recipient.rs), checks the executor, sender and receiver policies through is_authorized, which reads registry membership from storage (guards.rs lines 80-94, policy logic v1.rs lines 366-389), and move_balance debits from and credits to the named address (v3.rs lines 55-118, 209-232). BNB Smart Chain answers Geth/v1.8.2. At tag v1.8.2 cas20 transfer calls move and returns a 32 byte true (cas20_token.go lines 175-189); move checks the two policies and writes exactly the source and recipient balance slots (lines 239-269); isAuthorized walks stored policy ids and members only (cas20_policy.go lines 169-199). Neither path calls a contract, so neither opens a bracketing window inside take.

cleared.check: ERC-4337 handleOps as a carrier that runs several accounts' code in one transaction: can an ordinary account place operations before and after another user's payment to the PoolManager and book it.
cleared.result: EntryPoint v0.7 code (16,035 bytes) is at 0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032 on all 21 networks, and handleOps is public with only a reentrancy guard (EntryPoint.sol v0.7 lines 174-200), so any account can bundle a victim's signed operation between two of its own. A user operation runs as one call to the sender account, and a user who pays the PoolManager does sync, pay and settle inside one unlock in that call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288, 349-364); another operation cannot run inside it. An operation that sends tokens to the PoolManager outside an unlock gives them up as surplus whether or not anyone brackets it. Paymaster and beneficiary payments go to the paymaster and in native value, and native value is credited only as msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). No new loss found. Hazard of a user design that splits sync and settle across two operations is noted in one line only.

cleared.result: A retryable executes as its own transaction from the aliased L1 sender, and the L2 gateway's finalizeInboundTransfer pays the recipient there. A manual ArbRetryableTx.redeem only schedules the retry as a separate transaction after the caller's transaction (cleared in an earlier cycle from tx_processor.go and block_processor.go), so its transient sync never covers the payment. ArbRetryableTx exists on all three chains (code at 0x6e). Elysium has no CCTP, LxLy or Teleporter code. Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain carry CCTP v2 code, covered by the CCTP finding.

cleared.check: Task 2: balance changes without a transfer call between two frames of one transaction (native credits, protocol mints, fee refunds, rebases) that an ordinary account could book with sync and settle.
cleared.result: Native value is credited only as msg.value of settle (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354) and the PoolManager has no receive or fallback (grep of src/ finds none), so coinbase rewards, forced ETH, deposit mints and system credits in native value give no one a credit. On networks where the native asset has an ERC-20 face (Celo CELO token, Arc 0x3600..., Polygon 0x1010, OP and Zora legacy ETH) the only inflows that can happen inside an attacker's transaction without a call are SELFDESTRUCT payments, which are the attacker's own money. Fee refunds go to the transaction's fee payer on Celo and Tempo and the PoolManager is never one (Tempo fee spec; Celo cleared item on fee_currencies.go). HyperCore credits are separate system transactions (earlier cleared item). Rebases of B20 Asset splits and CAS20 multipliers need issuer roles and run in the issuer's transaction (earlier cleared items); token specific oracle rebases are a token hazard and were not swept.

cleared.check: L-768 and L-626, Task 2: does the closed MegaETH sequencer's post-state for PoolManager liquidity removals, fee collections, ERC-6909 mints and burns and take inside reverted frames equal an independent re-execution?
cleared.result: Task 2. In --block-list mode the validator fetched each block's witness with mega_getBlockWitness and the block from https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, verified the witness, re-executed every transaction with mega-evm v1.7.3 on the stock revm interpreter and compared state root, receipts root, logs bloom, withdrawals root and gas used with the header the sequencer published. Target set: every block holding a PoolManager ModifyLiquidity with negative liquidityDelta (210 events in 210 blocks), with zero liquidityDelta, i.e. fee collection (545 in 545), an ERC-6909 mint (40 in 40) or burn (81 in 81) from the full PoolManager log history of blocks 2,900,000 to 32,766,000 (cycles/013/theme-mined-branches.work/raw/logs-4326.json and cycles/015/theme-closed-producers-2.work/raw/pmtail-4326.jsonl), plus the 75 blocks of the take, settle and sync inside reverted frames listed in cycles/011/theme-closed-producers.work/raw/mega.json (75 of the 87 cycle 11 counted are in that file's sample). Result: 911 distinct blocks, 911 validated, 0 failed. Anchored check: 45 of these blocks (15 removal, 10 fee collection, 5 burn, 5 mint, 10 reverted-frame blocks, seed 16) were also run in chain-following mode with --start-block set to the parent block hash and --end-block to the block, which in addition checks the witness pre-state against the parent's state root (stateless-core executor.rs:837-841); 45 of 45 validated. Wider sweep: all other blocks that hold any PoolManager log or a cycle 11 sampled transaction, 42734 blocks; all 42734 were run, 42734 validated and 0 failed. Control: the same 911 blocks run with a build whose revm-interpreter MULMOD returns one more than the correct result whenever the 512 bit product exceeds 2^256 (patched copy under build/plant, [patch.crates-io] in build/sv-plant) give 611 validated and 300 failed, mostly with a receipts root mismatch; the failures cover 138 of 210 removal blocks, 67 of 545 fee collection blocks, 25 of 81 burn blocks and 75 of 75 reverted-frame blocks, so the comparison sees a wrong product in these blocks. So for every mined MegaETH liquidity removal, fee collection, ERC-6909 mint and burn and every sampled take inside a reverted frame, the closed sequencer's post-state equals an independent re-execution by the open interpreter, to the state root. Task 3 was not needed.
