cleared.check: Task 4: when a PoolManager call inside unlock meets a mega-evm compute gas, data size, key-value update or state growth limit, can an inner frame stop while outer frames continue with PoolManager state the source assumes rolled back?
cleared.result: Task 4. mega-evm v1.7.3 meters four extra dimensions per transaction (Rex constants: compute gas 200,000,000, data 12.5 MiB, key-value updates 500,000, state growth 1,000; crates/mega-evm/src/constants.rs:192-211) and, from Rex4, gives each inner frame 98/100 of its parent's remaining budget (limit/frame_limit.rs:162-171). A transaction-level exceed is latched and reported as OutOfGas; once latched, every later metered opcode in every frame halts (record_compute_gas returns false on a latched exceed, limit/limit.rs:460-480, and the instruction wrapper sets a halt action, evm/instructions.rs:581-594), and every frame return is marked OutOfGas (limit.rs:846-856), so the top frame halts and revm reverts the whole transaction apart from nonce and fee. A frame-local exceed found during execution ends that frame with Revert and revert data MegaLimitExceeded(kind, limit); revm's process_next_action reverts the frame's journal checkpoint for any non-ok result (revm-handler 20.0.3 src/frame.rs:416-423), which undoes storage, transient storage and logs of that frame, and the parent continues. A frame-local exceed found only when the frame returns (before_frame_return_result, limit.rs:801-845) rewrites a successful result to Revert after revm has already committed the frame; the source says so at limit.rs:827-830. The late detection exists for CREATE frames (code size recorded in after_frame_run, limit/data_size.rs:324-335) and for a SELFDESTRUCT whose usage was recorded before its inner instruction halted (limit.rs:450-456); the PoolManager bytecode has neither opcode, so no PoolManager frame can be committed and reported failed. Every outward call of the PoolManager reverts the PoolManager frame when the callee reports failure: the native and ERC-20 transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40-84), the hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-139) and the balanceOf read of sync and settle (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365). So a callee frame reported failed, whether rolled back or not, ends with the PoolManager frame reverted, and that revert undoes Lock (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-19), NonzeroDeltaCount (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:20-32) and CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:35-39) together with the payment. No rewrite goes from failure to success, so a payment frame can never be reported successful with its transfer undone. Read-only test on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc with eth_call and code overrides (probe/limits.py, probe/loop.py; the test contracts touch no PoolManager state): a child that creates 990 new storage slots under a parent that gave it all its gas returns success 0 with MegaLimitExceeded(3, 980) and the parent completes; through DELEGATECALL the child's writes are read back as zero after the failed call and the parent's own later write is present, while 900 and 979 slots succeed and persist. A child in an endless loop returns MegaLimitExceeded(2, 58,776,709) and the parent completes. These match the reading: a frame-local exceed rolls back that frame and only that frame.

cleared.check: Task 3. The emitter source between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 (category/vm/compiler and category/vm/runtime, file by file), and which changes reach instructions of the deployed PoolManager. The PoolManager's blocks were located by an instrumented copy of the emitter that writes a marker for every emitter function entered and every branch arm taken while each EVM instruction is emitted (shapes/instrument.py; the markers are logger calls and the emitted asm text is identical to the uninstrumented build).
cleared.result: Only compiler/ir/x86.cpp, x86/emitter.cpp, emitter.hpp, types.hpp, virtual_stack.hpp and runtime/allocator.hpp and cached_allocator.hpp differ; no runtime .cpp or .S file changed, so the arithmetic routines (math.S, the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP calls) are the same. Changes that reach the PoolManager: (a) shift_literal_by_non_literal (emitter.cpp 5231-5235 and 5254-5328) handles SHL, SHR and SAR of a literal value by a variable count with two unaligned loads from a 96-byte read-only window and per-qword shifts; it is used at 6 PoolManager sites, SHL at pcs 16643 (inside the TickBitmap.flipTick code, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:47-75), 16691 (the mask shl(and(tick, 0xff), 1), src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:72), 21183 (1 << bitPos, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:110) and 21364 (the De Bruijn table of BitMath.leastSignificantBit, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:40-42), SHR at 19356 (type(uint256).max >> (255 - bitPos), src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:96) and 23648 (the table of BitMath.mostSignificantBit, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:21-22); under v0.16.5 the same sites move the literal into an AVX register and take shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal. The window arithmetic was checked by hand: for shift 8k+b with k up to 32 the loads stay inside bytes 31 to 95 of the window and the mask sits at bytes 0-15 (SHL) or 80-95 (SHR, SAR), and for every bit i the two loads contribute the same stream bit. (b) touch_memory skips the bound check and memory growth when the same non-literal offset element was already checked with at least the same size in the block (6301-6313); 15 PoolManager MLOAD and MSTORE sites use it, and 14 of them run in the cycle 15 scenarios (the one left, pc 16254, is next to the hook call revert path at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). Since the element is the same value and memory never shrinks inside a frame, the skipped check would have passed. (c) The block-exit stack write orders elements by stack index through a preallocated count array and loads GPR-held words into a YMM register word by word (mov_words_to_ymm, 2061); every block exit with register-held values uses it. (d) block_prologue jumps straight to the error label when max_delta - min_delta > 1024 (1342), where v0.16.5 tested min_delta < -1024 or max_delta > 1024; no stack size satisfies both runtime checks in exactly the cases the new test catches, so the outcome is the same. (e) Read-only data alignment 32 to 64 bytes (735) and add96. Changes that do not reach it: MSTORE8 of a value held at a stack offset (3399-3412; the PoolManager has no MSTORE8), the CLZ rewrite (2692-2733 and 8266-8293; no CLZ opcode), debug comments, the allocator refactor (stack memory allocation only). Both versions were run on every input of this unit with no difference between engines or between versions.

cleared.check: Task 4, shapes. For MULMOD, ADDMOD, SDIV, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, BYTE, SHL, SHR, EXP, CALLDATALOAD, MSTORE8, MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE: every shape the v0.16.7 emitter can pick (read from the dispatch code), which shapes the deployed PoolManager's blocks use (from the instrumented asm log), and whether PoolManager scenarios execute each site (operand classes recorded at the same pc in the interpreter, which runs the same path as the native code because every result is equal).
cleared.result: Shapes the emitter can pick. SHL, SHR, SAR: fold of two literals; literal count of 256 or more (0, or the sign fill for SAR) or 0 (identity); literal count with the value in an AVX register (shift_avx_reg_by_literal) or in general registers or a stack slot (shift_general_reg_or_stack_offset_by_literal); variable count with a literal value of 0 (or all ones for SAR, identity), any other literal value (shift_literal_by_non_literal, new in v0.16.6/7), the value in an AVX register (shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal, count bounded to 256 in rax) or in general registers, or a stack slot moved to them (shift_general_reg_by_non_literal with test_high_bits192). BYTE: literal index of 32 or more gives 0; fold; literal or variable index with the source in general registers, an AVX register, or a stack slot (6 leaves). SIGNEXTEND: fold; literal index of 31 or more gives the value; literal index with the source in AVX or general registers or a stack slot; variable index bounded to 31 with the source in AVX, general registers, or a stack slot or literal (5 leaves). MULMOD and ADDMOD: literal modulus 0 or 1 gives 0; folds; a literal operand equal to the absorbing element; a power-of-two literal modulus becomes an AND mask (operand equal to 1 or 0) or mul_mod2 / add_mod2, which inline the product or sum truncated to n bits for n up to 128 and call runtime mul_192 or mul above; anything else calls the runtime. SDIV and SMOD: literal folds, divisor 0, power-of-two divisor (sdiv_by_sar with negation, smod_by_mask), otherwise the runtime call. EXP: literal folds and gas by exponent width, otherwise the runtime. CALLDATALOAD: literal offset bounded or out of range, variable offset bounded by bits with a runtime check. MSTORE8: value literal, in general registers, AVX, or a stack slot (general register or AVX temporary). MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE: runtime calls only. cleared.check: Task 4, edges. Micro programs that put each instruction into each shape with edge operands (0, 1, 2, 31, 32, 63 to 65, 127 to 129, 191 to 193, 254, 255, 256, 257, 511, 2^64-1, 2^64, 2^64+1, 2^128+5, 2^192+255, 2^255, 2^255+1, 2^256-2, 2^256-1, byte indexes 0 to 33 and above, power-of-two and other moduli including 2^96 and 2^128, and random words), run in the same harness (interpreter against native) and checked against the specification in Python; the shape each program gets was confirmed with the instrumented emitter (micro/shapes.json).
cleared.result: 2,154 programs and 158,802 calls: v0.16.7 scenarios=2154 mismatches=0, v0.16.5 scenarios=2154 mismatches=0, AVX-512 build scenarios=2154 mismatches=0. Every coarse PoolManager shape of the 12 instructions that occur is reached by micro programs except MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE, which are plain runtime calls shared with the interpreter and run in every PoolManager scenario. 155,196 interpreter results of SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD, MULMOD and ADDMOD equal the specification, and the native result equals the interpreter in every call. Ten further programs cover the two v0.16.7 memory changes: an offset element reused for MLOAD, MSTORE, MLOAD (the skip path, confirmed by its marker), MSTORE8 then MLOAD (no skip, as required), and MSTORE8 of a literal, register, AVX and stack-slot value, at 16 offsets up to 2^256-1 and two gas limits: no difference on v0.16.7 or v0.16.5. Planted faults: changing the carry offset of the SHR window load in shift_literal_by_non_literal (fault f3) breaks all 46 SHR programs of that shape; changing the bit width of mul_mod2 to n-1 for 2^128 and 2^96 in the stack-slot branch (f5) breaks the m2^128 and m2^96 programs of that branch; in the register branch for 2^128 (f4) it breaks those of that branch. On PoolManager inputs: f3 gives 539 mismatches in 2090 scenarios, f5 gives 0 in 2090 scenarios (4 scenario files and the first battery file of each path), and f5 changes nothing in the 2,007 mined transactions (0 differences). The PoolManager scenarios do run the 2^96 site (pc 22639) 113,230 times, always with a product above 2^256, yet f5 changes none of their results: on a correct node that branch returns an amount of at least 2^160, which either loses the comparison at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:68 or :90 or reverts later in a cast, and a garbage remainder almost always gives a garbage amount that does the same. The evidence for the two mul_mod2 sites is therefore the micro programs: 52,224 MULMOD results equal to the specification, including the moduli 2^96 and 2^128 in the register and stack-slot arms. The PoolManager scenarios only show that the site runs.

cleared.check: Task 2, halts other than REVERT, constructed with eth_call and state overrides against the deployed PoolManager of each of the 21 networks (HaltProbe.sol, halt.py, halt_fix.py in the work directory). A probe frame writes its own transient slot and then either (variant 1) enters unlock and, in the callback, mints 5 claims, syncs a currency and writes a second slot, or (variant 2) syncs a currency outside unlock, and then halts. Kinds: REVERT as control, INVALID (0xfe), stack overflow by unbounded internal recursion, out of gas by an endless loop, and, under STATICCALL, a TSTORE by the probe, PoolManager.sync and PoolManager.unlock. A later frame then reads the unlock flag, the nonzero delta count, the probe's delta, the synced currency and reserves with exttload (src/Exttload.sol:10-15), the probe's claim balance and the probe's own two slots. In a second test the call into the probe was given every gas value from 1 up to the first value at which it succeeds (step 1 over the last 8,000 gas below that value and step 9 or coarser below), so that out of gas falls at every reachable point inside the PoolManager, the callback and the balanceOf staticcall: 362,827 attempts, 362,743 of them failing. The first successful gas is 39,572 on most networks, 39,324 on Monad, 81,193 on MegaETH and 281,586 on Tempo, where creating a storage slot costs more.
cleared.result: No leak on any network: 0 failed attempts read back a write. The successful controls show every written slot (synced currency 0x00000000000000000000000000000000c0ffee16 and reserves 1000 plus the attempt id, the probe slots 7 and 9), so the reads can see a write that survives. A static call into PoolManager.sync or unlock fails at its first TSTORE (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:29-30) and writes nothing, so a static violation cannot leave a write by construction. PoolManager never catches a failed callee: the hook call bubbles the failure (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137), token and native payouts revert (src/types/Currency.sol:48-52 and 73-83), and the callback is a plain high level call (src/PoolManager.sol:110), so a halt in any of them reverts the whole unlock. On MegaETH the simulated call runs on the RPC node, not the closed sequencer (OPCODES.md, MegaETH row).

cleared.check: Task 2, call depth 1024: how deep a chain of self calls with all gas gets under a 30,000,000 gas eth_call, and what the PoolManager does when a call it makes fails for depth.
cleared.result: The chain stops at depth 358 on 18 networks, 357 on Tempo and 291 on MegaETH (98/100 forwarding), well short of 1,024, because each level keeps 1/64 of the gas: (63/64)^1024 is 9.9e-8, so reaching depth 1,024 needs about 10^10 gas at the top, and (98/100)^1024 is 1.0e-9 on MegaETH. Where depth were reached, the failed outgoing call returns 0 without halting the PoolManager frame, and every outgoing call of the PoolManager turns a failure into a revert (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, src/types/Currency.sol:52 and 83, src/PoolManager.sol:110), so the unlock reverts and its transient writes go with it.

cleared.check: Task 3, ERC-4337 bundles on every network, which join several users' operations into one transaction. Whether transient storage is cleared between operations, and a mined bundle in which two unrelated senders' operations both called the PoolManager. Bundles among PoolManager transactions (UserOperationEvent of EntryPoint 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, aa.py): Base 5,610 PoolManager transactions in blocks 61,965,599 to 61,973,598, 170 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Ethereum 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 26,489,705 to 26,490,154, 65 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Polygon 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 97,904,651 to 97,919,750, 223 bundles, 2 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Arbitrum One 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 527,245,513 to 527,333,512, 59 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Optimism 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 159,986,660 to 159,993,159, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Robinhood Chain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 122,805,462 to 122,811,461, 64 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Unichain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 64,830,284 to 64,836,583, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager.
cleared.result: Transient storage is not cleared between operations: EIP-1153 discards it only at the end of the transaction, and the EntryPoint runs every operation as a nested call of the one handleOps transaction. The unlock flag and the deltas cannot pass from one operation to the next, because unlock clears the flag and requires every delta to be zero before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Only the synced currency and reserves can. No mined bundle with two senders' PoolManager calls was found: the only multi-sender bundles have one operation that reaches the PoolManager, for example Base 0x61046bec99fa8dc23efda3e63f0bedc7e18b233fb191c09ff26edfbaced2b66c (EntryPoint 0.6, senders 0x0de04d745d88dc18e7c519f1935a3e27917e795f and 0xcbeebaf9d1f94a6678dad25e14afd2fb042bc579, only the second calls unlock, sync, settle, swap, mint and take). sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims.

cleared.check: Task 3, Tempo type 0x76 batched and sponsored transactions: does transient storage survive between the calls of a batch, and can two unrelated users share it?
cleared.result: The calls of a batch share one transient map: execute_batch takes one checkpoint before the first call, runs every call with the transaction's caller as sender, rolls the checkpoint back when any call fails and keeps all writes otherwise (handler.rs execute_batch, lines 1284-1366 on main). Every call has the same msg.sender, so only the signer's own calls share the state, and a fee sponsor pays fees without becoming a caller. Two unrelated users cannot share a batch, so no mined transaction of that kind can exist; zone portal batches are the one Tempo context that joins parties and are recorded as F-135. sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims.

cleared.check: Task 3, HyperEVM system transactions: are they joined with user transactions so that transient storage is shared?
cleared.result: No. The public replay client builds the environment for each system transaction and each signed transaction separately, calls transact once per transaction and commits state after each (run.rs lines 99-168 and the loop over system_txs at line 217). Each system transaction is its own transaction and starts with empty transient storage, so nothing joins it with a user's PoolManager call. The validator itself is closed (F-120).

cleared.check: Task 3, OP Stack deposit transactions: are deposits joined with other transactions?
cleared.result: No. The deposit specification processes each deposit as a transaction of its own with its own receipt, sender and gas accounting, and the revm journal used by op-reth clears transient storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize at the end of every transaction (inner.rs lines 141, 174 and 207) and restores it on checkpoint_revert (line 622). A deposit therefore shares no transient state with a user's PoolManager call.

cleared.check: Task 3, Arbitrum retryable redeems, automatic and manual: does a redeem run inside the transaction that scheduled it?
cleared.result: No. A redeem is returned by TxProcessor.ScheduledTxes as a new transaction (tx_processor.go lines 924-957) and the block processor applies it after the originating transaction as a transaction of its own, keeping the group's redeems and checkpoint (block_processor.go lines 91 and 126-159), and every transaction passes through StateDB.Prepare, which resets transient storage before code runs (state_transition.go lines 735-736). A redeem shares no transient state with the transaction that created or redeemed it.

cleared.check: L-799: in bor v2.12.0-beta, can the widened keccak result cache return the hash of a different input (key aliasing EVM memory, a fingerprint key, or an entry from an aborted speculative execution), which would give a wrong storage slot for a pool id (160 bytes) or a position key (58 bytes)?
cleared.result: Read on 2026-11-25 in 0xPolygon/bor at tag v2.12.0-beta (core/vm/instructions.go 258-330, interpreter.go 50-71, shared_cache.go, bounded_cache.go, keccak_cache.go). The widened cache keccakResultCache is a sync.Map from string(data) to common.Hash. Store copies the input (string(data)), so a stored key never points into EVM memory, and it takes the hash by value. Load builds a string view of memory without a copy, which sync.Map.Load compares and does not keep, and the calling goroutine owns that memory for the length of the call. The key is the full input, with no fingerprint, so inputs of different lengths or contents cannot share an entry. An entry written by a speculative execution that BlockSTM later discards is still keccak of its own key, since the hash is computed from the same bytes immediately before Store. On a miss the handler falls through to the ordinary path with the freshly computed hash. The cache exists only when a node sets the precompile cache flag (default false) and is dropped at the end of each block. The legacy path for 64 byte inputs, which v2.11.1 already has, copies the key into a [64]byte array. A standalone copy of the Load and Store logic (cycles/016/own-check.work/keccak_cache/main.go, sha256 standing in for keccak) was run with 16 goroutines on inputs of 58 and 160 bytes that differ in one byte, in buffers overwritten after every call: 12,800,000 lookups, 4,809,737 hits, 0 wrong, every stored key still maps to the hash of its own bytes, and a shorter run under the Go race detector reports no race. v2.12.0-beta is the only tag with this code; v2.12.0 does not exist yet and Polygon's endpoint reports v2.11.1. Whether Polygon's validators will set the flag is not known and does not matter for correctness as read. L-664 and L-668 keep the rerun of the opcode checks against a v2.12 node.

cleared.check: Leads L-032 and L-161 on the releases after v2.11.1: does any change to BlockSTM, its serial fallback or the merge of results let transient storage pass from one transaction to the next.
cleared.result: No. The executor, state database, journal, transient storage and state transition files are byte identical in v2.11.1, v2.11.2 and v2.12.0-beta, and the parallel state processor differs only in one error message. Cycle 11's reading therefore holds for every Polygon build that is released or proposed: each incarnation starts from a fresh state copy, Prepare installs a new transient map, and transient storage is not in the multi-version write set that the merge copies. The PoolManager's lock, deltas and synced currency (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) cannot leak across transactions on any of these builds.

cleared.check: Does 48 Club's virtual contract at 0x48, which its RPC uses to identify itself, change what a contract call to that address returns, so that a currency or recipient 0x48 behaves differently on its nodes.
cleared.result: No. Only a top-level eth_call with value 0x30 returns 0x30. The delegate's entry (bytes 0 to 0x268 of its 24,384 byte code) sends a caller equal to the PoolManager to a calldata driven program, a self call to another, and a caller equal to the hard coded owner to a third. cleared.check: RUSTSEC-2025-0137 (unsound reciprocal_mg10 in ruint before 1.17.0), which affects both public replay clients (hyper-evm-sync ruint 1.15.0, nanoreth f0cad31 ruint 1.16.0): can any EVM division reach reciprocal_mg10 with a divisor whose top bit is clear?
cleared.result: No. In ruint 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 every division goes through div_inlined (src/algorithms/div/mod.rs lines 47-104 of 1.16.0), which trims zero limbs and sends one and two limb divisors to div_nx1 and div_nx2. Both shift the divisor by its leading zeros before calling reciprocal or reciprocal_2 (src/algorithms/div/small.rs lines 69-75 and 138-144), and the normalized variants are only called when the shift is zero (lines 33-39, 109-114). The precondition d >= 2^63 that the advisory says is only debug-checked therefore always holds. DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD of the PoolManager (22, 3, 4, 3, 1 and 13 instances in the build) cannot reach the unsound input.

The comment itself says no block can pay for 4 GiB. The PoolManager's own memory use is bounded by its calldata and return data. cleared.check: L-808, RUSTSEC-2025-0137: which functions of ruint 1.15.0 (hyper-evm-sync, revm 19.2.0, revm-interpreter 15.2.0) and 1.16.0 (nanoreth f0cad31, hl-archive-node/revm fdf9b16, revm-interpreter 25.0.3) call reciprocal_mg10, and is the divisor normalised on the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD paths?
cleared.result: Yes on every path. reciprocal_mg10 is exported as reciprocal and called by reciprocal_2_mg10 (reciprocal.rs line 111), div_nx1_normalized and div_nx1 (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 39 and 75, 1.15.0 lines 27 and 62); reciprocal_2 is called by div_nx2_normalized, div_nx2, div_nxm_normalized and div_nxm (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 112 and 144, knuth.rs lines 35 and 120). The only non-test callers of those are algorithms::div (1.15.0 mod.rs lines 49-99) and div_inlined (1.16.0 mod.rs lines 56-107), which trim zero limbs, send one limb divisors with a one limb numerator to native division and route the rest to div_nx1, div_nx2 or div_nxm. Each of these shifts the divisor by its leading zeros before the reciprocal (small.rs lines 69-75 and 138-144, knuth.rs lines 105-120) and calls the normalized variant only when the shift is zero. Uint::div_rem, wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, reduce_mod, add_mod and mul_mod reach only those two entry points (div.rs and modular.rs of both tags). revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and 25.0.3 call wrapping_div and wrapping_rem after a zero check, add_mod and mul_mod directly, and / and % on absolute values in i256_div and i256_mod (arithmetic.rs lines 26-63 and 31-83, i256.rs lines 80-130 and 92-143); the hl-archive-node fork's arithmetic.rs, i256.rs and bitwise.rs equal the crates.io 25.0.3 files. The precondition d >= 2^63 therefore always holds, and FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 35, 48, 62-73, 112), SqrtPriceMath (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:62, 252), UnsafeMath (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14, 26) and TickBitmap (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26, 57-64) cannot hand it an unnormalised divisor.

A Rust harness (research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-library-paths.work/harness/src/main.rs) links each ruint version by path from the crates.io archives and runs DIV and MOD through wrapping_div and wrapping_rem with the handlers' zero check, SDIV and SMOD through a transcription of i256_div and i256_mod, ADDMOD and MULMOD through add_mod and mul_mod, and two sequences from the source: the 512 bit product and remainder of FullMath.mulDiv (two mul_mod calls, one by 2^256-1) and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp. 3,585,969 vectors: 106,769 from battery.py and targeted.py (every DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, MULDIV512 and DIVUP vector, including the 16,858 MULMOD and mulDiv vectors of the 1.21.0 equal-top-limb shape) and 3,479,200 new ones with divisors of every bit length 1 to 256 (every normalisation shift for one, two, three and four limb divisors), numerators of every limb count, 257 bit ADDMOD sums, 512 bit MULMOD products and FullMath shaped denominators. Both versions in release mode with debug assertions off, as the clients ship, gave 0 mismatches; the same builds with debug assertions on gave 0 mismatches and never tripped the d >= 2^63 assertion, which a direct call with d = 1 does trip (reciprocal.rs line 78 in 1.15.0, 79 in 1.16.0). cleared.check: Task 1, method and proof of execution. The harness of cycle 16 (category-labs/monad v0.16.7 with asmjit e8c8e2e4 and evmc f6b7c57e, v0.16.5 with evmc 34795f4e, the release keccak) was relinked with two recompiled objects only: a copy of category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp that, at chosen EVM pcs, emits an execution counter before the instruction (rax saved to and restored from a fixed address, mov and lea only, so flags and the virtual stack are untouched) and optionally, after the instruction, a call that records the word the instruction left on top of the stack (the code of Emitter::runtime_print_top1); and interpreter/execute.cpp built with a copy of instruction_table.hpp whose MONAD_VM_NEXT and MONAD_VM_NEXT_PUSH record the stack top at the same pcs. emitter.cpp is not changed. Two ways of reaching the sites were used: PoolManager calls (pc 12232, 15519, 22378, 22639) and, for operands no call can supply and for pc 16642, an entry into the deployed runtime's own basic block: bytes 0..46 of the 24,009-byte runtime are replaced by a 45-byte prologue (copy calldata[0x120:] to memory 0, push eight calldata words, jump to calldata word 0; a JUMPDEST at pc 38 stores the top word and returns it), the other 23,962 bytes unchanged. Entries used: 0x5703 (the 2^128 copy of mulDiv, called from Position.update at pcs 5969 and 5981), 0x5810 (the 2^96 copy, called from getAmount1Delta at pcs 23088 and 23161), 0x3c94 (Hooks.beforeSwap after the hook call) and 0x40d7 (the bytes4 mask block).
cleared.result: Arm identity. In the v0.16.7 asm log (which prints a comment per EVM instruction) the text emitted for each of the five site instructions is identical between the plain build, the counter build (once the five counter lines are removed; the rest of the 48,691-line log is identical) and the single-site capture builds (the plain text is a prefix of the capture build's text). The texts are: pc 22378 MULMOD loads a from [rbp-128..-104] into r13,r14,r15,r12 and b0,b1 from [rbp-96],[rbp-88], computes r10 = lo(a0*b0) by mulx, r11 = hi(a0*b0) + a1*b0 + a0*b1 (64-bit imul) and zeroes r8, r9; pc 22639 is the same with 32-bit imul and add on limb 1 (mod 2^96); pc 15519 SAR(128) of the word in r12..r15 is mov rax,r15; sar rax,63; mov r10,r14; mov r11,r15; mov r8,rax; mov r9,rax; pc 16642 SHL(3) of the word in r12..r15 is three shld and one shl by 3; pc 12232 CALLDATALOAD is the bswap_to_ymm arm with the bound test on the offset limbs and the 32-byte vmovups read. In v0.16.5 the same instructions open each site's text (v0.16.5 prints no per-instruction comment, so the text was located by the counter lines). Compiled from the prologue runtime, the enclosing blocks B5703, B5810, B3c94 and B40d7 equal the deployed runtime's blocks once label numbers, block numbers and read-only data offsets are replaced by the bytes they point to (both compiled in one process so that host pointers agree); the one exception, B3c94 under v0.16.5, differs only in the order of three independent stores at the block exit (see the v0.16.5 heap-address item). Marker counts, native = interpreter in every file and on both releases: pc 22378 274 (prologue) + 18 (ordinary calls); pc 22639 200 (prologue) + 57 (ordinary swaps) + 188 (hook swaps); pc 15519 116 (prologue) + 648 (ordinary swaps through a returns-delta hook); pc 16642 47 (prologue only); pc 12232 1,220 (ordinary extsload and exttload calls). cleared.check: Task 2 from the source: which callers pass a constant denominator, which pc each compiles to, and whether a wrong remainder at prod1 = 1 could become an accepted amount.
cleared.result: Callers. Position.update passes FixedPoint128.Q128 (src/libraries/Position.sol:93-96); both calls jump to 0x5703 (pcs 5969 and 5981), whose MULMOD is pc 22378. SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta passes denominator = FixedPoint96.Q96 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:240, :250); both of its compiled copies jump to 0x5810 (pcs 23088 and 23161), whose MULMOD is pc 22639. SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 pass Q96 as the multiplier with liquidity as the denominator (copy at 0x588a and mulDivRoundingUp, MULMOD by a runtime call), and SwapMath.sol:65, :74 and :104 use the denominator 1e6 (copy with MULMOD at pc 22513, runtime call); these are not mul_mod2 sites. Arithmetic. For a power-of-two denominator N = 2^k the correct remainder is prod0 mod N, which is never above prod0, so gt(remainder, prod0) at FullMath.sol:52 is 0 on a correct node and prod1 stays 1. The emitted arm can only produce a value below N (limbs 2 and 3 are zeroed, limb 1 is 32-bit for 2^96). With any remainder r below N, FullMath.sol:52-75 return at least 2^(256-k) - 1: 200,000 random cases per site of a Python transcription give a least value of exactly 2^160 - 1 for k = 96 and 2^128 - 1 for k = 128 (the borrow case r > prod0 with prod0 < N). Such a result cannot be accepted: Position.update returns it as feesOwed and Pool.modifyLiquidity casts it with toInt128 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:192, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-58), which reverts at 2^127 and above; getAmount1Delta returns at least 2^160 - 1, and every use reverts in a cast (Pool.sol:222-223 and :232-234 through SqrtPriceMath.sol:278-287 in modifyLiquidity; in a swap, SwapMath.sol:68-69 and :89-91 either cap the step at the target, after which the amount of at least 2^160 - 1 reaches the toInt128 casts at Pool.sol:455 or :459, or the comparison fails and the faulty value is replaced by amountRemaining). A quotient below 2^127 needs a remainder above 2^256 - 2^223 + prod0 at the 2^96 site and above 2^255 + prod0 at the 2^128 site, more than 2^222 above anything the arm can write. So the borrow of L-800 cannot be produced by this arm, and a remainder that stays below N changes an accepted amount on no path.

cleared.result: Not under v0.16.5. Four heap layouts of v0.16.5 give 2,000 of 2,000 cycle 15 scenarios equal between engines with identical native digests, and all v0.16.5 runs of this unit used a third and fourth layout. Different v0.16.5 validators can therefore run different machine code for the same contract, but no case where the order changes a result was found.

cleared.check: Shared stack arena of fork 0e44603 (core/vm/stack.go): one arena per EVM, each call frame starts at its parent's top, and stack() grows the slice with slices.Grow when fewer than 1,024 slots remain, while pop1Peek1 and pop2Peek1 hand out pointers into the slice. A parent that kept a pointer across a child call that grew the arena would read stale memory. Programs that push 2, 501 or 1,001 values, recurse to depth 0 to 8 so that every child forces a growth, and sum their own stack after the call.
cleared.result: 18 of 18 programs return (d+1)K(K+1)/2 on each chain and on Ethereum. opCall pops its operands by value and pushes its result through the arena pointer after the call (instructions.go:730-774), so no pointer survives a child frame. cleared.check: Can an ordinary account get a parent chain message executed with the PoolManager as sender?
cleared.result: No. The stock Inbox passes every message sender through applyL1ToL2Alias in _deliverToBridge (Inbox.sol:317-324), so a contract or unsigned message with the PoolManager as sender needs a parent chain sender equal to the PoolManager address minus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111, an address nobody holds a key or creation path for. The three ToFork functions undo the alias for an EOA caller, but they revert unless the parent chain id has changed, and the unsigned transaction they produce keeps the EOA check, which the PoolManager's code fails. Deposits credit the native balance without running code and are not a payment in settle, which reads msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364).

cleared.check: L-840 question 1. Does the spill step before the dependency loop of Emitter::write_to_final_stack_offsets in monad v0.16.5 remove every dependency cycle?
cleared.result: No, and it does not need to. The spill step (emitter.cpp:1401-1418) only frees one AVX register as scratch (init_yx1): when no register is free it moves the value of the first unreserved AVX holder (virtual_stack.cpp:530-541) to memory, or drops the register when the element already has a stack offset, general register or literal (virtual_stack.cpp:553-565). It runs before the dependency count is built at 1433-1461, so a spilled element is counted as a memory element. Cycles are left for the second loop (1564-1621). The dependency relation is a function: an element has at most one stack offset, so it blocks at most one other element (the owner of that offset). Every element that is not on a cycle is reached from a leaf and is written in the first loop (1478-1542), so after it exactly the cycle members have a count, and that count is 1. The second loop rotates each cycle through two AVX registers. yx1 is init_yx1 and yx2 is a free register or, when none is free, the register of the last AVX element written in the first loop (1550-1561). When no register is free, 15 of the 16 registers belong to elements other than init1; at most one of them (the popped jump target) is off the stack, so at least 14 AVX stack elements are written in the first loop and yx1 != yx2 holds in every order. Each cycle member's slot is read before it is overwritten, because the slots of a cycle are final indices of its own members only and stack indices of distinct elements are disjoint. The iteration order of the map decides which cycle is rotated first and which register serves as yx2; neither changes a stored word.

cleared.check: L-840 question 2. Is a dependency skipped at the AVX register check (emitter.cpp:1457-1459) ever read later from a register that an earlier write in the loop reassigned?
cleared.result: No. Every register write the writer emits goes to yx1 or yx2: the loads at 1496, 1499 and 1511 in the first loop and 1588-1598 in the cycle loop. In the first loop yx1 is init_yx1 until the first AVX element is popped, and from then on it is the register of the AVX element popped most recently (1484-1487). An AVX element x whose memory slot is a final index of another element e is not counted as a blocker of e, so e may be written over x's slot first. x is then read from its own register when it is popped. That register can be overwritten only after it became yx1, which happens when x itself is popped, and x is fully written by then. init_yx1 is a register no stack element holds. AVX elements are never on a cycle, because they have no outgoing edge, so all of them are written in the first loop, before any cycle-loop write to yx1 or yx2. The writer writes no general register: mov_general_reg_to_mem (1833-1840) only reads them, and mov_literal_to_ymm (1961-1988) writes only the target ymm and does not change flags. The pc of a popped jump target is taken into its operand before the writer runs (3544-3576).

cleared.check: L-840 question 3. Can an element whose stack offset lies below min_delta be left with a nonzero dependency count?
cleared.result: No element has such an offset. Stack offsets come from three places only: the entry elements of each index from -1 down to the new min_delta (virtual_stack.cpp:298-302 and 326-330), the positive offsets 0..max_delta-1 (305-308, 334-337) and offsets that a destroyed or moved element returned (free_stack_offset, 202-208), all of which were handed out from the first two. min_delta never rises inside a block (continue_block takes the minimum, 321). Stack::get also asserts its index is at most top_index and at() asserts it is inside negative_elems_ (365-383). An offset above top_index is skipped at 1450 and creates no count. Any element with a count after the first loop is on a cycle and has its count set to zero at 1577-1579. The instrumented build counted offset_below_min=0 and nonzero_after_cycles=0 in every compile.

cleared.check: L-840 task 2. The block-exit writer of v0.16.5 run in every forced order on the deployed Monad PoolManager runtime (24,009 bytes, the cycle 16 copy monad-pm-runtime.hex, sha256 9f68b8fc of the hex file), with a symbolic check of every block exit and a runtime replay of mined transactions.
cleared.result: The writer was rebuilt from the v0.16.5 file (sha256 1294ce58, equal to the jsDelivr copy fetched here) with both loops over dep_counts taken from a vector holding the same keys (src/patch_writer.py). The emitted instructions are the original ones in the forced order. Each emitted load and store also drives a symbolic machine, and at every block exit each final index must hold the element that owns it. One compile of the PoolManager has 659 block exits with something on the stack, 3314 stack elements in all, at most 24 elements and 9 blocked elements in one exit, 26 dependencies skipped at the AVX check, 98 cycles (longest 7) and no exit that has to spill an AVX register. Exits by element count: 1 to 6 elements 475, 7 to 15 170, 16 or more 14. Permutation indices 0 to 719 gave every block with up to 6 elements all its orders, with a seeded shuffle for larger ones (seed = index), and shuffle seeds 1 to 200 reordered every block: 920 compiles, 0 wrong final words, 0 AVX elements read after their register was overwritten, and the same final-state digest 18e601f3245c1db8 as the map's own order. The orders do change the machine code: two forced orders differ by 2,312 to 3,306 lines of the 48,757-line asm log. Two planted faults show the check can fail: one temporary register for cycles gave 140 to 141 wrong words per compile, and rereading AVX elements from memory gave 16 to 27 wrong words depending on the order (200 seeds). At run time the instrumented build replayed the 2,007 mined Monad PoolManager transactions of cycle 16 from their pre-state under 12 orders (map order, permutation indices 1 to 5, shuffle seeds 101 to 106): 24084 transaction runs, 0 mismatches between interpreter and native code, 0 divergences from the block. With the planted reread fault 1382 of 2,007 transactions mismatched. The runtime comparison is per transaction frame, not per block exit; the per-exit comparison is the symbolic one.

Monad has about 650 PoolManager transactions per 1,000 blocks and eth_getLogs is limited to 100 blocks, so a full census was not possible from public endpoints. All 30,092 transactions with a PoolManager log or an ERC-20 Transfer from or to the PoolManager in blocks 125,250,001 to 125,295,000 (eth_getLogs in 450 windows of 100 blocks, https://rpc.monad.xyz and https://rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, Monad/0.16.7 at start and end) were traced with callTracer. 33,893 completed ERC-20 syncs, 24,580 syncs inside reverted frames, 42,244 completed settles, all equal to the model's value; no transaction ends with an ERC-20 synced; 6,771 of 16,675 blocks hold several. The client source explains why: every transaction, and every re-execution after a failed optimistic merge, runs on a fresh State built over the block state (execute_transaction.cpp lines 458 to 497), transient storage lives in AccountState::transient_storage_ (account_state.hpp line 70), and BlockState::merge copies only the account and storage_ of each address (block_state.cpp lines 194 to 250), so transient storage never reaches the next transaction.

cleared.check: MegaETH client source: where transient storage is cleared between transactions.
cleared.result: mega-evm (main, version 1.7.4; crates.io 1.7.2) pins revm 40.0.3, which uses revm-context 18.0.3. TLOAD and TSTORE are the stock host handlers wrapped for compute gas (mega-evm src/evm/instructions.rs lines 611-612 and 2205-2206) and the host delegates tstore and tload to the stock journal (src/evm/host.rs lines 90-91). That journal clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize (revm-context 18.0.3 src/journal/inner.rs lines 154, 188, 246). The sandbox that mega-evm uses for keyless deploys merges accounts and storage only, and its own path calls commit_tx (src/evm/execution.rs line 1023). EIP-1153 requires all transient values to be discarded at the end of the transaction. The producer itself is closed; the mined census above is the evidence that it behaves this way.

cleared.result: For transaction 0x00cefb67 (index 111 of 124 in block 124,744,439) the two PoolManager slots of pool ee7e75fa that an earlier transaction of the block wrote are reported with the value that transaction wrote, not the parent-block value, and the other four slots equal the parent value. The rerun mismatches of that transaction therefore do not come from a wrong pre-state.

cleared.check: L-813 for Monad: does the reserve balance check report a frame as failed while keeping its writes?
cleared.result: No. revert_transaction calls dipped_into_reserve after the transaction has executed, for MONAD_FOUR and later, and a positive answer reverts the whole transaction; there is no frame-level outcome. The check skips accounts with contract code, so the PoolManager (24,009 bytes of code) is never tested, and a revert of the whole transaction discards every PoolManager write with it (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114).

cleared.check: Monad main, Barrett reduction module in uint256.hpp: does anything on the interpreter or compiler path of MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV or MOD call it?

cleared.check: F-138 pattern on the OP Stack: can an ordinary account post a deposit whose sender is the PoolManager, so that a token transfer runs in the PoolManager's name without unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 291-297)?
cleared.result: No. The portal aliases every caller that is not an EOA or a 7702 delegated EOA, and neither the PoolManager addresses nor their un-aliased preimages have code or a sent transaction on Ethereum; reaching either needs a private key for a fixed address or a CREATE2 address match, about 2^160 work.

cleared.check: Base Transactions (EIP-8430) phases against the transient storage model of the PoolManager (lead L-090, assumption A1).
cleared.result: A failing phase reverts its journal checkpoint, which restores TSTORE writes, and later phases are skipped; transient storage is shared across the calls of one transaction, as with a multicall contract. An unlock still has to finish inside one top-level call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Token gas reimbursement is a normal transfer call. Read from main before activation; the shipped release must be reread.

cleared.check: Denim's 200 ms blocks with second-resolution block.timestamp.
cleared.result: The PoolManager reads neither TIMESTAMP nor NUMBER, so its accounting is unaffected.

cleared.check: Lagoon post-execution transaction and SDM refunds: balance moves outside EVM execution (assumptions A2, A3).
cleared.result: The settlement credits only tx.from and debits only fee vaults and the block beneficiary, bounded by the transaction's own gas used, and runs after the frame ends, so it cannot fall between a sync and a settle and cannot touch the PoolManager's balance.

cleared.check: Lagoon SuperchainETHBridge.relayETH to the PoolManager.
cleared.result: relayETH forces ETH in through SafeSend without a call. Native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354), so ETH forced into the PoolManager credits nobody and stays as surplus; no pool or claim balance moves. This is the F-137 bracket only for an ERC-20 path, which relayETH does not have.

cleared.check: EIP-7825 transaction gas cap on these chains and its effect on swaps (assumption A9).
cleared.result: Same cap as Ethereum for user transactions, and deposits are exempt up to their 20 million gas guarantee. A swap too heavy for one transaction can be split with price limits and a liquidity removal has no loop over other ticks (OPCODES.md, cycle 18), so the cap delays without loss, as recorded in F-064. Simulated calls ignore the cap on all seven endpoints, which earlier scripts must be read with.

cleared.check: Which client produces Celo mainnet blocks today (L-877), from statements after the switch, header markers, and the block hashes reported by the two builds behind forno.
cleared.result: celo-reth. Celo Core Co announced on 22 July 2026 that mainnet is running op-reth (Celo's build is celo-reth). The decisive later statement is op-geth pull request 509, merged 18 August 2026: block 75,046,581 holds a CIP-64 transaction (index 29, 0xe9e0248c...) that celo-reth's fee rule accepts and op-geth's rejects; 'celo-reth nodes processed the block, op-geth nodes rejected it as a BAD BLOCK', 'the block is canonical', and 'the lenient rule is still live in the sequencer'. A sequencer that applies celo-reth's rule and not op-geth's is not op-geth. cleared.result: The swap step was taken from the tagged source and agrees with the reruns below. The tick table is a doubly linked list of initialized ticks: ticks(int24) returns liquidityTotal, liquidityDelta, prevTick and nextTick. prevTickGlobal and nextTickGlobal bracket the current tick, and a three layer bitmap tree is used only to find a neighbour on insertion (TickStructure._addOrRemoveTick, TickTree.getNextTick). The fee in pips is globalState.lastFee. On 1.0/1.1 it is changed by Fee(uint16) when the plugin calls setFee. On 1.2.2 the plugin's beforeSwap returns overrideFee and pluginFee, the fee is overrideFee + pluginFee when overrideFee is not 0 and lastFee + pluginFee otherwise, and SwapFee is logged just before Swap. The community fee and the plugin fee only split feeAmount after the step and change neither price nor amounts. PriceMovementMath.movePriceTowardsTarget is the v3 step with the input recomputed from the new price, and TokenDeltaMath.getToken0Delta/getToken1Delta and PriceMovementMath.getNewPrice equal SqrtPriceMath getAmount0Delta, getAmount1Delta, getNextSqrtPriceFromInput and getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput operation by operation. cleared.check: Task 2. Which executor answers each public method: eth_call, eth_estimateGas, eth_callMany, eth_createAccessList, eth_simulateV1, the realtime methods and the mega_ namespace.
cleared.result: No documented read-only method is run by the sequencer. The gateway sends eth_call to its compute pool and rewrites it to the node method mega_callWithBlock. It sends eth_estimateGas there too, rewritten to eth_estimateGasWithCpuLimit, and sends eth_callMany and eth_createAccessList to the same pool. Each page says the node simulates the call. The architecture page says RPC nodes are replicas that apply the sequencer's results without running them again, and that replicas are the default. Called directly, mega_callWithBlock and eth_simulateV1 return -32601 'is not supported', and debug_traceCall and trace_call are listed as unavailable. The mega_ methods that remain (getBlockWitness, getWithdrawalProof, outputAtBlock) read data and execute nothing. eth_sendRawTransactionSync and realtime_sendRawTransaction return the sequencer's own receipt for a submitted transaction. That is the producer's result, but only for a real transaction, which this review may not send. No response field names the executor. The battery and the targeted vectors therefore cannot reach the producer through a read-only call. This rests on the published docs. The gateway source (mega-rpc) is private, so it is unconfirmed that the compute pool holds replicas only.

cleared.check: Task 3. What the docs and public source say about the producer's compiler, and what the only public MegaETH compiler computes for MULMOD, SAR, SHL, SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD and CALLDATALOAD, with constant operands at pcs 22378, 22639, 15519, 16642 and 12232.
cleared.result: The docs never mention a compiler or JIT. llms-full.txt (752,661 bytes) has no match for jit, AOT, ahead-of-time, evmone or revmc. Only the stateless-validator README (line 26) calls the sequencer's executor parallel and JIT-compiled. The one public compiler is megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler, which is archived (default branch aot-compiler). It specialises nothing on constant operands. compiler.cpp passes immediates only to PUSH and fuses only PUSH followed by JUMP or JUMPI (lines 136-139, 175-180), so MULMOD by 2^128 or 2^96, SAR 128, SHL 3 and CALLDATALOAD run the generic handler. Several of its handlers break the specification. A transcription compiled with clang 18 (build/proto_handlers.cpp and .out) confirms four of them: (1) sar computes is_neg as x < 0 on an unsigned _BitInt(256) (aot_instructions.hpp:297-305 with aot_execution_state.hpp:18), so SAR(128, -5) gives 2^128-1 where the specification gives all ones; (2) signextend builds its mask as 1u << (b-1) in 32 bits (aot_instructions.hpp:207-218), so SIGNEXTEND(15, 2^127+7) gives no sign fill; (3) byte shifts by a byte count where a bit count is needed (lines 275-285); (4) mulmod writes stack[2] and never pops (lines 184-190). sdiv and smod divide _BitInt values, which is undefined at INT_MIN / -1. Dynamic JUMP lands on the next JUMPDEST at or above the target, because get_jumpdest never checks the key it found (aot_execution_state.hpp:53-58). The README says the prototype supports opcodes up to Shanghai. The PoolManager build hits those handlers at 19 SAR, 114 SIGNEXTEND (40 of them SIGNEXTEND 15) and 13 MULMOD sites, and every swap unpacks a BalanceDelta with sar(128) and signextend(15) (src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:63, :69). Under those handlers mined swap amounts would be wrong in nearly every block. The validator reproduces every block's state root, and mined swaps replay to the unit (OPCODES.md cycles 10 to 18). So the production executor does not use these handlers, and the prototype says nothing about the code that writes blocks. Its source is not public, and the five sites can be read only through mined results.

cleared.check: Task 4. Mined executions at the five sites and re-execution of their blocks with the pre-state anchored to the parent root. 212 PoolManager transactions were traced with debug_traceTransaction (struct logger): all 116 transactions with a PoolManager log in blocks 32,814,963 to 32,826,734 (123 logs in 100 blocks), all 82 transactions with a Swap in the 51 pools whose hook has BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA (from the 143 Initialize events of the full history), and the 14 census transactions that call extsload(bytes32[]). The selection is complete, not sampled, so there is no seed. The first pass hit HTTP 429 on 107 transactions; those were rerun on one thread with 1.5 s pauses on the same endpoint. No other endpoint was used. Each block was then run with the stateless validator build of cycle 16 (e1618ed7, mega-evm v1.7.3), anchored at the parent block's hash.
cleared.result: Executions inside PoolManager code frames: pc 15519 (SAR of a hook's BeforeSwapDelta, src/types/BeforeSwapDelta.sol:27 via src/libraries/Hooks.sol:266-270) ran 87 times in 82 transactions and 79 blocks; pc 12232 (CALLDATALOAD of the array length, src/Extsload.sol:42) ran 14 times in 14 transactions; pcs 22378, 22639 and 16642 never ran. Every replica result equals Python. All 87 SAR inputs have the top bit clear and 17 are zero words, so no mined hook returned a negative specified delta. None of the 116 new transactions reaches any site. All 193 blocks (93 site blocks and 100 new blocks) were reproduced, state root and receipts root included, with the witness pre-state checked against the parent's state root. The cycle 16 build with a planted MULMOD fault fails 32 of 45 of these blocks: 29 of 30 new blocks and 3 of 15 returns-delta blocks. So the comparison can see a wrong product in ordinary swaps. Cycle 17 showed that a whole-output comparison cannot see a faulty word at pcs 15519, 22378 or 22639, because SIGNEXTEND 15 at pc 15522 and the quotient at FullMath.sol:66-75 drop the bits concerned. The same property means a fault at those sites changes no amount. pc 22378 runs only in calls that revert at Pool.sol:192, and pc 16642 has no caller. This raises the mined coverage of pc 15519 and pc 12232 from zero to the counts above. It cannot raise coverage of the other three sites, because no mined transaction reaches them.

cleared.check: Every non-test caller of enter_execution in evm2 35aa3280 (the was_running flag) and what it does with the transient storage map.
cleared.result: enter_execution (crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs:454-458) only sets running and the guard puts the old value back on drop (mod.rs:1230-1239). It has five callers: execute_precompile (mod.rs:407), inspect_log (mod.rs:969), execute_tx (mod.rs:1315), execute_message_inspected (mod.rs:1456) and run_interpreter (mod.rs:1854). Four of them run a precompile, an inspector hook, a message or an interpreter frame inside the transaction that is already running, on the same State and therefore on the same transient map, which is what a CALL does on Ethereum. The fifth, execute_tx, is the entry of a top-level transaction and is reached only from transact and transact_with_inspector. The flag exists so that setters can refuse changes while code runs (mod.rs:421-443). It does not start a second transaction.

cleared.check: Where evm2 creates, clears and copies the transient map: clear_transaction_state, ExecutedTx resolution, committed_copy, take_transient_storage, rollback.
cleared.result: The map is a field of State (crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs:58-59). clear_transaction_state empties it with the journal, logs and warm sets (state/mod.rs:555-569). It runs when an executed transaction is committed, discarded or detached (tx.rs:222-245), when a transaction or system call fails (mod.rs:1318-1320, system.rs:133-136), after validate_tx (mod.rs:1346) and when the backing database is replaced (state/mod.rs:269-272 through Evm::set_database at mod.rs:700-702). committed_copy builds a new State with an empty map (state/mod.rs:135-150) and has no caller outside tests in evm2 or in the 578 Rust files of the Tempo workspace. take_transient_storage removes the slots of one named address (state/mod.rs:873-878). Each TSTORE is journaled (state/mod.rs:837-866) and rollback restores it (state/mod.rs:911-918), so a reverted frame or batch puts the PoolManager's slots back. Nothing clears the map between frames: execute_initial_frame in crates/evm2/src/ethereum/mod.rs contains no clearing step.

cleared.check: Every non-test caller of transact, call_tx, validate_tx, system_call, execute_system_call, committed_copy, set_database and take_transient_storage in the Tempo workspace at a9d6748 (all 52 members including consensus, payload builder, transaction pool, precompiles, precompile macros, zones) and in evm2 (including evm2-jit and evm2-inspectors).
cleared.result: None runs while a user transaction is on the call stack. Block level: the EIP-2935 history system call before the first transaction (crates/evm/src/block.rs:858-870) and the committee system call after the last one (block.rs:554-603, called from finish_with_block_access_list at block.rs:1043-1048); evm2's own block executor runs transact once per block transaction and its system calls before or after them (crates/evm2/src/block/ethereum/execution.rs:188, 213, 285-458). Separate EVM instances: the pool validator (crates/transaction-pool/src/validator.rs:572), the payload prewarm workers (crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs:181-194), the zone sequencer, payload and RPC crates (crates/zones/evm/src/executor.rs:306, crates/zones/payload/src/builder.rs:865, crates/zones/payload/src/prewarming.rs:176, crates/zones/node/src/rpc/mod.rs:1507), genesis (crates/evm/src/genesis.rs:76, 104) and the fuzz harness. The system transaction handler calls execute_system_call as the body of the system transaction itself, at its start (crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs:512-536), and only for the fixed system signature (crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs:234-236). No precompile, the fee manager, the account keychain, the payment channel reserve, the T14 configurable account shim or the batch handler calls any of these functions. Evm::transact has no running check (mod.rs:1285-1288), so the guarantee rests on there being no such caller, which the search confirms for this revision.

cleared.check: Storage credit settlement drains transient slots at the end of a transaction (take_transient_storage).
cleared.result: settle_storage_credit_refunds takes only the slots of 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 (crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs:444-490) and is called from settle_transaction (config.rs:251-256), which the AA handler calls after execute_batch has returned (crates/evm/src/handler.rs:1704-1720). cleared.check: Nested calls made by precompiles (TIP-20 zone deposit forwarding) and T14 batch calls: map shared, emptied or cleared?
cleared.result: The only precompile in production that calls user code is TIP-20 deposit_virtual (crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs:1073-1115), which goes through the storage provider's call (crates/precompiles/src/storage/evm.rs:677-740). That runs a message with Host::execute_call on the same Evm, so it shares the map like a CALL and is journaled; the provider refuses it inside a checkpoint or past the nested call limit (evm.rs:689-695), and deposit_virtual refuses it from inside another precompile (tip20/mod.rs:1081-1088). The callee sees msg.sender equal to the token, so a reentry into the PoolManager from the portal has the token as its own locker with its own deltas, which is ordinary CALL semantics; the payout side of that path is F-135. A batch of calls in one Tempo transaction runs each call as a top-level frame on the same State under one checkpoint (crates/evm/src/handler.rs:1284-1371) with the same sender, which matches a smart account multicall on Ethereum: an unlock has relocked before its call returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), and a sync left open by one call of the batch belongs to the same sender.

cleared.check: Task 1, the code the C-Chain runs and every writer of the asset partition. The public endpoint answered web3_clientVersion avalanchego/1.15.3 commit 983815fd, go 1.26.10, before and after every batch. At v1.15.3 the node registers the SAE C-Chain VM for the EVM chain id (node/node.go:1240, saevm.Factory from vms/saevm/cchain), and graft/coreth holds only params, nativeasset, customtypes and precompile packages. A search of the whole avalanchego v1.15.3 tree and of the libevm revision it pins (d398bc4dbe41, go.mod:30) lists every caller of AddAssetBalance, SubAssetBalance, GetAssetBalance, SetState with SkipStateKeyTransformation and MarkHeldXChainAsset.
cleared.result: There are four writers and none is open to an ordinary account today. (1) Import.transferNonAVAX calls AddAssetBalance for each non-AVAX output (vms/saevm/cchain/tx/import.go:237-246), run from FinishExecutingBlock (vms/saevm/cchain/hooks.go:257-269). Import.sanityCheck rejects any non-AVAX input or output with no fork gate (tx/import.go:117-128). The txpool runs it on every gossiped transaction (txpool/txpool.go:163) and PotentialEndOfBlockOps runs it on every atomic transaction, also when VerifyBlock rebuilds a peer's block and compares hashes (hooks.go:464, sae/blocks.go:77-90, sae/block_builder.go:77-127). A block carrying a non-AVAX import is therefore rebuilt without it and rejected. (2) Export.transferNonAVAX calls SubAssetBalance (tx/export.go:267-281); export inputs are rejected the same way (export.go:136-138) and each input needs a secp256k1 signature that recovers to the debited address (export.go:174-196), which the PoolManager, a contract, cannot give. (3) NativeAssetCall (graft/coreth/nativeasset/contract.go:142-157) is mapped to DeprecatedContract, which reverts, from Banff on (graft/coreth/params/hooks_libevm.go:113-124, 133-147). (4) AddAssetBalance with a zero amount only touches the account (extstate/statedb.go:139-143). The validators that still run the older full coreth tree check the same thing behind rules.IsBanff (coreth plugin/evm/atomic/import_tx.go:106-117 on ava-labs/coreth master and at avalanchego v1.14.2). The SAE end of block ops only move native AVAX and nonces (vms/saevm/hook/hook.go:186-212, saexec/execution.go:416-436).

cleared.check: Task 2, whether a write into the asset partition of the PoolManager account could land on a key the EVM later reads as a PoolManager slot.
cleared.result: No, by construction and independent of who writes. libevm applies TransformStateKey in GetState, GetCommittedState and SetState unless the caller passes SkipStateKeyTransformation (libevm core/state/statedb.go:346-363, 419-425, statedb.libevm.go:115-121). The C-Chain hook clears bit 0 of byte 0 of every EVM key (extstate/statedb.go:48-56), so SLOAD and SSTORE (core/vm/instructions.go:517, 528) only reach keys with that bit clear. Asset keys always have it set (assetBalanceKey, extstate/statedb.go:59-62). The two key sets are disjoint, so no asset balance can equal any PoolManager slot, including the half of the keccak derived pool, tick, position and bitmap slots whose own bit 248 is set: those are stored at the key with the bit cleared. The fold of F-040 is the price of this separation and is already covered there. The only raw EVM read is GetCommittedState before Apricot Phase 1 (extstate/statedb.go:102-113), which sets SSTORE refunds of blocks from 2020 and does not run today.

For 52 pool state words of 13 pools seen in recent Swap logs (32 of them with bit 248 set in the slot), eth_getStorageAt of the slot, eth_getStorageAt of the slot with bit 248 flipped, extsload of both all return the same non-zero word. The raw asset partition could not be read: eth_getProof answers 'the method eth_getProof is not available' on api.avax.network (the SAE RPC does not register it), debug_storageRangeAt, debug_dumpBlock and debug_accountRange do not exist, and the other public endpoints tried (publicnode, ankr, 1rpc, drpc, meowrpc, omniatech) returned a challenge page, an API key demand, a quota error or no answer. cleared.check: Task 4, whether the held X-chain asset flag (the former IsMultiCoin) on an account changes SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, SELFBALANCE or EXTCODEHASH.
cleared.result: The flag is a bool account extra (customtypes/state_account_ext.go:11-25), set only by AddAssetBalance and read only there. TransformStateKey ignores the address (extstate/statedb.go:48), so SLOAD and SSTORE are the same with or without it. BALANCE and SELFBALANCE read the native balance, which the flag does not touch. The flag enters stateObject.empty() (libevm core/state/state_object.go:95-97), so it only matters for an account with nonce 0, zero balance and no code: EXTCODEHASH of such an account returns keccak256 of empty code instead of zero (instructions.go:417-426), it escapes EIP-161 deletion, and a value call to it skips the new account surcharge. The PoolManager has code and nonce 1, so none of this applies to it, and src/ does not use EXTCODEHASH or code size checks (no match for extcodehash, extcodesize or .code.length in src/). The CREATE collision check reads nonce and code hash only (core/vm/evm.go:456-459), so a pre-Banff asset balance at a future address cannot block a deployment.

cleared.check: Native AVAX that an ordinary account can push into the PoolManager outside the EVM: an atomic import whose output address is the PoolManager mints AVAX to it at the end of a block (hook.go:209-211, tx/import.go:206-224), and export cannot debit it without its key.
cleared.result: Harmless. Native settle credits msg.value and never reads the native balance (src/PoolManager.sol:349-355), and sync of the native currency only resets the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:279-283). Minted AVAX is a surplus nobody can claim through the PoolManager, the same as a forced send by SELFDESTRUCT on Ethereum, and it arrives between transactions, never inside an unlock.

cleared.check: Lead L-913, measured. For each network, the gas cap of a mined ordinary transaction, and the gas of a full liquidity exit of a real position by its real owner at the real PoolManager, compared with that cap and not with the eth_call limit.
cleared.result: Every sampled exit fits under the mined cap with a margin of at least 15 times on every network, including HyperEVM small blocks. Method: for each network, positions of the deployed PositionManager were sampled below nextTokenId (the newest 40 ids and random older ones), kept when liquidity > 0 and hooks = 0, and eth_estimateGas was called from ownerOf(tokenId) for modifyLiquidities with BURN_POSITION (all liquidity removed and fees collected) then TAKE_PAIR to the owner, on 2026-11-25. Largest estimate per network (positions estimated): Ethereum 232,219 (20), OP Mainnet 281,366 (9), Base 235,285 (20), Unichain 234,404 (7), Zora 222,099 (20), World Chain 285,481 (20), Ink 167,714 (4), Soneium 240,197 (20), Celo 243,990 (20), X Layer 215,639 (20), Arbitrum One 258,999 (20), Robinhood Chain 269,856 (20), Elysium 223,274 (20), Polygon 403,097 (20), BNB Chain 320,073 (19), Avalanche 264,918 (20), Monad 382,525 (18), MegaETH 534,813 (20), Tempo 976,067 (20), Arc 205,841 (20), HyperEVM 197,982 (20). Mined caps: 16,777,216 on Ethereum, the seven OP Stack chains, BNB Chain and Arc; 30,000,000 on Celo (block limit), Monad and Tempo; 32,000,000 on the Arbitrum family; 33,554,432 on Polygon; 3,000,000 in HyperEVM small blocks and 30,000,000 in big blocks; at least 50,000,000 on Avalanche and 210,000,000 on X Layer (block limit); at least 984,000,000 on MegaETH (mined user transactions). The worst ratio is Tempo, 976,067 against 30,000,000. The two failures (one burned between calls on OP Mainnet, one BNB Chain token whose transfer reverts, 0x9c3aba46) are not gas. The gas of the exit does not grow with anything another account does: Pool.modifyLiquidity has no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), it writes two tick words, at most two bitmap words, the position (src/libraries/Position.sol:76-101) and the pool liquidity (Pool.sol:226), and clears ticks with delete (Pool.sol:592-594). The only zero to nonzero writes it can make are the two fee growth inside words of the position (Position.sol:100-101), which depend on the position, not on others. Outputs: out/exits.json, out/exits_137.json.

cleared.check: MegaETH, normal sequencer path: can an ordinary account grow the SALT bucket of a victim position's fee growth words until the two fresh writes of a removal (Position.sol:100-101) exceed what one user transaction can carry?
cleared.result: Not at a practical cost. User transactions with 984,000,000 gas were mined in blocks 32,838,613 to 32,838,912, so the per transaction cap set by the sequencer is at least that. Under the rule recorded in F-105 (storage gas 20,000 times (multiplier minus 1), a bucket doubles at 80 percent use), two writes exceed 984,000,000 only at multiplier 32,768. My model puts that at about 3.36 million entries in one bucket and 7.3e14 gas, about 733 ETH at the 1,000,000 wei base fee floor, spread over about 74,000 blocks, because each entry costs more as the bucket grows and a 10,000,000,000 gas block holds fewer of them. The base fee would rise long before that. The L1 deposit path with its 1,000,000 gas limit stays F-105.

cleared.check: Scripts in OPCODES.md that ran out of gas or ran above the mined cap under eth_call (full-range swaps on Polygon, Monad and Tempo, scripts above 16,777,216 on the OP Stack chains).
cleared.result: These are swaps. Pool.swap stops at the caller's sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a swap too long for one transaction is split by price limits, and no victim needs a swap to exit. The dust-tick cost hazard is already F-064, F-111, F-115, F-039 and F-063.

cleared.check: Ethereum: every path that starts a call whose sender is not set by a signature or by the calling frame, and whether an ordinary account can make that sender the PoolManager.
cleared.result: None can. The only such calls are the EIP-4788, EIP-2935 and request queue system calls (including the builder deposit and exit queues in go-ethereum master), each with From params.SystemAddress 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe and a fixed target (core/state_processor.go lines 379-395, 411-425, 465-480; params/protocol_params.go line 246). Signed transactions must come from an account without code other than a delegation (core/state_transition.go preCheck, line 602). An EIP-7702 authority is recovered from its signature (core/types/tx_setcode.go lines 145-165) and is rejected if it holds code that is not a delegation (core/state_transition.go lines 1144-1146), so the PoolManager, with 24,009 bytes of code and nonce 1, can never be an authority.

cleared.check: Polygon: bor state sync (commitState), span commits and any other system message, and whether their sender can be the PoolManager.
cleared.result: No. Every system message is built by GetSystemMessage with From params.BorSystemAddress 0xffffFFFfFFffffffffffffffFfFFFfffFFFfFFfE and Value 0 (consensus/bor/statefull/processor.go lines 71-80, params/config.go line 271), and CommitState sends it to the StateReceiver (consensus/bor/contract/client.go line 73). The StateReceiver accepts only that system address (System.sol lines 4-7) and forwards each record to its receiver as onStateReceive(uint256,bytes) with itself as msg.sender (StateReceiver.sol lines 42-57). No path names a sender chosen by Ethereum or Heimdall. The PoolManager has no fallback and no onStateReceive, so a record naming it as receiver reverts. Its nonce on Polygon is 1.

cleared.check: BNB Smart Chain: Parlia system transactions, who signs them and where they may go.
cleared.result: Every system message is built with From header.Coinbase (parlia.go lines 1389, 2069, 2096, 2110, 2131, 2137-2146), the coinbase must equal the address recovered from the header seal (lines 996-998), and a transaction counts as a system transaction only if its target is one of the fourteen system contracts, its gas price is zero and its recovered sender is the coinbase (lines 323-335, 106-121). The sender is therefore a validator key and the target a fixed system contract. Even a validator cannot make it the PoolManager, because that would need the PoolManager's private key. The PoolManager's nonce is 1.

cleared.check: Avalanche C-Chain: atomic import and export, the native asset precompiles, and any other path whose sender is not a signer or calling frame.
cleared.result: None reaches the EVM with a chosen sender. An import is an operation that mints to the named addresses and runs no EVM code (vms/saevm/cchain/tx/import.go lines 206-225, hooks.go lines 228-243). An export debits a C-Chain address only when a secp256k1 signature recovers to that address (export.go lines 175-197). nativeAssetCall used the precompile's caller as sender when it was active and is now DeprecatedContract, which reverts (graft/coreth/nativeasset/contract.go lines 176-180); an eth_call to 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000002 and 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000001 on avalanchego/1.15.3 reverted with empty data.

cleared.check: Monad: system transactions and staking syscalls.
cleared.result: A system transaction is accepted only when its recovered sender is SYSTEM_SENDER 0x6f49a8F621353f12378d0046E7d7e4b9B249DC9e, it is a legacy transaction, and its target is the staking precompile (validate_system_transaction.cpp lines 47, 51, 59); it then runs the native staking syscall, not EVM code at a chosen address (execute_system_transaction.cpp lines 178-182, 205-232). SYSTEM_SENDER cannot be an EIP-7702 authority (validate_monad_transaction.cpp line 53). The header comment calls it a key known to consensus (system_sender.hpp lines 22-25); I did not establish whether the key is public. In neither case can the sender be the PoolManager, whose nonce is 1.

cleared.check: MegaETH: deposits, mega system transactions, keyless deploys and pre-block system calls, for an ordinary account.
cleared.result: An ordinary account cannot make any of them carry the PoolManager as sender. Deposits take from from the portal, which aliases contract callers (see the MegaETH finding of this unit for the governance path). Mega system transactions must be legacy transactions recovered to 0xA887dCB9D5f39Ef79272801d05Abdf707CFBbD1d and calling the Oracle contract (system/tx.rs lines 22-25, 40-70; execution.rs lines 104-110). Pre-block system calls use 0xff..fe (system/tx.rs lines 129-133). The keyless deploy signer is recovered from its signature (cleared in earlier cycles).

cleared.check: Tempo: system transactions, sub-blocks, fee payers, type 0x76 batches with keychain signatures, and TIP-1107 configurable accounts (T14, scheduled for 8 December 2026).
cleared.result: None lets an ordinary account act as the PoolManager. A system transaction is a legacy transaction with signature (0,0) and sender Address::ZERO (envelope.rs lines 26-29, 234-236, 379-384), and the block executor accepts one only with target address zero carrying sub-block metadata, refusing every other target (block.rs lines 617-660); the committee system call uses caller zero and a fixed target (lines 589-591). Sub-block transactions are refused (lines 671-676; handler.rs line 1400). A fee payer signs separately and does not change the sender. A keychain signature names user_address, which must equal the recovered signer (handler.rs lines 667-676); a key authorization must be signed by that account or, from T6, by an admin key of it (handler.rs lines 566-573, 775-792); and the keychain precompile accepts authorizeKey only when msg.sender is tx.origin and the transaction is signed by the root key or an admin key (account_keychain/mod.rs lines 1193-1209). The PoolManager is never tx.origin, so no key can be registered for it. A configurable account address is the last 20 bytes of a keccak256 of its configuration (tip-1107.md lines 84-99) and must have empty code or the 0xef marker (line 171); the PoolManager has code, and matching its address would need a 160 bit preimage. Address zero, the protocol fee controller on Tempo, reaches only the sub-block metadata target and the committee contract.

cleared.check: Arc: who may name the sender of a CallFrom subcall, checked in source and on chain.
