On arc/v1: an EOA calling CallFrom directly with the PoolManager as sender reverted with 'unauthorized caller'; an EOA calling Memo with a USDC transfer ran it as the EOA (reverted 'transfer amount exceeds balance'); a contract placed by state override calling Memo reverted with 'sender spoofing requires tx.origin as sender'. The PoolManager is never tx.origin.

cleared.check: HyperEVM: senders of system transactions in a fresh census, and whether an ordinary account can make HyperCore name the PoolManager.
cleared.result: In blocks 52231708 to 52233207 (1500 blocks, eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet') there were 1031 system transactions from 28 senders: the HYPE bridge 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, 25 token system addresses 0x20..., the CoreDepositWallet 0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24 (2,175 bytes of code) and the treasury 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00. None names the PoolManager or its owner as sender, target or argument, HyperCore spotMeta links none of 195 linked tokens to either, and the PoolManager's nonce is 1. The archive client takes the sender from the upstream from field, falling back to 0x2222... for empty input and the token system address otherwise (nanoreth src/node/types/reth_compat.rs lines 236-249), and treats any zero gas price transaction as a system transaction (executor.rs lines 44-49), so the sender is whatever HyperCore states. That choice stays with HyperCore at operator level, recorded as F-020; an ordinary account cannot link a token to the PoolManager (cleared in cycle 4).

cleared.check: Has any path that writes a sender outside a signature ever acted as the PoolManager on the nine networks?
cleared.result: No evidence of it. eth_getTransactionCount of the PoolManager is 1 on all nine endpoints (Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM), the value set at creation. Deposits, Parlia system transactions, Monad system transactions and HyperEVM system transactions bump the sender's nonce, so none of them has been sent in its name. Bor system messages and Tempo system transactions do not bump a nonce, but their senders are fixed constants.

cleared.check: Signature checks that tokens or Permit2 could run on behalf of the PoolManager (EIP-2612 permit, ERC-1271).
cleared.result: None can succeed. src/ has no isValidSignature function (no match for isValidSignature or 1271 in src/), so an ERC-1271 check against the PoolManager reverts or returns no magic value, and an ecrecover check would need its private key. The PoolManager also never approves a spender: its only outgoing calls are transfer, balanceOf, the hook selectors, unlockCallback and empty value calls (src/types/Currency.sol:40-80, src/PoolManager.sol:104-114).

cleared.check: What the code does when a call reaches it with msg.sender equal to the PoolManager itself.
cleared.result: Nothing useful to an attacker. unlock calls IUnlockCallback(msg.sender).unlockCallback, and the PoolManager has no such function, so the call reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). take, settle, mint, burn, clear, swap, modifyLiquidity and donate require the lock (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99). The owner functions check msg.sender against the stored owner (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:19-23) and fee collection against protocolFeeController (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57). The danger of a forged PoolManager sender lies in calls to tokens, which bypass all of this code.

cleared.check: L-907: which reading of CAS20 routing is right, the cycle 19 probe (byte 10 = 0x02 or 0xff reverts under Jenner) or the tagged source (only ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 are routed).
cleared.result: The tagged source is right and the probe was misread. The three cycle 19 addresses 0xca52...0001, 0xca52...0000 and 0xca52...00ff all have byte 10 equal to 0x00. A new probe with byte 10 in {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0xff} on dataseed1 (Geth v1.8.2 4e1c8247), dataseed (same build), 48 Club (two builds in one batch, 9b93ce23 and 132104cd) and reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f, with web3_clientVersion before and after, shows ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 reverting and 0x02 and 0xff answering empty success with gas estimate 21000 under the Jenner time override, and all of them answering empty success without it. No build routes differently from the tag, so the lead's concern that validators on different builds disagree has no support in these answers.

cleared.check: L-908: every CAS20 function at v1.8.2 that changes a holder's balanceOf without a transfer signed or sent by that holder, who may call it, and whether an account with no role can move the PoolManager's balance between its own sync and settle.
cleared.result: No such path for an account with no role. balanceOf reads the raw balance slot for both variants (cas20_token.go lines 88-93); the Stablecoin variant adds only currency() (cas20_stablecoin.go lines 35-48); the Asset multiplier changes only scaledBalanceOf, balanceOfUI and totalSupplyUI (cas20_asset.go). The balance changing entries are mint and batchMint (MINT role, cas20_admin.go and cas20_asset.go lines 501-506), burn of the caller's own balance (BURN role), seizeWithMemo (SEIZE role, subject to the seize exempt policy), updateMultiplier (OPERATOR role, no balanceOf change), transferFrom (needs an allowance the PoolManager never grants; the PoolManager has no approve call) and permit (ecrecover only, cas20_permit.go lines 198-244, so a contract holder cannot be the signer). There is no interest, rebase, forced conversion or mint to all holders. A mint to the PoolManager between sync and settle credits the settler (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), but only a MINT role holder can do it, so it is an issuer action already recorded under F-007 and F-076.

cleared.check: L-887: whether a CAS20 token answers balanceOf or transfer differently when the caller is a contract under CALL, STATICCALL or DELEGATECALL.
cleared.result: Only the frame type matters, as the source says, and the PoolManager uses the frames that work. cas20EnterCall rejects DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE with DelegateCallNotAllowed() and any nonzero value with NonPayable() (cas20.go lines 88-100; DelegateCall passes directCall = false at evm.go line 461), and writes in a STATICCALL frame fail with write protection. On Chapel (Jenner active) the live token 0xca52000000000000000001217954ab5467577565, whose code is 0xef, was called from a contract placed by override: CALL balanceOf answered 32 bytes, STATICCALL balanceOf answered 32 bytes, STATICCALL transfer failed with 0xbeaba5b7, DELEGATECALL failed with 0x0d89438e, and CALL transfer(dead, 0) failed with PolicyForbids 0xa43fec12 because the token's sender policy does not list the caller, on Geth v1.8.1-56d84e62 (bsc-testnet.bnbchain.org) and on the cells reth-bsc answered. The PoolManager reads balanceOf with a high level view call, which compiles to STATICCALL (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96), and pays with CALL (src/types/Currency.sol:73), so neither the caller being a contract nor the frame changes what it sees.

cleared.check: L-917: on the five networks with protocol tokens or system code at reserved addresses, does an eth_call code override at such an address take effect, or does the node keep routing to native code.
cleared.result: It depends on the client and the range, and the answer is now measured. BNB Chain: the override takes effect at every CAS20 address, the singletons, 0x70, 0x1000 and 0x2000 on Geth v1.8.2 (override.go lines 75-82 put DisabledPrecompile in the map, and EVM.precompile then treats the address as an ordinary account, evm.go lines 46-51), and at CAS20 addresses on reth-bsc; reth-bsc keeps the native 0x70 precompile under Jenner and ignores the override there. Base: at the two live B20 tokens and at three unused 0xb200 + 9 zero byte addresses the stub is ignored; with any code present the native B20 code answers balanceOf with 0, while the same unused addresses without code revert. Tempo: the same holds for the 12 byte TIP-20 prefix (pathUSD and two live tokens answer natively, unused addresses revert with Uninitialized without code and answer 0 with code); the fee manager, TIP-403 registry, factory and DEX ignore the override. Arc: the override takes effect at 0x3600..0000, 0x3600..0001, 0x3600..0004 and 0x1800..0005 and 0x1800..0009. HyperEVM: the read precompiles 0x800 to 0x813 ignore the override; 0x2222..22, 0x3333..33, 0x5555..55 and the token system addresses 0x2000..00 and 0x2000..77 take it. On every reth or revm based endpoint (Ethereum, the OP Stack chains, Celo, X Layer, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM) and on avalanchego 1.15.3 an override at an active precompile (0x01, 0x02, 0x04, and 0x100 where active) is ignored, while Geth based bor, BSC and Nitro replace the precompile.

cleared.check: Task 4: on each network, which of 0x01 to 0x1ff, the PoolManager address and the pmdiff addresses are routed to native code, measured by a CALL with empty calldata and 200,000 gas from a contract placed by override (success, return size, gas used including access cost) against the same call on Ethereum.

The pmdiff addresses are ordinary everywhere. Addresses in 0x01 to 0x1ff that answer as something other than a cold empty account: 1: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 10: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 8453: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 130: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 7777777: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 480: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 57073: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 1868: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 42220: 0x1-0x11 0xfd 0x100; 196: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 42161: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x6b-0x74 0xc8 0xff-0x100; 4663: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x6b-0x74 0xff-0x100; 99901: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x6b-0x74 0xff-0x100; 137: 0x1-0x9 0xb-0x11 0x100; 56: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x70 0x100; 43114: 0x1-0xa 0x100; 143: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 4326: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 4217: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 5042: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 999: 0x1-0xa. cleared.check: Whether an ordinary account can make an unused address in a native token range look like a token (B20 and TIP-20 treat any code as an initialized token; CAS20 needs the marker 0xEF), and so open or close a currency that pools could use.
cleared.result: No. Base routes 0xb2 followed by 9 zero bytes (flipping byte 9 or any earlier byte gives an ordinary account, flipping byte 10 or later stays routed), Tempo routes the documented 12 byte prefix 0x20c0 + 10 zero bytes, and CAS20 fixes 10 bytes. Getting code at such an address needs a CREATE or CREATE2 address or a private key with 80 to 96 fixed bits, and the CAS20 marker 0xEF cannot be deployed at all (EIP-3541). Tokens are created only through each network's factory. A pool whose currency is such a token is a pool with an issuer, already covered by F-027, F-031 and F-076.

cleared.check: Lead L-820: reth's parallel executor for blocks with an access list. Does each transaction start with empty transient storage, and is the rebuilt access list checked against the header?
cleared.result: Yes to both. A worker executes each transaction with execute_transaction_without_commit, which detaches the overlay through take_pending_state and calls clear_transaction_state, which clears transient_storage together with the journal, logs and warm sets (evm2 evm/tx.rs lines 240-249, evm/state/mod.rs lines 563-579); a nested transaction gets committed_copy with an empty transient map (lines 135-150). The canonical executor commits worker results in block order and builds the access list from that commit (reth bal/execute.rs lines 157-196), and validation.rs lines 113-131 reject the block when the rebuilt hash differs from the header's. So the unlock flag, deltas and synced currency in src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-26 and src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 cannot cross from one transaction to the next on this path. A builder that ships a false access list only gets its block rejected, which is an operator matter.

Native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so ETH arriving without a call books to no one. Hegota schedules FOCIL, which changes inclusion only, and EIP-8141 frames, which cycle 8 read. Neither fork has a mainnet date.

cleared.check: Monad PR #2667 (v0.16.6), which checks memory bounds once per offset stack element in compiled code. Can a compiled MLOAD or MSTORE skip an expansion it needs?
cleared.result: No. touch_memory serves only accesses of at most 32 bytes (MLOAD, MSTORE, MSTORE8) and skips the check only when the same immutable stack element has already been checked for at least as many bytes. That earlier check runs before it in the same straight-line block, or in a fall-through block that is not a jump destination (emitter.cpp jumpi, lines 3516 to 3536 on main). Memory never shrinks within a frame, and a failed check leaves the frame. The path exists only in v0.16.6 and later, which validators do not run, and simulated calls use the interpreter.

cleared.check: Monad MONAD_NINE memory cap (8 MB per transaction, counted over the current frame and its parents), measured on the live interpreter. Can an ordinary account use it to make a PoolManager call of another user fail, or to make the PoolManager continue after a failed sub-call?
cleared.result: The cap holds at its exact edge: a write ending at byte 8,388,608 succeeds and one ending at 8,388,640 fails as out of gas. Only frames of the same transaction count, so an outside account can reach a victim's PoolManager call only through a hook or token in the victim's pool (pool-creator). Every PoolManager sub-call treats failure as a revert of the whole call: hook calls at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-135, payouts at src/types/Currency.sol:44-80, and the revert wrapper at src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:84-112. No path continues past a frame that the cap stopped. A hook that returns several MB makes its own pool's calls fail through the copy at Hooks.sol:140-149, which is a pool-creator hazard already covered by F-004.

cleared.check: Lead L-933: can a transaction from Monad SYSTEM_SENDER, whose key system_sender.hpp calls known, reach the staking reward, snapshot or epoch change functions?
cleared.result: No such path was found. The three syscalls are dispatched only in ExecuteSystemTransaction::execute_staking_syscall (execute_system_transaction.cpp lines 209 to 233). The staking precompile's dispatch table has no REWARD, SNAPSHOT or ON_EPOCH_CHANGE case and falls back to precompile_fallback. A system transaction must be legacy, addressed to the staking contract, with gas limit and fee 0 (validate_system_transaction.cpp lines 41 to 75), which an ordinary transaction cannot pass because of its intrinsic gas. The system sender cannot appear in an authorization list (validate_monad_transaction.cpp line 53). eth_call from the system sender with REWARD and SNAPSHOT reverts with 'method not supported'. Whether the key itself is published was not found. The address is not the PoolManager or its owner.

cleared.result: Yes. The five function bodies are byte-identical on main (and master, which has the same file) and on tag v0.8.6. The whole evm.rs and opcode.rs are identical on v0.8.5, v0.8.6, b1179556 and release/0.8. On the tag the hook fails a value CALL from or to address(0) (line 534), from or to an account whose slot keccak(account, 2) at 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000001 is nonzero (lines 542-567), and to an account self-destructed earlier in the transaction (lines 571-593); it emits an EIP-7708 Transfer log from 0xff...fe only for a nonzero amount between distinct accounts and only when the frame succeeds (lines 595-604, 860-889). cleared.check: Task 3 of L-944: native take from the real PoolManager at 0x8366a39c...0951 by eth_call with state overrides (a driver at a fresh address calls unlock, runs the items, records success, return data and balances, and reverts), sent in JSON-RPC batches bracketed by web3_clientVersion and arc_getVersion to both Arc endpoints at the same block 33,142,279, and the same scripts to the Ethereum PoolManager 0x000000000004444c...8A90 at block 26,495,018. Recipients: a codeless address, a contract that reverts, a contract that loops until out of gas, an address made blocklisted by a state override of its slot at 0x1800...01 (no public blocklisted address could be listed: getLogs over the precompile's Blocklisted event needs more than the 1,000 block range the official endpoint allows, dRPC allows 100, and the explorer API returned a challenge), address(0), the precompiles 0x01, 0x02, 0x04 and 0x100, the Arc addresses 0x1800...00 to ...03 and the USDC face 0x3600...00, the PoolManager itself, and a contract that self-destructs when called. Amounts 0, 1 and the rest of the balance (2,410,964.98 USDC on Arc). Also settle with value 1, sync(address(0)) with value, settle with value 0 and take with value.
cleared.result: The two Arc endpoints return byte-identical records on all 17 scripts (54 items), so the builds 37812c61 and 8e8edb7a agree on every probed value path. Against Ethereum, success flags, return data and balance changes are equal except where F-125 and F-049 already say: a payout of 1 or of the full balance to address(0) or to the blocklisted address fails on Arc with NativeTransferFailed wrapping Error('Zero address not allowed') or Error('Blocked address') and moves nothing, and every take to 0x1800...00 to ...03 or to 0x3600...00 fails on Arc even with amount 0, because those addresses reject empty calldata, while they are plain accounts on Ethereum. Each failure reverts only the take, so the caller's delta is never debited without a transfer or the reverse (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). The reverting and gas burning recipients give identical wrapped errors on both chains. The precompiles 0x01, 0x02, 0x04 and 0x100 accept value on both, and the full PoolManager balance can be paid to them, which the caller owes and must settle. A take to the PoolManager fails on both, since no contract in src/ outside src/test declares receive or fallback. The self-destructing contract was created before the transaction, so it is not marked destroyed and the take succeeds on both; the destroyed-in-transaction branch of the hook was not reached by these probes. The settle items behave alike on all three: settle credits msg.value, sync and take are not payable.

cleared.check: Do the Arc precompiles that the USDC face calls (NativeCoinAuthority.transfer at 0x1800...00, NativeCoinControl.isBlocklisted at 0x1800...01) behave in mined transactions as the v0.8.6 source says, given that most mined native settlements and payouts on Arc pass through the face 0x3600 as well.
cleared.result: Yes in the mined sample. The replay models transfer(from, to, amount) as: caller must be 0x3600, zero addresses and blocklisted accounts refused, a zero amount moves nothing and logs nothing, otherwise balances move by exactly amount and a Transfer log from 0xff...fe is emitted when from differs from to (native_coin_authority.rs v0.8.6 lines 286-345), and isBlocklisted as a read of slot keccak(account, 2) of 0x1800...01. cleared.check: Assumption T3, ranked first in the blind list: transient slots of the real PoolManager written in one transaction must be empty in the next transaction of the same block. eth_simulateV1 at the real PoolManager address ran, in one simulated block, a driver (state override) that calls unlock and syncs a stub token inside the callback, ending (1) in success with the currency still synced, (2) INVALID inside and at the top, (3) REVERT, (4) a completed unlock followed by INVALID at the top. After each transaction a separate transaction read IS_UNLOCKED, NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT, RESERVES_OF and CURRENCY through exttload(bytes32[]), and the driver read its own transient slot; a second block read them again. Worldchain, Celo and X Layer were run on thirdweb, ankr and drpc endpoints because the networks.json endpoints refused eth_simulateV1 with HTTP 401 and 403.
cleared.result: On all 16 networks the in-transaction read returned the synced stub token, so the write happened, and every later transaction and the next block read 0 in all four PoolManager slots and in the driver slot. An IS_UNLOCKED value of 1 would have let any later caller run take() outside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99,291-297,112). No leak exists on the simulation path of these endpoints. Raw answers with web3_clientVersion before and after are in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json and xtx-alt.json, script research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/scripts/xtx.py.

Constants recomputed in python3: the 19 TickMath multipliers equal floor(2^128 / sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i)) plus 0 or 1, the log constant 255738958999603826347141 equals floor(2^64/log2(sqrt(1.0001))) plus 1, the four transient slot constants equal keccak256(name) minus 1, and getSqrtPriceAtTick(+-887272) returns MAX_SQRT_PRICE and MIN_SQRT_PRICE.

PoolManager has no receive or fallback, so native value enters only through settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307) or through value that bypasses code.

cleared.check: Step 3 comparison of the fifteen highest ranked blind assumptions with OPCODES.md, findings.json and cleared.json.
cleared.result: Twelve of the fifteen were already tested with evidence that exercises the scenario itself (arithmetic, signed opcodes, division by zero, call output buffers, keccak lengths, jump analysis, gas, sender spoofing, empty-code calls, shared transient frames, frame rollback, dual faces). Three were exercised only near the scenario: transient storage across transactions (one generic simulation on Arbitrum), top-level value without a debit (internal calls only) and TSTORE alone in a static frame. cleared.check: Which block producers run a code path other than the public endpoint: external builders behind rollup-boost (op-rbuilder and World Chain's PBH builder).
cleared.result: A builder's block reaches the chain only after the sequencer's own execution client and every follower execute it again; rollup-boost validates the builder payload with engine_newPayload on the local client and falls back to the local block, and the canonical chain is derived from L1 batches that verifiers re-execute. A builder that computed a pool result differently would produce a block that the clients answering these RPCs reject. The validation call in rollup-boost's server.rs discards the returned status and acts only on a transport error (lines 277-281 of the published source), so an invalid builder block surfaces at op-node's own newPayload instead; that is liveness at operator level and moves no funds. The rollup-boost text was read through search highlights of the published pages.

In revm-context 43.0.3, which rc.1 pins, checkpoint_revert drains the journal and reverts every entry with the transient map passed in (src/journal/inner.rs:622-640), and a TransientStorageChange entry restores the old value (revm-context-interface 43.0.2 src/journaled_state/entry.rs:454-468), so a sync recorded at src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 inside a failed phase is rolled back with it.

cleared.check: Base reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd base/v1.5.6: what a failed or halted deposit does to the journal and to transient storage.
cleared.result: The handler is BaseHandler in base-common-evm, its own copy of the OP handler. execution_result turns a halted deposit into the error HaltedDepositPostRegolith before any commit (crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs lines 334-336); run sends every error to catch_error (revm-handler 42.0.1 src/handler.rs lines 100-108). catch_error, for a transaction error of a deposit, calls checkpoint_revert(JournalCheckpoint::default()) (line 368), bumps the nonce and adds the mint, then commit_tx (line 377); any other error goes to discard_tx (line 386). The Cargo.lock at tag v1.5.6 pins revm 42.0.1 and revm-context 42.0.0 from crates.io and reth from base/reth tag base-v2.5.2.11 commit 9e380dd, the commit the endpoint names. In revm-context 42.0.0 checkpoint_revert replays the journal with the transient map (src/journal/inner.rs lines 622-640, and revm-context-interface 42.0.0 entry.rs lines 432-440 put back or remove each TSTORE), commit_tx clears transient_storage (inner.rs lines 141-158), and so do discard_tx (174-192) and finalize (207-250). Every block transaction runs through ExecuteEvm::transact (executor/block_executor.rs line 255, evm.rs line 450), which calls finalize after transact_one even on error. So a failed or halted deposit leaves no transient value, first because its own TSTOREs are replayed away, then because the commit and the finalize clear the map.

MegaHandler::catch_error calls op-revm catch_error and, when that returns an error, discard_tx (lines 1163-1194). op-revm at ethereum-optimism/optimism f67d87cd returns HaltedDepositPostRegolith for a halted deposit (rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs lines 380-385) and for a failed deposit reverts to the default checkpoint (line 417) and calls commit_tx (line 435). The v1.7.4 Cargo.lock pins revm 40.0.3 and revm-context 18.0.3, which clear transient storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize. MegaEvm::discard_tx, the panic recovery path, calls finalize (evm/mod.rs lines 420-436). The block producer is closed, and which mega-evm revision mega-reth v2.3.1 links was not read.

cleared.check: Older op-revm catch_error leaves the journal in place for errors other than a failed deposit (Celo b08a8d0, X Layer a492b62, MegaETH f67d87cd). Does that let transient storage of a failed transaction reach the next one?
cleared.result: No. In these revisions catch_error has no discard_tx branch (for example okx/optimism a492b62 rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs lines 423-484), unlike op-reth v2.8.0, which added discard_and_surface_error for this reason (lines 489-502). Every block path calls ExecuteEvm::transact, which runs finalize after transact_one whether or not it failed (revm-handler 20.0.3 src/api.rs lines 68-77), and finalize clears transient_storage (revm-context 18.0.3 inner.rs line 246). MegaETH adds discard_tx after any failing catch_error (execution.rs lines 1176-1186), and X Layer discards after a failing system call (alloy-op-evm lib.rs lines 416-426). The errors in question also stop the transaction or the block, so no PoolManager code of that transaction completes.

cleared.check: Base v1.5.6: EVM executions outside a user transaction frame (EIP-2935 and EIP-4788 system calls, the L1 attributes deposit, irregular state changes, EIP-8130 phases).
cleared.result: apply_pre_execution_changes runs the EIP-2935 and EIP-4788 system calls (executor/block_executor.rs lines 171-173) through transact_system_call, which is SystemCallEvm::system_call_with_caller (evm.rs lines 452-459): run_system_call ends in BaseHandler::execution_result with commit_tx (handler.rs line 340), and system_call_with_caller then finalizes (revm-handler 42.0.1 src/system_call.rs line 135). The create2 deployer, BaseTime and EIP-8130 account steps write to the database without running code (block_executor.rs lines 179-204). The L1 attributes deposit is an ordinary deposit transaction to the L1Block predeploy, and every Base block read in the scan window also carries a second system deposit at index 1 from 0xdeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddead0001 to the BaseTime predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000030 (eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex on the last block of the window); both run through the same deposit handler as any deposit. The targets are fixed and the caller chooses none of their code. EIP-8130 phased transactions are in the source but inactive on mainnet: everest_timestamp is None in the mainnet config (crates/common/chains/src/config.rs line 479). If activated, the phases of one transaction share its journal, a reverting phase is undone by checkpoint_revert, transient writes included (eip8130.rs lines 1260-1346), and the transaction ends with commit_tx or discard_tx (lines 369 and 1632). base-common-evm2 is not linked into the base binary (no crate of the v1.5.6 lock depends on it).

cleared.check: Celo: CIP-64 fee currency debit and credit calls, the core contract reads, and the system calls. Is transient storage cleared between them and the user transaction, and does the user choose their code?
cleared.result: The debit runs before the user frames, through the non-committing system call inside a checkpoint. On success the checkpoint is committed and the debit's transient storage is cleared before the user transaction runs (crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs lines 635-676, clear at line 668); on rejection checkpoint_revert undoes it (line 678). The credit runs after the user frames, inside build_execution_result (line 876), through core_contracts::call, which runs a committing system call and then clears transient_storage itself (contracts/core_contracts.rs lines 211-248, clear at line 243). Inside that call execution_result calls commit_tx (handler.rs line 1298), which clears the user transaction's transient map too, after the user's last frame has returned. The fee currency's code therefore runs once with the user transaction's transient values present, but transient storage is keyed by address, the PoolManager's lock is already false after a completed unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:113), and the fee currency must be on the governance-held FeeCurrencyDirectory list, so the user picks among listed currencies and chooses none of their code. Core contract reads use call_read_only inside a checkpoint that is reverted (core_contracts.rs lines 142-173). EIP-2935 and EIP-4788 run through OpBlockExecutor as on the other OP chains (alloy-celo-evm block/executor_factory.rs line 114).

cleared.check: X Layer: the blacklist query before user deposits, the gasless allowance query before user transactions, and the system calls.
cleared.result: Both queries are system calls from SYSTEM_ADDRESS to fixed addresses (TxBlacklist proxy and GaslessWhitelist proxy 0x19787404b0c70021b4752028f7e3a92313885B27, rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/xlayer_gasless_contract.rs lines 40-41) through transact_system_call, which commits and finalizes on success and calls discard_tx on error (alloy-op-evm lib.rs lines 410-428). The user supplies arguments (the deposit source hash, or the target and a calldata prefix) and no code. The query runs before the user transaction and its journal is finalized first, so no transient value crosses in either direction. EIP-2935 and EIP-4788 run in apply_pre_execution_changes (block/mod.rs lines 843-845).

cleared.check: MegaETH mega-evm v1.7.4: pre-block system calls, Oracle system transactions, the sequencer registry update, and the KeylessDeploy sandbox.
cleared.result: Pre-block calls (EIP-2935, EIP-4788, the sequencer registry pending changes) use transact_system_call_with_gas_limit, which runs run_system_call and then finalize on success and on error (src/evm/interfaces.rs lines 299-318; block/eips.rs lines 67-80 and 142-155; system/sequencer_registry.rs line 381), and system_call_with_caller also finalizes on both paths (interfaces.rs lines 273-284). Their targets are fixed system contracts. Oracle system transactions come from a fixed signer (cleared in cycle 20). The KeylessDeploy sandbox runs caller-chosen init code in a second EVM with its own journal, so it starts with an empty transient map and its transient values are dropped. It is intercepted only at depth 0 and outside a sandbox (system/intercept.rs line 301 at v1.7.4, unchanged from v1.7.3), so the outer transaction has no PoolManager frame before or after it. This repeats the cycle 4 and 5 clearances at the v1.7.4 tag.

Their system and bridge-delivered transactions were read in earlier cycles: Arbitrum retryables and HyperEVM system transactions give no opening for bracketed payments (OPCODES.md line 324), bor resets transient storage per transaction and per re-execution (line 238), Tempo has no caller that starts a transaction while another runs (line 385), and senders set without a signature were listed for Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM (line 407). cleared.check: What a carried transient slot would do to src/, and whether a failed deposit could leave one.
cleared.result: A failed deposit cannot leave a PoolManager transient value even on a client that skipped the clear at commit: any TSTORE the deposit made is a journal entry, and the revert to the first checkpoint puts the previous value back or removes the key (revm-context-interface 43.0.2 src/journaled_state/entry.rs lines 455-470). The only values that can outlive a successful transaction on a faulty client are the synced currency and reserves, because unlock writes the lock false (src/PoolManager.sol:113) and reverts unless the delta count is 0 (line 112). A carried synced currency would be read by the next transaction's settle as paid = balanceOf - reservesBefore (src/PoolManager.sol:349-361) and could credit one account with another's transfer. All builds read here clear the map at the end of every transaction, so that case does not arise.

cleared.check: Task 3: who can place code at 0xf8c3f4243c4d8c02831a718a7978fd869f094300 on the networks where it is empty, and does that account gain control of the removal callbacks.
cleared.result: Anyone can place code there, and nobody gains control. On Ethereum the address was created at block 21,696,306 by transaction 0x7311a22f...2811 from 0xb7a249bd to the CREATE2 deployer 0x4e59b448 with salt 0x...0492 and 3,272 bytes of init code; keccak256(0xff ++ 0x4e59b448... ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode)) reproduces the address. The deployer has its 69 byte code on Polygon, Avalanche, BNB Smart Chain and World Chain, and the original call carries no signature of its own, so any account can send the same call there and get the same 2,488 byte runtime, because the address commits to the init code. That runtime has no SSTORE, SLOAD or ORIGIN; it keeps the Ethereum PoolManager address 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90 as an immutable, checks CALLER against it (PC 0x37b to 0x3aa), and answers beforeRemoveLiquidity with HookNotImplemented (0x0a85dc29) on Ethereum, Base and OP Mainnet. eth_call of the third-party removals with that runtime placed at the hook address by state override reverts with WrappedError(0xf8c3..., 0x21d0ee70, HookNotImplemented, HookCallFailed) in all 8 runs on Polygon and Avalanche, so the pools stay frozen after a replay. Other code cannot reach the address: a CREATE2 or CREATE output equal to a fixed 160 bit address, or the signing secret of a CREATE2 output, needs about 2^160 work. The address has nonce 0 on all four networks.

cleared.check: Task 3: pools on 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000020 (bit 5) and 0x00000000000000000000000000000000dead0030 (bits 5 and 4) that hold third-party positions, on Robinhood Chain pools 0x4996584f... and 0x7d10f8e6....
cleared.result: No freeze of principal. These flags gate only donate (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:317-335); removal and swaps call no hook (bits 9, 8, 7, 6 unset). Donate to such a pool reverts, which takes nothing from LPs. Nobody can place code at either address: both have nonce 0 and no code on all 21 networks (raw/xchain.json), neither is a precompile or system address on any of them (raw/emptycall.json answers success and empty data), and producing a CREATE or CREATE2 output or a signing secret for a fixed address needs about 2^160 work.

cleared.check: Whether the permissionless deterministic factories that a hook deployed on one network could be replayed through exist on all 21 networks.
cleared.result: Yes. The CREATE2 deployer 0x4e59b44847b379578588920ca78fbf26c0b4956c has its 69 byte code and CreateX 0xba5ed099633d3b313e4d5f7bdc1305d3c28ba5ed its 11,838 byte code on all 21 networks. So a hook address made through 0x4e59b448 or through CreateX CREATE2 on one network can be filled on any other by whoever has the init code, and what that account controls is decided by the init code alone. A CreateX CREATE3 address does not depend on the init code, so when its salt does not carry the deployer in its first 20 bytes (the permissioned deploy protection in the CreateX README) any account can place any code at it on another network. Of the 82 hook addresses in use that are empty on some network, 25 have contract code on another network (raw/xchain.json); only 0xf8c3f424...4300 among them sets bit 9, 8, 5 or 4, and it is cleared above.

cleared.result: Task 1, the rule as cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/census2.py applies it (cycle 18 and 19 census.py scripts are a different test: they replay sync and settle in callTracer frames, they do not balance flows). Inputs per block range: ERC-20 Transfer logs with the PoolManager as topic1 (out) or topic2 (in), counted only when the log has exactly three topics and 32 bytes of data (census2.py:69); WETH style Deposit(dst) logs naming the PoolManager, counted as in (census2.py:73-74); and every PoolManager log: Swap amounts as signed int128, Donate amounts, ModifyLiquidity pool ids, Initialize keys, and ERC-6909 Transfer logs with from = 0 (claims minted) or to = 0 (claims burned) (census2.py:76-91). Per transaction and currency: net = out + minted - in - burned; owed = sum of Swap amount0/amount1 of pools holding the currency, positive when the pool pays, minus Donate amounts (census2.py:106-111). A row is flagged only when net > owed and the transaction holds no ModifyLiquidity log of a pool with that currency (skipped-liquidity) and no pool event on a pool missing from the Initialize list (skipped-unknown-pool) (census2.py:118-123). Hook deltas have no event (src/PoolManager.sol:181, 224) and enter only through the Transfer and claim logs they cause; protocol fee collection has no event (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57) and is recognised afterwards by rule.py from the trace (collectProtocolFees output) or from a fall of protocolFeesAccrued (cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/rule.py:171, 185). Native currency: a native transfer leaves no log, so a native row exists only when a claim of id 0 is minted or burned, or on Arc where 0xff..fe Transfer logs exist; on every other network such rows are counted as native-no-logs and skipped (census2.py:116). What the rule cannot see: (a) every native outflow on 20 of 21 networks; (b) any currency of a pool that has a ModifyLiquidity log in the same transaction, because the event carries liquidityDelta and no amounts (src/PoolManager.sol:175), so an outflow dressed as a liquidity removal or fee collection is never judged; (c) pools absent from the Initialize list; (d) a wrong amount that the PoolManager itself computes and logs: the Swap event is emitted from the same delta that is paid (src/PoolManager.sol:234-251), so an arithmetic fault in Pool.swap, SwapMath, SqrtPriceMath or FullMath that overpays a swapper is booked as owed and never flagged; this census therefore cannot test the opcode and integer library hypotheses of this cycle, which the mined swap replays in OPCODES.md test instead; (e) ERC-6909 transfers between accounts (from and to both nonzero, src/ERC6909.sol:30, 45), so claims moved from a victim and then burned for a take net to zero; (f) balance changes without a standard Transfer log, in either direction (rebases, mints that log only Deposit, tokens with nonstandard events); (g) freezes, which move nothing; (h) the flag is one sided: an inflow larger than owed is not reported.

Across all six trees the whole non-test search returns one shift method call (Base pausable_feature.rs:31), no call of wrapping_from or saturating_from on a Uint, no I256 or Signed integer arithmetic, and Uint shifts only in the storage packing helpers, Base string length decoding and the Tempo order book bitmap. Every other shift is on a primitive u8, u64, u128 or i16 and does not go through ruint. A reading of ruint 1.21.1 src/from.rs:160-225 and 494-512 narrows the conversion fault: TryFrom of a negative primitive returns an error and saturating_from returns zero, which are correct. cleared.check: L-967, Base v1.5.6 B20 precompiles, factory, policy registry and precompile storage under ruint 1.19.0. The sites are packing.rs:87, 114, 142, 144 and 161 (U256 shifted by usize offset*8 or byte_count*8), types/vec.rs:316 (byte_offset*8), types/bytes_like.rs:305 (shift by the constant 1), policy logic v1/v2/v3 (u64 shifts by the constant POLICY_ID_TYPE_SHIFT) and pausable_feature.rs:31 (U256::ONE.checked_shl(feature as u8)).
cleared.result: No faulty input is reachable. Every packing shift is reached only after the check offset + bytes > 32 returns an error (packing.rs:102, 129 and 152), so offset*8 is at most 248, and create_element_mask shifts only when byte_count < 32 (at most 248). vec.rs:316 uses (index % elems_per_slot) * T::BYTES, which is below 32. The 1.19.0 truncation needs an amount of 2^32 or more. checked_shl uses the overflowing_shl flag, which in 1.19.0 (src/bits.rs:394-409) inspects only the carry out of the last limb it moves and ignores limbs dropped whole. U256::ONE has no bits in dropped limbs, and the amount is a u8 enum value, so the flag is correct for every reachable input. B20 balances, supply and allowances use checked_add and checked_sub on U256 (b20_stablecoin/logic/v3.rs:111-115, 138, 322, 332), which the 1.19.0 faults do not touch. balanceOf returns the stored balance without the UI multiplier (b20_asset/logic/v3.rs:940-980, multiplier capped at type(uint128).max). The PoolManager reads these values through balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90) in sync and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-289, 349-364), and no value it reads passes through a faulty ruint path.

cleared.check: L-968, Tempo a9d6748 tip20/mod.rs, tip20/rewards.rs, stablecoin_dex/mod.rs and orderbook.rs, tip_fee_manager/amm.rs and tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs under ruint 1.21.1: Uint shifts and signed to Uint conversions.
cleared.result: ruint 1.21.1 has neither shift fault, so only wrapping_from matters, and no file calls it. tip20, rewards, amm and the channel reserve use only checked U256 arithmetic and unsigned conversions (U256::from of u128 or u64 and try_into to u128, for example rewards.rs:164-171 and 362-373). The order book shifts U256::ONE and U256::MAX by (tick & 0xFF) as usize, which is 0 to 255, or by 255 - bit_index with bit_index below 255 (orderbook.rs:508-509, 588-596, 638-646). Word indices are i16 values shifted as i16 and never reach ruint. The signed tick arithmetic is tick_to_price(tick) = (PRICE_SCALE as i32 + i32::from(tick)) as u32 (orderbook.rs:693-695). Its least value over all of i16 is 100000 - 32768 = 67232, so it is never negative, and base_to_quote and quote_to_base turn it into U256 with U256::from of a u32 (orderbook.rs:119-160). stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:2059 is inside the test module that starts at line 1863 and repeats the same formula. The signed credit deltas at stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:196 and tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs:825 are i128 differences of u64 counters (storage_credits/mod.rs:228-245) cast to u64, without ruint. An eth_call of tickToPrice and priceToTick on the DEX precompile at block 0x307b756 (50,837,334) gave 100000 + tick for all 13 aligned ticks from -32760 to 32760, InvalidTick for unaligned ticks and TickOutOfBounds outside 98000 to 102000 (rpc/tempo-ticktoprice.json).

cleared.check: L-969, every caller of TIP20Token::system_transfer_from and channel_reserve_transfer at a9d6748. The tag tempo/v1.19.1 holds byte-identical copies of tip20/mod.rs, tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs, stablecoin_dex/mod.rs and tip_fee_manager/amm.rs. It schedules T14 for mainnet at 1,796,742,000 and leaves T15 unscheduled for mainnet (crates/hardfork/src/constants.rs:254, hardfork lib.rs:438-440). Probes for later tags (tempo/v1.19.2, v1.20.0, v1.20.1, v1.21.0, v2.0.0) returned 404. The latest block read was 50,837,521 at timestamp 1,795,657,040, so T14 is not active yet.
cleared.result: No caller lets an ordinary account move the PoolManager's TIP-20 balance. The StablecoinDEX pulls from sender in decrement_balance_or_transfer_from (stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:299-305, 325-351), and every caller passes the dispatcher's msg_sender (swap_exact_amount_in:428, swap_exact_amount_out:494, place:697, place_flip:869; dispatch.rs:25-66). TipFeeAMM rebalance_swap and mint pull from msg_sender (amm.rs:239, 360; dispatch.rs:56-68). The fee path uses transfer_fee_pre_tx from the transaction's fee payer (tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:158-177), which must sign. In the channel reserve the payer is always msg_sender at open (mod.rs:168-247), and top_up, request_close and withdraw require msg_sender == descriptor.payer (mod.rs:380, 481, 623). Pulls come only from msg_sender, at mod.rs:232-243 and 422-438. settle and close move only reserve custody. They require the payee or operator (mod.rs:854-864), and they need a voucher from the payer or the authorized signer for any amount above what is already settled. The PoolManager can be a payer only by calling the reserve itself. Its code calls only currency contracts and hooks (src/types/Currency.sol:40-90, src/libraries/Hooks.sol). eth_call from the PoolManager address to the reserve 0x4D50500000000000000000000000000000000000 with the transfer, balanceOf and withdraw(uint256) selectors reverted with the unknown selector error 0xaa4bc69a (rpc/tempo-reserve-selectors.txt), so a pool that uses the reserve address as a currency cannot make the PoolManager open, fund or capture a channel. receive_policy_sender differs from the account whose balance moves only when the reserve pays out. For a payee it is the descriptor payer when the channel was opened at T12 or later, and the reserve itself otherwise. For a refund it is the reserve (mod.rs:94-100, 324-329, 553-565, 642-647). In both cases only reserve custody that the payer deposited moves. A channel whose payee is the PoolManager only donates the payer's own tokens to it.

cleared.check: Task 3 (L-960, L-976): Arbitrum retryable redeems at Nitro consensus-v61 and its go-ethereum fork. Is the callvalue of a scheduled redeem taken from the ticket escrow in state, and is transient storage empty when the redeem starts?
cleared.result: Yes to both. ArbitrumRetryTx in StartTxHook moves tx.Value from the escrow address to tx.From with util.TransferBalance, which fails with ErrInsufficientBalance when the escrow holds less (arbos/tx_processor.go lines 472-477; arbos/util/transfer.go lines 67-76), and tx.Value is the retryable callvalue stored at submission (arbos/retryables/retryable.go lines 366-381). At submission the callvalue is moved from the sender to the escrow with the same checked transfer (tx_processor.go line 320). The EVM call then checks CanTransfer for tx.From and debits it (fork core/state_transition.go line 725, core/vm/evm.go Call, core/evm.go lines 139-147). Each redeem, scheduled or made by ArbRetryableTx.redeem, runs as its own ApplyTransaction in the block loop (arbos/block_processor.go lines 373-375, 483, 612), and every transaction goes through StateDB.Prepare, which replaces transient storage before execution (fork core/state_transition.go line 737, core/state/statedb.go lines 1598-1599). A plain ArbitrumDepositTx mints and moves value without running any code (tx_processor.go lines 225-233), so it can only raise the PoolManager balance, which native settle does not read (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). The fork was read at f3a966e, the pin of v3.11.3; the pin of consensus-v61 could not be confirmed without the GitHub API, and the same lines are identical on the fork master branch.

cleared.check: Task 3 (L-960): OP Stack deposits with a mint field. Is the CALLVALUE of a deposit debited from the sender after the mint?
cleared.result: Yes. op-geth adds the mint to msg.From before execution (core/state_transition.go lines 474-480) and then applies the ordinary CanTransfer check and EVM transfer of msg.value from msg.From (lines 574-579). op-revm at op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4 adds the mint to the caller balance and subtracts the balance spending, and only raises the balance to the value when the configuration disables the balance check (rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs lines 137-151), a switch used by eth_call, not by block execution. The minted ETH was locked in the portal on L1 by the depositor, so the PoolManager is credited with value that its caller paid. The handler builds of Base, Zora, World Chain, Celo, X Layer and MegaETH were not read here; the op-stack-eth unit of this cycle covers failed deposits.

Each system transaction is its own transact with a fresh journal, so transient storage starts empty. The closed validator itself was not read; its receipts are checked against this execution by the archive clients (run.rs line 236). cleared.result: No. A system transaction (legacy, signature (0,0)) is the only envelope that recovers to zero (envelope.rs 29, 379-384), and the block executor accepts it only with target address zero (cycle 20, block.rs 617-660). Primitive secp256k1, P256 and WebAuthn signatures derive the address from a public key, which needs a keccak preimage of a zero address. A keychain signature returns its claimed user_address after checking only the inner signature (tt_signature.rs 951-976); prepare_keychain then requires user_address to equal the signer (handler.rs 670-676) and either loads an active key of that account from the keychain precompile (validate_keychain_authorization, account_keychain/mod.rs 1309-1333, handler.rs 717-744) or, for a key authorized in the same transaction, requires the authorization to be signed by the account itself (handler.rs 566-573 before T6) or by an admin key the keychain already holds for it (handler.rs 776-792). A full-history scan of the keychain precompile at 0xAAAAAAAA00..00 found 14616 KeyAuthorized and 17 AdminKeyAuthorized logs and none for account zero, and the precompile's own authorizeKey requires msg.sender to be tx.origin. A configurable account signature with account zero is refused when it is decoded (ZeroAccount, primitives configurable_account/mod.rs 332-335, 477-490), and an unregistered account must equal the address derived from its configuration (384-414). So address zero, Tempo's protocolFeeController, cannot call setProtocolFee or collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35, 47).

cleared.result: The value frame hook loads the target inside a checkpoint and, when it is marked self-destructed, returns a metered revert with ERR_SELFDESTRUCTED_BALANCE_INCREASED before any value moves (evm.rs 569-593). cleared.check: Tempo v1.19.1-a9d6748 (the build rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz reported on 2026-11-26): fee charge and refund arithmetic, integer types and casts, and whether a signed, wrapped or truncated value can reach a TIP-20 balance write.
cleared.result: The upfront fee is calc_gas_balance_spending(gas_limit, gas_price) = U256(gas_limit u64) saturating_mul U256(gas_price u128), div_ceil 10^12 (primitives transaction/mod.rs:61-65); the gas price is converted with u128::try_from and fails the block on overflow (handler/config.rs:257-258), the base fee with u64::try_from (config.rs:319-320). settle_transaction computes actual_spending the same way from tx_gas_used and takes refund = collected.checked_sub(actual_spending), a fatal error otherwise (config.rs:269-273). The TIP-20 side uses U256 with checked decrement_balance and checked opted-in supply updates (tip20/mod.rs:1525-1552, 1558-1594), and the fee manager refunds from its own custody of that transaction's prepayment (tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:234-273). The one signed value is the i64 refund counter. Tempo maps a negative counter to i64::MAX on purpose (config.rs:260-264) and evm2's final_refund caps it at spent / MaxRefundQuotient (evm2 interpreter/host.rs:70-83). From T7 (timestamp 1,783,605,600, 9 July 2026, constants.rs:233) the quotient is 1 and SstoreClearingSlotRefund is 0 (hardfork gas_params.rs:71-73, 120-132). sstore_refund only goes negative by subtracting the clearing refund (evm2 version/gas_params.rs:344-379), which is now 0; storage-credit refunds are non-negative u64 counts times STORAGE_CREDIT_VALUE with saturating_mul (config.rs:444-487); batch refunds are summed with saturating_add (handler.rs:1306, 1357, 1371); EIP-7702 auth refunds are 0 from T1 (gas_params.rs:109-110). So the counter cannot end negative today, and if it did the result would still be a refund bounded by the payer's own prepayment. No wrapped value reaches a balance write.

cleared.check: Tempo: which accounts pay and receive fees and refunds, and whether an ordinary account can make the PoolManager (0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029) the fee payer or make the fee flow touch a TIP-20 balance the PoolManager holds.

The cycle 23 stablecoin-l1 unit showed that no envelope recovers to an address without a key, and the PoolManager has no key. Both fee moves run outside the call frames: the debit before the first call and the refund after the last (handler.rs:1581-1588 and 1717-1731), so no balanceOf(PoolManager) read between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) can see them. cleared.check: Celo (forno.celo.org reports reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, read as celo-reth v1.0.10 in cycle 22): CIP-64 debit and credit amounts, types and casts, and whether the F-144 wrapped refund can reach a fee-currency balance write in a way that moves funds other than the sender's own prepayment.
cleared.result: The debit is gas_limit as u128 checked_mul effective_gas_price, converted to U256 (handler.rs:543-545). The credit runs after the refund step (handler.rs:864-876; refund at 1213-1215), so refunded() is already the capped value: revm's set_final_refund returns min(refunded as u64, gas_used / 5) as i64, which is non-negative. refund_in_erc20 = price saturating_mul (remaining + refunded as u64) as u128, tip and base charge use spent_sub_refunded (handler.rs:327-343). The three parts add up to price times gas_limit, which is what the debit took, so the wrapped refund only moves value between the sender and the fee recipients. The credit pays caller, block beneficiary (or the fee handler when it is zero) and the fee handler (handler.rs:296-304, 354-364). None is the PoolManager unless the sequencer names it as beneficiary, which is an operator action, and the credit runs after execution.

cleared.check: Celo mined evidence for the F-144 shape: CIP-64 transactions whose main call transfers the fee token back to the sender, and whether the debit had cleared the sender's slot first.

In a seeded sample of 40 (seed 23023), the sender's balance at the previous block never equalled the debit, so the debit did not clear the slot and the counter could not go negative. No mined example of the wrapped refund was found. forno refuses debug_traceTransaction ('rpc method is not whitelisted'), so the gas used before refunds, and with it the refund applied, cannot be read from that endpoint. cleared.check: X Layer (reth/v2.3.0-f60420a xlayer/v0.0.7): post_exec_settlement_deltas and gasless transactions, amounts, types and recipients.

The submodule pin of the running build could not be confirmed, because the GitHub API is not available. The post-exec refund is a u64 from the sequencer's payload or the producer's inspector. It is rejected when it exceeds evm_gas_used (block/mod.rs:566-599, 1003-1016). Deltas are U256 saturating_mul of the gas delta by base fee, priority price and effective price (block/mod.rs:702-752). The sender gains with saturating_add, and beneficiary, BASE_FEE_RECIPIENT and the operator vault lose with checked_sub, an underflow failing the block (block/mod.rs:645-679, 754-780). The code comment limits it to forks after Karst. Gasless status comes from a view call to the fixed contract 0x19787404b0c70021b4752028f7e3a92313885B27 returning (bool, uint64); malformed output decodes to not gasless (xlayer_gasless_contract.rs:47-48, 124-165). A gasless transaction only has its price set to zero, so no fee moves. The sender is the transaction signer, and every adjustment is applied after the transaction has run. No PoolManager balance or msg.value is involved.

cleared.check: Base v1.5.6 (endpoint build) and v1.6.0-rc.1: fee charge, refund and reimbursement, including the EIP-8130 phase loop and payer settlement.
cleared.result: v1.5.6 uses revm's post_execution::refund unchanged and pays fees only to the L1, base and operator fee vaults and the beneficiary, with a U256 base fee amount from basefee as u128 saturating_mul gas used (handler.rs:242-320). No pre-execution storage write exists on Base, so the counter cannot end negative there. EIP-8130 settlement clamps a negative counter to zero before the 1/5 cap: u64::try_from(signed_refund.max(0)) (v1.5.6 eip8130.rs:1716-1718; v1.6.0-rc.1 eip8130.rs:1917-1919). The fee, base amount and priority amount use checked_mul and checked_sub, and the payer refund uses prepay.checked_sub(total_cost) and a checked balance add (v1.6.0-rc.1 eip8130.rs:1841-1909). The payer is the sender or the account a payer_auth signature recovers to (eip8130.rs:945). v1.6.0-rc.1 adds gas-limit billing, which spends all gas and sets the refund to 0 (handler.rs:265-313). EIP-8130 is gated on Everest, which has no date (OPCODES.md).

cleared.check: Monad 0.16.7: charge on gas limit, the refund counter and the reserve balance rule.
cleared.result: execute_final asserts gas_refund >= 0 and gas_left <= gas_limit (execute_transaction.cpp:376-378). With charges_gas_limit, compute_gas_refund returns 0, so the counter is never cast or used (monad_transaction_gas.cpp:22-31) and the sender is billed gas_limit times price. The reward is a uint256 product sent to the beneficiary or the staking contract (execute_transaction.cpp:381-411). dipped_into_reserve skips every account whose code is not an EIP-7702 delegation (reserve_balance.cpp:86-96), so the PoolManager is exempt. cleared.check: Whether any of these fee paths changes a value the PoolManager reads inside a call: msg.value, a balance read between sync and settle, or gas forwarded to a hook or a token.
cleared.result: All fee debits run before the first call frame and all refunds and credits run after the last. msg.value is the signed transaction value or a call value, and no handler read changes it. Tempo AA batches carry no value. The PoolManager reads balances only inside its own frames (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), so a fee move cannot fall between its sync and settle. Inside the main call, Celo and Tempo price SSTOREs on slots the debit wrote as already written, so gas readings differ from Ethereum. The PoolManager forwards all remaining gas and never branches on a gas value (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, and no gasleft() outside src/test), so no line of src/ computes or decides differently.

cleared.check: Task 1 to 4 on Ethereum: every mined PoolManager transaction of the window re-run through a model of src/ from its prestate and compared word by word with what the chain returned, logged and stored. scripts/model.py rewrites every PoolManager entry point from the text of src/ (PoolManager.sol:103-377, ProtocolFees.sol, ERC6909.sol, ERC6909Claims.sol, Extsload.sol, Exttload.sol, Pool.sol:100-612, Position.sol, TickBitmap.sol, Hooks.sol:131-320) with the pool math of tools/opdiff/v4math.py, and walks the mined call trace frame by frame. It starts persistent storage from the transaction's own prestate (prestateTracer), so tick bitmap words, liquidityNet and fee growth outside are the values at the transaction's position in its block, and starts transient storage empty. It takes from the trace only what the source takes from outside: calldata, msg.sender, msg.value, hook return data and token balanceOf return data. For every PoolManager frame it compares the frame output (swap and modifyLiquidity deltas, feesAccrued, settle amount, unlock result, every extsload and exttload word), every PoolManager log word (Swap, ModifyLiquidity, Donate, Initialize, ERC-6909 Transfer and others), and the deltas the PoolManager wrote into the calldata of afterSwap and afterAdd or afterRemoveLiquidity hooks. At the end it compares every PoolManager storage word in the prestateTracer diff (slot0, liquidity, both fee growth globals, tick words, bitmap words, positions, protocolFeesAccrued, ERC-6909 balances, allowances, operators) and flags any word it wrote that the chain did not, and any word the chain wrote that it did not. A model read of a word that is not in the prestate is also flagged.

cleared.result: Trace requests re-execute from the parent block with the RPC VM, declared as vm::VM vm_{vm::VM::InterpreterOnly} (category/rpc/monad_executor.cpp:1306-1309, used at 1821-1824). Block execution builds vm::VM vm{trace_calls ? InterpreterOnly : Dual} (cmd/monad/main.cpp:485-488), so validators that do not record call traces run compiled native code. Every node asserts that the delayed execution results carried in each consensus header hash to the block headers it computed itself (category/execution/runloop/runloop_monad.cpp:125-155, MONAD_ASSERT at 680-681). So the 20,000 transactions checked against the source above were run by the interpreter, and the committed state they match (1,500 blocks, scripts/committed.py) is accepted by the node only while its own results equal what the validator quorum executed. Whether rpc.monad.xyz itself runs with trace_calls was not confirmed.

cleared.check: The SAE executor of avalanchego 1.15.3 read for transaction boundaries and the EVM it runs.
cleared.result: Execute (saexec/execution.go:293-470) sets the transaction context and runs core.ApplyTransaction once per transaction on one StateDB. ApplyTransaction prepares and finalises state per transaction, which clears transient storage. The interpreter is libevm with vm.Config{}, the same one eth_call uses. cleared.check: Whether a public account can cause a reorganisation or profit from one against a PoolManager user, including replay of a settled or taken transaction in another order (lead L-1046).
cleared.result: A reorganisation needs block producers on all three networks: bor producers and Heimdall milestones, BSC validators with BEP-126 votes, Avalanche validators under Snowman. A re-included transaction keeps its signature and nonce and runs once. Its unlock is atomic (PoolManager.sol:104-114), so a take without a matching settle reverts whatever the order. A different order can change the price a swap gets, which is the ordinary ordering risk that slippage limits in routers handle. Only the owner or fee controller can change the protocol fee, and only a pool's own hook can change its dynamic fee, so a replay cannot pay more than the pool's state at that position gives.

cleared.check: Lead L-1047: what an ordinary account can undo or reorder around another account's PoolManager transaction, using the entry points that need no unlock.
cleared.result: Ordering cannot move a credit. sync writes only transient slots of the current transaction (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:23-30, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), which EIP-1153 clears at the end of the transaction, so a sync in an inserted transaction is gone before the victim's starts. settle compares the balance with what the victim's own sync recorded inside its own transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so tokens sent to the PoolManager by another transaction before that sync are part of the recorded reserves and are credited to no one. ERC-6909 transfer and transferFrom move only the caller's claims or allowances given to it (src/ERC6909.sol:25-45). extsload and exttload are views. initialize only succeeds on a pool with no price (src/libraries/Pool.sol:101), so a front-run can choose the starting price of a pool nobody has created; modifyLiquidity takes no price bound (src/types/PoolOperation.sol:8-16), so a direct caller without a slippage check of its own would add at that price. That is the same on every network and is the job of the caller's router. Inside one block, a builder or searcher can sandwich swaps, which the swapper bounds with sqrtPriceLimitX96. Reorgs on mainnet are one block deep in the 2025 data (about 0.11 percent of slots) and blocks finalize about 18 minutes behind the head; a reorg drops or reorders whole transactions and cannot split one settlement.

cleared.check: Lagoon post-execution transaction and Sequencer-Defined Metering: can the refund settlement change the PoolManager's balance or what a frame sees between sync and settle.
cleared.result: No. The 0x7D transaction is not executed as EVM code; each refund credits tx.from and debits the block beneficiary and fee vaults after the refunded transaction's frame ends and before commit. The PoolManager is never tx.from or a fee recipient, and src/PoolManager.sol:349-364 reads balances only inside frames.

cleared.check: Lagoon interop: can a relayed message make the PoolManager act for someone else, and can a forced-inclusion deposit execute a message or see transient storage of a sequenced transaction.
cleared.result: L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.relayMessage calls any target except two messengers with msg.sender equal to the messenger, so a message to the PoolManager can only call unlock, which calls unlockCallback on the messenger and reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:104-110), or functions that need no lock and act on the messenger's own claims. CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage reverts for deposits. Deposits run first in a block, each in its own transaction, and op-revm clears transient storage at commit.

cleared.check: Native and token calls from the PoolManager to the Lagoon predeploys in the op-contracts v10.0.0 sources (leads L-417 and L-892): P1 native take with empty calldata, P2 transfer, P3 balanceOf.
cleared.result: None of the ten predeploy sources has a receive or fallback function or a transfer or balanceOf selector, so P1 reverts at the proxy's delegate call, and P2 and P3 revert; no payout is stranded and no balance can be synced. ETH that SuperchainETHBridge relays to the PoolManager arrives by SafeSend self-destruct, and native settle credits only msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), so it becomes an unclaimable surplus that no account can take.

cleared.check: Lead L-1048: which blocks can be reorganised after public RPC served them, and can an ordinary account trigger it, for example with a forced-inclusion deposit.
cleared.result: Only blocks between the safe and unsafe head (13 seconds on Base to 3,302 seconds on Zora at the time of the query), and only through sequencer equivocation, a batch missing the sequencing window or an L1 reorg. A deposit is placed by derivation at the start of an L2 block whose L1 origin includes it and does not invalidate earlier sequenced blocks; after Lagoon deposits cannot execute interop messages. In the one halt of the year found (Base, June 2026), validators never accepted the bad block, so nothing served was removed.

cleared.check: Task 2 (L-1035): the 3,135 caught PoolManager frames in the 20,000 MegaETH transactions of cycle 23, grouped by revert data and by the frame where the revert started, and replayed through the source model; then whether a mega-evm v1.7.4 resource limit (compute gas, data size, KV updates, state growth) can stop a frame after take has paid out and before settle while the outer transaction succeeds.
cleared.result: All 3,135 are unlock frames. 3,091 carry a revert that started in the caller's own unlockCallback after the PoolManager calls inside it returned: 2,997 frames with selector 0x17080d7e from 0x00000000c070d95ed0f9c86de3b51e740c263ef8, 86 with 0xecbd9804 from 0x94bdc671f0c35f44a1daa53143fd1f868d1623b9 and 8 with 0xbbd6b10b from 0x16b424408f3a12dcbe2045b07a9cd2b9f52038db, each one word holding the swap delta the callback just received, the quote-by-revert pattern. unlock carries them unchanged (src/PoolManager.sol:110). The other 44 are AlreadyUnlocked from nested unlock calls by 0xb18bcb4cf0690202d022bd3b4b86d5cfecf05489, 0x3aaf3c5befcde71962b138e5cd767c547c55137b and 0xb6df2bb754417fd3b726061633e43fa61b8a3edf, which the model raises from the replayed state (src/PoolManager.sol:105). The rate is one searcher contract on one network. MegaLimitExceeded(uint8,uint64) has selector 0x84b90267 and appears in none of the 521,190 frames of the 20,281 stored MegaETH transactions, and every one of the 12,133 failed frames has the error string execution reverted. In mega-evm v1.7.4 a frame-local exceed found during execution returns Revert (limit/limit.rs:152-161) and revm reverts that frame's journal, and a transaction-level exceed halts every frame and the transaction (limit.rs:31-41, 852-860). take and settle are separate frames inside the callback, and the PoolManager only returns from unlock when NonzeroDeltaCount is 0 (src/PoolManager.sol:112). A stopped take frame takes its transfer and its delta back with it. A stopped callback makes unlock revert. The one case the source comments name, a frame that already committed and is reported as Revert (limit.rs:833-837), leaves the PoolManager books consistent, because a committed take frame recorded its debit (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and every PoolManager child failure makes the PoolManager revert its own frame (Hooks.sol:137, Currency.sol:51-53, 82-86, 94). Cycle 10 reached the same reading on v1.7.3. No limit stops a frame between take and settle while the outer transaction succeeds with other users' funds moved.

cleared.result: The official endpoint answers like the revm and reth family on every probe where the families differ. On the eight error probes it returns the reth texts and code -32003 ('EVM error: StackUnderflow', 'EVM error: InvalidJump', 'out of gas: gas required exceeds: 100000', 'EVM error: InvalidFEOpcode', 'EVM error: OpcodeNotFound'), the same strings as f0cad31 and reth v2.11.0, where both geth builds say 'stack underflow (0 <=> 2)', 'invalid jump destination', 'out of gas' and 'invalid opcode: INVALID' with code -32000. It equals f0cad31 on all 30 probes that do not depend on the moment of the call, including eth_estimateGas results that no Ethereum client gives (0x536a, 0x535e and 0x1185a, where reth v2.11.0 says 0x5448, 0x542a, 0x11670 and geth 0x5448, 0x542a, 0x116f5), the same rejection text for an override with both state and stateDiff, and ECRECOVER priced at 15,000 gas (gas difference 0x3b19 against 0xc39 on Ethereum), which is nanoreth's HlSpecId::V2 multiplied precompile price. Opcode results, cold and warm access gas (0xef036, 0xee7fb, 0xee790, 0xedd50, 0xed321 everywhere), failed precompiles that consume all forwarded gas, and the absence of Prague and Osaka precompiles 0x0b and 0x100 also agree. The nine probes that differ all describe the call context: the official endpoint runs eth_call in a block numbered latest plus one with the parent's timestamp and hash chain (BLOCKHASH(NUMBER-1) equals the hash of the latest block on both endpoints), a gas limit of 30,000,000, ignores the block argument (an old number, a block hash, 'pending' and a nonexistent hash all give the latest-plus-one context), and returns a live HyperCore oracle value from 0x807 (0x93fda) where f0cad31 forwards an unrecorded call and returns 0x93fe4 and b92ad36 halts out of gas. So official eth_call runs revm, behind reth's RPC types, inside a process that holds live HyperCore state. The node README states that the same hl-node binary runs run-validator and run-non-validator and that --serve-eth-rpc serves this RPC; whether the RPC path calls the same execution code that builds blocks cannot be seen from outside, and the hl-node binary itself was not obtainable (binaries.hyperliquid.xyz/Mainnet/hl-node answered HTTP 403). None of the context differences reaches src/: the PoolManager reads no NUMBER, TIMESTAMP, BLOCKHASH, BASEFEE, PREVRANDAO or GASPRICE and calls no precompile; its only gas reads are the forwarded gas of three calls.

cleared.check: Whether the 512-bit paths of the Position fee copy of mulDiv (Position.sol:94-96), the amount > uint160 copy (SqrtPriceMath.sol:97) and mulDivRoundingUp at SqrtPriceMath.sol:105, which no producer has executed, can decide a balance.
cleared.result: They cannot. The Position copy takes prod1 != 0 only when the fee owed is at least 2^128, and Pool.sol:192 then reverts in toInt128 (SafeCast.sol:56-58). The two SqrtPriceMath sites need an amount above 2^160 in a step that exhausts the remaining amount (SwapMath.sol:75-82 and 94-98), so params.amountSpecified - amountSpecifiedRemaining equals amountSpecified and Pool.sol:455 or :459 reverts in toInt128 (SafeCast.sol:40-43). Their results are therefore only ever computed in transactions that revert. The exact-input fee copy (SwapMath.sol:65) takes the 512-bit path only for |amountRemaining| near 2^236 or more; its result is only compared with amountIn, and any value below amountIn leads to the same revert at Pool.sol:455 or :459.

Run alone from the parent block it reads one PoolManager word with extsload (selector 0x1e2eaeaf) and returns after 765 steps without a swap, while on chain it swapped; the earlier transaction at index 1 of the block is an ERC-4337 bundle that emits PoolManager logs, so the pool state it read differs. Run after the six earlier transactions of the block, the earlier transaction 0xfafea290... (a call to 0x1b99198e... with selector 0xbeefbeef, reverted on chain) succeeds in the reference, so the block state diverges before the target, and the target again reads one word and returns. Why the reference takes the other path in the earlier searcher call was not confirmed; gas, which the reference does not model, is the likely input. The only PoolManager frame the reference ran is that read, so this record says nothing against the PoolManager; it is left unexplained in the sense that the earlier transaction was not reproduced.

cleared.check: Task 4: at the real PoolManager address of each network, one eth_call (no transaction) runs a probe through unlock. Inside the callback the probe calls mint(Q, 0x1234, 5), sync on a stub token that reports a balance of 0x77, then exttload and extsload of the same 20 indexes, then burn(Q, 0x1234, 5), so the unlock settles. A stateDiff override first writes a distinct marker into the persistent slot of every index except the ERC-6909 balance of Q and slots 0 and 6. The indexes are the five transient slots the PoolManager writes (IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT, NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT, CURRENCY_SLOT, RESERVES_OF_SLOT, the delta slot keccak(Q, 0x1234)), the balance slot balanceOf[Q][0x1234], a pool state slot keccak(id, 6) and its +6 word, slots 0 and 6, and each of these with bit 248 flipped. Can a persistent and a transient slot with one index share an entry, and does any network fold a pair of these real PoolManager keys?
cleared.result: No transient fold and no persistent fold outside Avalanche. On 20 networks every read equals the Ethereum answer: exttload returns 1, 1, the stub token, 0x77 and -5 for the five transient slots and zero for their bit 248 partners, while extsload of the same indexes returns the persistent markers, and extsload of the balance slot returns 5 from the mint inside the same call. So a TSTORE at an index leaves the persistent slot of that index untouched and the reverse, on every network, including during an unlock. On Avalanche the transient reads are also exact, and every persistent pair reads one shared value, which is the F-040 rule acting on real PoolManager keys: the two overrides of a pair land on one entry, the override of slot 0 with bit 248 set replaced the owner word, and the mint of 5 to balanceOf[Q][0x1234] (whose index has bit 248 set) was added to the marker written for the partner index with bit 248 clear. The persistent and transient key spaces stay separate there too. The client version was read before and after each call; the build strings are in the output file. The source lines this rests on are src/libraries/Lock.sol:8-26, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:8-32, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:13-36, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:11-39, src/Extsload.sol:10-15 and src/Exttload.sol:10-15.

cleared.check: Task 1 for reth v2.11.0, the build the Ethereum endpoint reports (reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc), which runs on evm2 at rev 66687c18. How is (address, slot) keyed in the EVM state, the transient map, the execution cache, the txpool prewarm snapshot and the reuse of speculative results?
cleared.result: Every map is keyed by the full address and the full 256 bit slot. evm2's StorageKey is a 52 byte repr(C) struct of the address and the slot, and equality compares all 52 bytes (crates/evm2/src/storage_key.rs lines 12-56). Transient storage is a separate map of that key (crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs lines 58-59, 799-812) and persistent slots sit in per-account maps keyed by the slot word (lines 653-690). The execution cache keys storage by (Address, StorageKey) in fixed-cache 0.1.10 (cached_state.rs lines 967-968, 1063-1100); the crate's get compares the full key with key.equivalent and treats any other occupant of the bucket as a miss, and a colliding insert replaces the entry (fixed-cache lib.rs lines 316-350, 386-440; crate checksum 2fe63500 matches the lock file). The txpool snapshot looks up the full address and U256::from_be_bytes of the full slot, per parent hash (txpool.rs lines 13-38). The reuse of speculative results commits a prewarm result only when every recorded (address, slot) read still equals the current value and every account read matches, with balance differences allowed only where the transaction did not observe the balance and both balances are nonzero (reuse.rs lines 284-342, 367-401). No key is truncated, hashed down or reused across transactions.

cleared.check: Task 1 for bor v2.11.1 (the endpoint reports bor/ebcfea01452d/v2.11.1-private): the BlockSTM multi-version key, the per-incarnation committed-state cache and transient storage of the V2 parallel state.
cleared.result: The multi-version key is 54 bytes: the full 20 byte address, the full 32 byte slot, a subpath byte and a type byte that separates account, state and subpath entries (core/blockstm/mvhashmap.go lines 90-150). ParallelStateDB keeps local writes in map[common.Address]map[common.Hash]common.Hash (core/state/parallel_statedb.go line 96, SetState lines 1040-1060) and its committed-state cache in a map keyed by stateKey{addr, slot} (lines 168, 1008-1032). Transient storage is a separate map that Prepare replaces for every transaction (lines 1137-1150, 1277-1279). The keccak result caches were cleared in cycles 8, 11 and 16 as keyed by the full input. bor v2.11.1 has no MULMOD memo: opMulmod calls uint256 MulMod directly (core/vm/instructions.go lines 200-204).
