cleared.check: Task 1 for avalanchego 1.15.3 (commit 983815fd, libevm d398bc4dbe41): is there a second key rule next to the bit 248 fold of F-040, and does any rule cross accounts or reach transient storage?
cleared.result: There is one rule. libevm's StateDBHooks interface has a single method, TransformStateKey (core/state/statedb.libevm.go lines 41-53), applied in GetState, GetCommittedState and SetState (core/state/statedb.go lines 349, 359, 422). The C-Chain hook clears bit 0 of byte 0 and ignores the address (vms/saevm/cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go, partitionStateKeysHook). The only other variant is the skip option, used for asset balances and for GetCommittedState before Apricot Phase 1, which is history. The rule maps a key of an account into the same account, so a write by one contract cannot reach the PoolManager's storage. Firewood was not read; the transform sits above the state store, so a store behind it receives keys that are already folded.

cleared.check: Task 3 for the Avalanche fold: can an ordinary account make a PoolManager write land on, or a PoolManager read return, another user's entry?
cleared.result: No. The PoolManager writes only fixed slots 0 to 6 (src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:11 and the declarations in src/ProtocolFees.sol, src/ERC6909.sol, src/PoolManager.sol), keccak256 outputs of mapping keys (src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:66-73, src/ERC6909.sol balance and allowance mappings, src/libraries/Position.sol:34-62) and such outputs plus an offset of at most 6 (src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:324-347). Under the fold two of these collide only if they agree in 255 bits. An account that picks pool ids, owners, ticks and salts to aim one of its own slots at one fixed victim slot needs about 2^255 tries; two slots it controls both are useless to it. A fixed slot S with bit 248 set is 2^248 + S, and a keccak output equal to it is a preimage search of the same size. Adding an offset of at most 6 changes bit 248 only if the lower 248 bits of the hash are within 6 of 2^248, which has probability about 2^-245. No PoolManager function writes a caller-chosen index; extsload and exttload only read (src/Extsload.sol:10-15, src/Exttload.sol:10-15). The live test shows half of the keccak slots used (the balance slot 0x8f57 for instance) already live at their folded index on chain, which is harmless because every access to them goes through the same rule.

cleared.check: Task 1 for Monad v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 (the endpoint reports Monad/0.16.7): TrieDb key encoding, the page encoding of storage, the account and storage cache, and the per-transaction state of parallel execution.
cleared.result: No two (address, slot) pairs share an entry. With the monad state machine the TrieDb is page encoded: the trie path is keccak(address) then keccak(page key), the page key is the slot shifted right by 7 and the offset in the page is the low 7 bits (category/execution/monad/db/storage_page.hpp lines 41-44, 173-191; trie_db.cpp lines 87, 134-194; db.hpp lines 84-87). Page key and offset together give back the whole slot (compute_slot_key), so the split is one to one. The storage cache key is the 20 byte address, the incarnation and the 32 byte page key, compared with memcmp over all bytes (storage_key.hpp; bytes_hash_compare.hpp lines 31-44; db_cache.hpp lines 50-64, 102-160). In execution, persistent and transient storage are two separate immer maps keyed by the full bytes32 slot of one account state (account_state.hpp lines 52-70, 126-153), and the native runtime passes the full 32 byte key and the recipient address to the host (category/vm/runtime/storage.cpp lines 37-110). trie_db.cpp differs between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 only in include comments, and state.cpp and block_state.cpp are identical. The runtime's sha3 hashes the memory range directly with no cache (category/vm/runtime/keccak.hpp).

cleared.check: Task 1 for MegaETH (the endpoint reports mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42): the SALT bucket mapping and the plain key format.
cleared.result: A storage entry's plain key is the 20 byte address followed by the 32 byte slot, 52 bytes (salt/src/types.rs line 295). The bucket is a 64 bit hash of the plain key modulo the bucket count (salt/src/state/hasher.rs lines 40-43), so many keys share a bucket, but every lookup compares the stored plain key with the whole requested key (salt/src/state/state.rs lines 833-840 and 993-1000). A shared bucket changes storage gas (F-042, F-062 and the portal finding) and not which value is read. Cycle 9 cleared the same rule with probes; the run above adds the PoolManager's real keys.

It never rewrites a key of a user contract. opKeccak256 in OffchainLabs/go-ethereum hashes the memory range with no cache (core/vm/instructions.go lines 236-249). Both files were read on master and v3.12.0 because raw.githubusercontent.com serves no v3.13.0 tag and the fork commit inside b72783f is private (cycle 23); storage.go is byte identical on the two revisions.

cleared.check: Priority gas auctions on Arbitrum One, which replaced Timeboost: whether ordering by priority fee lets an ordinary account reach other users' funds in the PoolManager.
cleared.result: Ordering decides only which transaction runs first. Each unlock runs to completion inside one transaction and reverts as a whole unless every delta is settled (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), and the mempool stays private, so an account can pay to run before or after a visible transaction from the feed but cannot see pending ones or insert work inside another account's unlock. What a later swap loses to an earlier one is bounded by the price limit and the router's minimum amount, as on Ethereum.

cleared.check: shift_literal_by_non_literal in the v0.16.6 and v0.16.7 emitter, used by the tick bitmap masks shl(and(tick,0xff),1) and 1 << bitPos (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:73, :110), read again line by line.
cleared.result: For SHL, the 96-byte table holds 7 as the bit mask, 32 zero bytes, then the value. The window load at value minus k bytes and the carry load one byte lower are shifted per 64-bit lane by b bits, and the carry is moved right by 8. With the count clamped to 256, this gives bit i of lane j equal to bit 64j+i-8k-b of the value for every count from 0 to 256. SHR and SAR use value, fill, fill words, the mask at offset 80, and the mirror image of this rule. The fill is all ones for a negative literal under SAR. The highest byte any load reaches is the first byte of the third word, which holds fill. Cycle 16 ran 46 micro programs per shape and a planted fault on this path. The reading agrees with them.

cleared.check: The once-per-element memory bound check of v0.16.6 (emitter.cpp lines 6301-6313 at v0.16.7).
cleared.result: The check is skipped only when the same stack element, holding the same offset, already passed a check for at least the same read size in the same compiled block. Memory never shrinks within a frame, and a failed first check leaves the frame. So the skip never admits an access the full check would refuse, and it never omits an expansion charge, which is zero for memory already allocated. Cycle 23 ran the PoolManager natively at v0.16.7 with this code and found no difference from the interpreter.

cleared.check: Whether the Barrett reduction added to uint256.hpp on main reaches any EVM opcode handler.
cleared.result: It does not. Of 109 VM and runtime files on main, only uint256.hpp contains it. The mulmod that runtime/math.hpp calls is the division-based one (uint256.hpp lines 955-962 on main), and math.hpp changed only in an include and a revision constant. The udivrem change on main (the remainder is taken from the n significant words, and the rest is zero) gives the same words as v0.16.7, because Knuth division leaves the higher words of the normalised numerator zero.

cleared.check: Whether public endpoints and validators can disagree silently about a PoolManager result.
cleared.result: The public endpoints serve stored call frames (debug_traceTransaction with callTracer answered on rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz and rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com on 2026-11-26), so they run --trace_calls and execute blocks with the interpreter (cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7). Monad's asynchronous execution page says a node whose delayed merkle root disagrees falls out of consensus and re-executes. rpc.monad.xyz served latest block 125,590,812 and finalized block 125,590,811, both at most one second old. Its interpreter state therefore agreed with the validator-voted roots at the tip that day. A divergence would stall the tracing fleet. It would not stay hidden.

cleared.check: Lead L-1085: how far unsafe runs ahead of safe, who can replace those blocks, and whether forno's op-geth backend serves replaced blocks.
cleared.result: Celo about 330 seconds to safe and 21 minutes to finalized, X Layer about 90 seconds and 22 minutes. Replacing an unsafe block needs the sequencer or an L1 reorganisation before the batch lands, which is operator level. cleared.check: Task 2: which checks a transaction passes at acceptance and which run only at execution, and every way a transaction of an accepted block can end differently from what the builder assumed.
cleared.result: At building and at verification (VerifyBlock rebuilds the block and compares hashes, sae/blocks.go:59-98) worstcase.ApplyTx runs txpool.ValidateTransaction against the worst-case header (legacy, 2930 and 1559 types only, so no EIP-7702 delegation can appear, worstcase/state.go:181-195), refuses senders with code (lines 207-209), checks exact nonce, fee cap against the worst-case base fee, block gas left, and balance for gasLimit times the worst-case price plus value, on the settled state minus every earlier debit of the unsettled blocks (lines 239-322, sae/block_builder.go:181-235). At execution saexec.Execute applies every transaction of the block in order with core.ApplyTransaction on the state left by the previous one (saexec/execution.go:346-364). An error that is not a revert is fatal and stops the node (lines 362-364, 97-103); nothing is skipped and nothing is reordered. The libevm checks that run only at execution are CanExecuteTransaction, which returns nil on the C-Chain (cchain/hooks.go:245-247), and InvalidateExecution, which no code in avalanchego 1.15.3 calls (search of the whole tree). The only values that differ from the header are BASEFEE and the effective GASPRICE: the header carries the worst-case base fee (ACP-194 baseFeePerGas rule) and execution uses the gas clock base fee, which is at most that (saexec/execution.go:325-332). Gas charged is max(gasUsed, ceil(gasLimit/2)) after execution (hook/hook.go:218-221); this does not change the GAS opcode or what any call returns. A transaction that reverts rolls back all of its PoolManager writes as on Ethereum, and transient storage is replaced per transaction by StateDB.Prepare (libevm core/state_transition.go:436, core/state/statedb.go:1335). So the PoolManager cannot be left with an unlock half applied (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25), with transient storage from an earlier transaction, or with a native payout made and the rest of the transaction dropped (src/types/Currency.sol:48).

cleared.check: Task 3: can an ordinary account use the gap between acceptance and execution against another user, and how receipts and logs are served for accepted blocks not yet executed.
cleared.result: Receipts exist only after execution: RecentReceipt blocks until the transaction has executed (saexec/receipts.go:48-73), getReceipts goes through restoreExecutedBlock and returns nothing for an unexecuted block (sae/rpc/receipts.go:28-41), logs are read from the database written at MarkExecuted (sae/rpc/receipts.go:77-79, blocks/execution.go:142), and the log filter backend treats any header above the last executed block as absent and resolves latest through the same rule (sae/rpc/filters.go:34-35, 121-127). Execution is deterministic and the order is fixed at acceptance, so a receipt served at latest is what every honest node computes; settlement (safe) about five seconds later records the agreed state root (ACP-194, blocks/access.go:110-123). An attacker cannot place a transaction ahead of one already accepted, and a victim transaction priced against latest executes on latest plus at most the accepted blocks ahead of it, which is the same exposure as pending transactions on Ethereum and is bounded by the victim router slippage limit. No path lets an ordinary account take or freeze another user funds through the gap.

cleared.check: Task 5 and lead L-1072: is Firewood the C-Chain database at 1.15.3, and does its key encoding add a rule below the bit 248 transform.
cleared.result: Firewood is opt-in. The state scheme defaults to the empty string (cchain/config.go:85, not set in defaultConfig at 127-139), and the empty scheme selects HashDB (saedb/tracker.go:121-126). When Firewood is chosen, its storage key is keccak256(address) followed by keccak256 of the full 32-byte slot as handed down by the StateDB (firewood/base_trie.go:18-33), the same path an MPT uses; the slot it receives is already the output of the bit 248 transform (cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go:47-56). Firewood therefore adds no fold of its own. Validators must agree on the settled state root in every header (ACP-194 block settlement), so a store that keyed differently would fork the node away. No public endpoint states which scheme it runs.

cleared.check: Task 1 for reth v2.11.0 (Ethereum endpoint as recorded in cycle 24) and Tempo's pinned reth rev 167933d (reth-engine-tree 2.11.0 in Tempo's Cargo.lock). Where the commit-without-rerun path is, what it records, how it validates, and whether producers use it.
cleared.result: The path is PrewarmResults::take_valid in payload_processor/reuse.rs. The Tempo rev differs from the v2.11.0 tag only in test attributes. The read set holds every storage word loaded from the database with its value (RecordingDb::get_storage, lines 917-937), every account loaded with nonce, balance and code hash but not the code bytes (get_account, lines 882-900; without_code, 945-949), a flag that rejects the result when code was loaded by a hash the database does not know (902-915, 460), and the block environment fields COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, PREVRANDAO and GASLIMIT (1027-1049). Block hashes and transient storage are not recorded: block hashes are fixed by the parent, and transient storage is not a database input. Before commit, every storage read must equal the current value (validate, 285-290) and every account must be identical, except that a balance may differ when the transaction did not observe it, both balances are nonzero and below 2^128, and the account was not created, destroyed or wiped (compare, 375-402; 305-307). BALANCE, SELFBALANCE, SELFDESTRUCT and an out-of-funds call make a balance exact (61-71, 1027-1055, 1070-1078). A value send records the smallest balance left, which becomes an AtLeast bound (1001-1019, 484-496). The path runs only in engine validation of received blocks (ConfigureEvm::reuses_prewarm_results doc, reth crates/evm/evm/src/lib.rs lines 669-686). It needs the flag --engine.prewarm-reuse, which defaults to false (crates/node/core/src/args/engine.rs lines 570-577; TreeConfig default prewarm_reuse false, crates/engine/primitives/src/config.rs lines 286, 376). Ethereum's EthEvmConfig opts in (crates/ethereum/evm/src/lib.rs lines 489-493). TempoEvmConfig's ConfigureEvm impl (tempo crates/evm/src/lib.rs line 224) does not override the default of false, so a Tempo node never reuses through this path, whatever the flag says. A wrong reuse during validation could only make a node reject a correct block, because the header's state root is checked. It cannot make a wrong state canonical.

cleared.check: Tempo v1.19.1 block producer (payload builder): does it commit a speculative result without running the transaction again?
cleared.result: It can, under narrow conditions. With prewarming on (the default) and the hidden flag --builder.parallel (default false; the node warns that it 'is still in development and should not be used', crates/node/src/node.rs lines 131-133, 172, 194-201, 1054-1072), the builder commits a recorded replay through execute_transaction_with_actions (crates/payload/builder/src/lib.rs lines 653-668). Replays are made only for transactions that is_parallel_candidate accepts: TIP-1045 payment-lane transactions with a nonzero nonce key (crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs lines 177-178, 497-508). A payment-lane transaction must call a TIP-20 token or the TIP-20 channel reserve with payment calldata (crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs lines 299-312, 622-637). No call to the PoolManager can qualify. Replay checks every recorded account (lines 96-111 of crates/evm/src/action_replay.rs), rechecks exact SLOADs, and applies balance changes as Sinc and Sdec deltas on the current value with overflow and underflow checks (lines 123-170). A reverted transaction is not replayed (lines 45-48). So a TIP-20 transfer to the PoolManager committed by replay in transaction A credits the exact delta. Transaction B's sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) then run normally on the committed state. With the default flags every pool transaction runs normally (lines 474-489, 93, 113-120 of prewarming.rs return without_replay when not parallel). Tempo validators have no reuse path (previous item).

cleared.check: Do the reth-derived nodes behind the OP Stack, Celo, X Layer, Arc and MegaETH endpoints contain a commit-without-rerun path? Client builds were read with web3_clientVersion this session (work/clientversions.json).

The prewarm task of those forks only sends proof targets from speculative runs. It saves to the cache the state of the real execution (arc-reth prewarm.rs lines 229-253, 297), so it is cache warming only. Cycle 24 read that cache. Releases with the file are op-reth v2.8.1 (OP Mainnet), op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 (Unichain, Ink, Soneium) and base v1.6.0-rc.3 (reth-engine-tree 2.8.1). The v2.8.1 logic matches v2.11.0 in revm form: exact storage, an unknown-code reject, BALANCE, SELFBALANCE, SELFDESTRUCT and OutOfFunds observation, and the same balance rules (reth v2.8.1 reuse.rs lines 276, 369-390, 427, 454, 907-917, 1016-1075). The path needs the engine flag (default false, v2.8.1 engine.rs lines 603-606) and an EvmConfig that opts in. The trait default is false (v2.8.1 crates/evm/evm/src/lib.rs lines 528-530). OpEvmConfig at op-reth/v2.8.1 and v2.10.0-rc.4 (rust/op-reth/crates/evm/src/lib.rs) and BaseEvmConfig at base v1.6.0-rc.3 (crates/execution/evm/src/config.rs line 141) do not override it. cleared.check: Monad v0.16.7 optimistic execution and merge: read set, validation before merge, and whether producer and validator share it.
cleared.result: Every transaction runs against the block state up to that point. After the previous transaction is done, it is merged only if BlockState::can_merge accepts its originals; otherwise it runs again and must merge (execute_transaction.cpp lines 456-497). Validators run the same code, so this one path decides the canonical state. can_merge compares every original storage word with the block's current word, and a word the block state has not seen must be zero (block_state.cpp lines 156-192). An account that differs passes only through try_fix_account_mismatch (state.cpp lines 650-710). That function refuses when either side is dead, or the code hash, incarnation or nonce differ, or relaxed validation is off, or the balance was read exactly, or the new balance is below the recorded minimum. Otherwise it shifts the current balance by the difference. Every balance read through the host sets validate_exact_balance (evmc_host.cpp line 87 calls State::get_balance, state.cpp lines 233-241). A debit records a minimum or exact balance (state.cpp line 712 onward). Original values for SSTORE gas are the recorded originals. Transient storage belongs to the per-transaction State object. Code is keyed by the code hash that is compared. Every PoolManager input listed in the task is in this read set.

cleared.check: bor v2.11.1 BlockSTM: does a speculative result become canonical without a serial check?
cleared.result: No. On import, ProcessBlock races the V2 parallel processor against the serial processor. The parallel result is checked against the header by validateStateForPipeline before it is used. On error the node falls back to the serial result (core/blockchain.go lines 1308-1420). The block producer (miner/worker.go) has no parallel or BlockSTM path, so Polygon blocks are produced serially. A wrong speculative read set could only make an importer fall back or reject a block. The V1 StateDB records balance, nonce, code, self-destruct and storage reads in MVHashMap (core/state/statedb.go lines 1053-1201) and has no relaxed balance rule.

cleared.check: BNB Smart Chain v1.8.2 and reth-bsc: speculative paths.

cleared.check: Task 2: the PoolManager inputs that a speculative result could get wrong. These are its own native balance, a token balance changed earlier in the block, transient storage, hook code created earlier in the block, and original slot values for SSTORE gas.
cleared.result: The PoolManager never reads its own native balance. Currency.balanceOfSelf with address zero (src/types/Currency.sol:90-92) is reachable only from sync and settle, and both take the native branch first: sync resets the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283) and settle uses msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). Native take sends value with CALL (src/types/Currency.sol:45-49). A send with too little balance fails, and both reth and Monad record such a send as a minimum or exact balance. Case by case for reth v2.11.0. (a) Native transfer in A, then native settle or take in B: the balance is unobserved and B's changes are applied as a delta on the current balance (reuse.rs lines 296-321), and a take is bounded by AtLeast. (b) Token transfer in A, then sync and settle in B: balanceOf reads token storage, which is compared exactly (285-290). (c) Initialize in A, then swap in B: slot0 and the pool words are storage, compared exactly. (d) Hook deployed in A and called in B: B's account read of the hook changes from None to Some and gives Differs (376-379), or the code hash comes from A's published prediction and is compared. Unknown code is rejected (902-915). (e) ERC-6909 mint in A, then burn in B: storage. (f) A reverts after a successful speculative run: B is validated against the state that block execution actually committed (take_valid reads the executor's database, 223-247), and a replaced prediction is retracted (179-187). (g) SSTORE gas and refunds: the first SSTORE of a word loads it through get_storage, so the original value is a recorded read. Transient storage (src/libraries/Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol) is per transaction in evm2 (cycle 24, evm2 state/mod.rs lines 799-812) and is not an input across transactions. Monad answers each case the same way through can_merge, with exact storage and code hash and an exact observed balance. No input of a PoolManager transaction falls outside these read sets.

cleared.check: Task 3: the returned words against arithmetic that does not come from src/. For each swap the exact amounts over the part of the move inside the position, A0 = L*2^96*(b-a)/(a*b) and A1 = L*(b-a)/2^96 as Fractions; the pool must receive gross g with g*(1e6-f) >= 1e6*A_in, pay o <= A_out, take at most |amountSpecified| on exact input, pay at most amountSpecified on exact output, credit fee growth of at most g - A_in, and after settlement hold the deposits plus the swap delta. Donate: delta equals the amounts, fee growth is floor(a*2^128/L) and the PoolManager holds deposits plus donation. Clear, settleFor and ERC-6909: conservation of deltas, token units and claims.

cleared.check: Task 4: the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:40-52). Boundaries per price; whether a wrapped product can pass line 43; and whether a swap step can reach the fallback and return.
cleared.result: A wrapped product never passes line 43: with a*s >= 2^256 the EVM product is a*s - k*2^256 < a*s, so its quotient by a is below s (300020 searched pairs, seed 25025, none). Line 45 wraps for a in [ceil((2^256 - L*2^96)/s), floor((2^256-1)/s)]. Because the fallback consumes the whole remaining amount, the specified amount must fit int128 at src/libraries/Pool.sol:455-459, so a <= 2^127 and the step starts above 2^128.99 (a positive tick). TickBitmap.nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord never targets below the start of the word that holds tick 0 (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:85-105), so the target is at least 2^96; a below the amount to target then needs L*s/s_t > 2^160, the pool must hold more than about 2^160 units of currency1 in that range, and the step output is at least about 2^64*s_t, above 2^127, so amountCalculated.toInt128 reverts. 46206 sampled reachable inputs (16637 at line 45, 29569 at line 43) all give an output of at least 2^160, a next price at or above the exact N/(N/s + a) and at or above the target. No grid swap with real deposits reached the fallback (no case of ids 0 to 1394 took pc 23900 fallthrough or pc 23942 taken). With pool state written by override (spacing 32767, L 2^100, 2^120 and 2^128-1, prices 2^130, 2^150 and 2^159.9) 54 swaps were run around the boundaries and 24 of them reached the fallback through line 43 or line 45; all 54 revert with SafeCastOverflow on all 21 networks, in the reference and in Monad's interpreter and native code. A wrong word there cannot pay out the real currency: no input lets the swap return.

cleared.check: L-1100: with --builder.parallel or the T15 test is_payment_v3, can a replayed action reach a contract other than a TIP-20 token or the channel reserve, for example a TIP-20 transfer to the PoolManager followed by settle.

Both payment rules require every call to target a TIP-20 address (0x20c0 prefix) with a recognised payment selector or the channel reserve, and forbid access lists and authorization lists (crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs:282-330, 622-637); v3 only adds trailing bytes and voucher signatures. A TIP-20 transfer whose recipient is the PoolManager is a candidate, but a TIP-20 transfer is a precompile write and runs no code at the recipient, so no PoolManager code runs in the replay. The PoolManager's settle in the next transaction is not a payment and always runs serially (crates/payload/builder/src/lib.rs:653-668), reading the token balance the replay wrote. A replay that no longer applies is skipped as invalid_replay (lib.rs:713-731). Replay exists only in the block builder; other validators execute the block through newPayload, so a replay that diverged from serial execution gives a state root they reject and the block is not finalized. Parallel building is off unless the operator enables it (lib.rs:153-154).

cleared.check: Task 5: does anything in src/ depend on finality, including ERC-6909 claims and protocol fee accrual.
cleared.result: No. unlock opens the lock, runs the callback and reverts unless the nonzero delta count is zero before it locks again (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114); take, settle, settleFor, clear, mint and burn all require the lock and only move transient deltas besides the transfer or claim write (src/PoolManager.sol:291-336, 349-364). The lock, deltas, delta count and synced reserves live in transient storage (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32), so nothing carries between transactions. sync may run without the lock but only writes transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). ERC-6909 transfer, transferFrom, approve and setOperator are plain storage writes (src/ERC6909.sol:25-64). Protocol fees accrue in persistent storage within the same swap transaction (src/ProtocolFees.sol:66-70) and are withdrawn only by the controller (lines 44-57). No file in src/ outside src/test reads block.number, block.timestamp, blockhash, tx.origin or any other block field (search of src/). A replaced block removes every PoolManager effect of its transactions together, so core has no state that a later block can see half applied.

cleared.check: Task 1: what happens to a notarized block whose execution turns out wrong under T14.
cleared.result: It is not finalized. A validator whose certify returns false broadcasts nullify for that view and does not build on the block; a finalization needs a quorum of certify results (commonware-consensus 2026.11.0 simplex/mod.rs:106-111, 138-140). The chain does not halt on one bad block: the view is nullified and the next leader proposes on a certified parent. Validators that cannot complete verification withhold their finalize vote and count as faulty for that view (marshal/standard/deferred.rs:33-37). No slashing of the proposer was found in the files read. The executor treats an INVALID answer as the verdict and caches it (crates/consensus/src/executor/actor.rs:64-80).

cleared.check: ParseBytes.parseSelector (src/libraries/ParseBytes.sol:9-14) and parseFee (16-21) load a full word into a bytes4 and a uint24 without masking. Does a hook answer with nonzero bytes after the selector, a caller whose address has nonzero upper bytes (so the first calldata word carries them), or a fee word with bits above 24 change the outcome?
cleared.result: No. In the reference EVM with the driver at an address whose upper 16 bytes are nonzero and hooks that pad the selector with 0xff bytes, all ten hook functions are accepted exactly as with zero padding (out/dirtysel.json), so the compiled comparison at Hooks.sol:152 cleans both sides to 4 bytes. Fee words 2^255 | 0x400000 | 500 and 2^24 | 0x400000 | 500 behave as 0x400000 | 500, and 2^24 | 500 as no override, on all 21 networks, because isOverride and removeOverrideFlag mask (src/libraries/LPFeeLibrary.sol:61-70). cleared.result: Every native settle case returns the reference words on every network. settle or settleFor with value while an ERC-20 is synced reverts with NonzeroNativeValue and the value stays with the caller. A take above the PoolManager's balance or at 2^127 reverts. A take to a recipient that rejects value reverts with WrappedError(NativeTransferFailed), so the debit is undone. Where a recipient has code on one network and not on another the outcome differs (listed per network in the first cleared item), and every such difference changes only whether the caller's own payout goes through or lands at that address. A take to the PoolManager itself reverts everywhere, because the contract has no receive or fallback function. No take or settle credited anyone other than the caller or the named recipient.

cleared.check: Which precompile addresses answer a value call with empty input differently from Ethereum (Prague and Osaka rules: 0x09 to 0x11 fail on empty input, EIP-2537 says an error burns all gas supplied).
cleared.result: On Avalanche and HyperEVM the addresses 0x0b to 0x11 accept the payout, so they hold no BLS12-381 precompile at the endpoint's fork, and a native take there leaves the caller's own value at that address. The call to 0x100 with empty input succeeds on these two and on Ethereum alike (checked on reth v2.11.0 and on eth.drpc.org on 2026-11-26), so it says nothing about a P-256 precompile. On Polygon 0x0a accepts the payout on the drpc gateway and on polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), so bor has no point evaluation precompile there. On api.avax.network 0x0a fails with invalid input length and 0x0b accepts. On every other network these addresses fail as on Ethereum. The PoolManager neither calls precompiles itself nor reads their answers apart from the success flag of a payout the caller chose.

cleared.result: 562 of 575 cases (v0.16.7) and 561 (v0.16.5) give the same result in both engines and, apart from harness modelling of balances and precompiles, the reference words. All 143 native value cases agree between engines once the harness balance lines are written as 64 hex digits (the first run wrote odd-length hex, which the harness misreads). 13 hook cases differ: the native side reverts the whole unlock with empty data in 12 and the interpreter side in 1. The same PoolManager call sent alone (initialize with an afterInitialize hook that returns 1 to 31 bytes) gives InvalidHookResponse in both engines, a rebuild of the harness that only records each call's result after it returns makes 10 of the 13 agree and leaves 3 others different, and zeroing or filling the native stack changes nothing. A result that moves with host-side bookkeeping points at the harness's host process, not at Monad's EVM semantics. The root cause was not found; it is a lead.

cleared.check: Task 1, distribution of the Monad mainnet validator binary. Monad's node operator documentation installs the apt package monad from https://pkg.category.xyz/ (suite noble), version 0.16.5 for mainnet and 0.16.7 for testnet. The repository index (InRelease dated 18 Nov 2026, Packages.gz sha256 7ad122d7...19357) lists monad 0.16.5 as pool/main/monad_0.16.5_amd64.deb, size 739,508,498, sha256 0b27486fc85fefedfdb44637e1ee52a1f59e0287594562f5260fa86abf62acc8, description 'Monad BFT stack (with debug symbols)'. The file was downloaded without credentials into research/network-risk/cycles/026/theme-monad-shipped-binary.work/dl and its sha256 equals the index value.
cleared.result: The package can be fetched, so the shipped binary is open to inspection. Its data.tar and control.tar are zstd compressed, no zstd tool or Python module is installed, and building zstd from its release source inside the work directory was refused by this session's permission system, so no file of the package was unpacked and no ELF reading was done. The build recipe of the tagged source was read instead: monad-bft v0.16.5 docker/devnet/Dockerfile builds with gcc-15 and g++-15 and ASMFLAGS, CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS of -march=haswell (C and C++ also -fno-omit-frame-pointer), Rust with target-cpu=haswell, through cargo build --release, and links the execution library from the monad-execution submodule; the execution toolchain gcc-avx2.cmake sets -march=haswell for ASM, C and C++; asmjit is built from third_party/asmjit as a static library (CMakeLists.txt:69-71). The cycle 23 harness used clang++ -O2 -march=haswell with asmjit e8c8e2e4. The emitter passes the runtime's CPU features to asmjit only to initialise the code holder (emitter.cpp:734) and validates instructions only in testing builds (emitter.cpp:614-616), so the emitted bytes do not depend on the validator's CPU. cleared.check: Task 3, effect 1: the interpreter side of the cycle 25 harness gave different results for one scenario when the world held 3,066 token accounts (rep1369.txt). Rerun here: the scenario five times in one process with the large world gives five different top level gasleft values on each engine (for example 149823397 interpreted and 149808185 native on the first repetition), the same sequence in two processes, while the small world gives 149618850 on both engines in every repetition. Only the driver's top level gas differs; every step line, storage word, balance and log is the same.
cleared.result: The cause is the harness host. Host::call copies the whole World before each call and assigns the copy back when the call fails (research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/src/harness.cpp:413, 424). libstdc++ map assignment destroys and rebuilds each node, so the code vector of every contract is freed and allocated again. The calling frame still runs with runtime::Context::env.code pointing at the old code buffer (research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/src/harness.cpp:236, 244). Valgrind reports 50 contexts of invalid reads in copy_impl called from CODECOPY, all inside the freed 9,537 byte block that holds the driver contract, from the interpreter and from native code. What CODECOPY reads then depends on how the allocator reused the freed block, which the 3,066 token entries copied on every call change. Controls: under valgrind, which never reuses a freed block at once, the large world gives 149618850 on both engines in all five repetitions (SAME); with MALLOC_PERTURB_=165 or 90 the small world varies too. The PoolManager runtime has no CODECOPY (scan of build/PoolManager.json), so no PoolManager code was read from freed memory. In the node, Context::from takes the code span from the Intercode, which a shared pointer keeps alive for the whole call (vm.cpp:83-84, code.hpp:36-62), and a revert does not free it. This is not Monad code and a validator cannot hit it.

cleared.check: Task 4, places where the interpreter and native code of v0.16.5 could differ by design. Native code subtracts a block's whole static gas on entry (x86.cpp:443-448) and tests the sign only at JUMPDEST blocks or after 1,000 gas of unchecked static work (emitter.cpp:1030-1046, 1284-1298, emitter.hpp:51). Stack bounds are tested once per block in block_prologue (emitter.cpp:1301-1333). Runtime routines add the remaining block base gas back before the CALL 63/64 rule and the SSTORE sentry (call.cpp:136-147, storage.cpp:70-73), and the depth limit and memory expansion are runtime code shared by both engines (call.cpp:152-154, types.hpp:330-341). copy_result_data turns a negative gas_remaining at STOP, RETURN or REVERT into out of gas (context.cpp:174-176).
cleared.result: When a frame cannot pay a block, both engines fail the frame with all gas consumed; native code may fail earlier inside the block, or at the next check up to 1,000 gas later, and reports Error where the interpreter reports out of gas, which a caller sees only as failure. The static cost of a block is paid by the interpreter before it leaves the block, and dynamic costs are computed by the same runtime, so a block that fails on one engine fails on the other. In the PoolManager build there are 917 blocks by Monad's splitting rule (cycle 23 counted 913 entered or reachable); 49 of them hold 64 instructions with an effect outside the frame (39 SSTORE, 8 TSTORE, 12 LOG, 4 CALL, 1 STATICCALL) followed by more instructions of the same block. Every block with static gas has its out of gas test moved to its start. In those 49 blocks, an out of gas run lists an outgoing call or a write on the interpreter side that native code never makes. The failing frame is reverted on both sides, so no PoolManager storage word, transient word, balance, log or outgoing call that persists can differ, which matches the 20 cycle 23 runs whose frame lists differed with equal state. These files were read at v0.16.5; mainnet runs 0.16.7, and the reread at that tag is an open lead.

cleared.check: Task 4: bor's MULMOD memo at the newest tag that has it (v2.12.0-beta) and on develop, which is the only ref that carries Salvador (SalvadorBlock 98688600 at params/config.go:478 on develop; v2.12.0-beta has no Salvador entry; tags v2.12.0, v2.12.0-beta2, v2.12.0-beta3, v2.12.0-rc1, v2.12.1 and v2.11.3 return 404). Exact reuse condition and proof that a reused reciprocal belongs to the same full 256 bit modulus.
cleared.result: core/vm/mulmod_memo.go is byte identical on v2.12.0-beta and develop, and so are core/vm/evm.go, instructions.go and interpreter.go. opMulmod pops x and y by value and passes z = the stack top (instructions.go:200-205). An entry is reused only when z[3] != 0 and mm.ok and mm.mod == *z (mulmod_memo.go:56-57), where mm.mod is a uint256.Int, an array of four uint64, so the comparison is on all 256 bits. On a miss the code stores a value copy of *z in mm.mod and mm.mu = uint256.Reciprocal(z) before z is written (lines 58-60). The reciprocal in mm.mu is therefore always the reciprocal of exactly the value in mm.mod, and a hit requires mm.mod to equal the new modulus in every limb, so a reused reciprocal belongs to the same full modulus. MulModWithReciprocal (holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 uint256.go:688-715) then runs the same umul and reduce4(&p, m, mu) as MulMod (uint256.go:720-735) with mu equal to Reciprocal(m), with z aliasing m in both, so the word is the stock word. Narrow moduli (z[3] == 0) and m == 0 bypass the memo. The memo is a field of the EVM (evm.go:217-219) and is never cleared; it outlives frames, reverts and transactions of one EVM, which is harmless because its value is a function of its key. Direct test: memo.go copied verbatim from v2.12.0-beta, compiled with go1.24.7 against uint256 v1.3.2 source, one memo instance for the whole run, consecutive moduli sharing the top limb, the bottom limb, three limbs, the top or bottom 192 bits, differing by one in the top limb, or repeating, each pair also run as FullMath does with 2^256-1 between: seed 2026112626, 1,000,000 pairs, 5,000,000 MULMODs, 1,271,986 memo hits, 0 mismatches against math/big; seed 2026112627, 250,000 pairs, 0 mismatches. A planted fault keying the memo on limb 3 only does not finish 10 pairs in 20 seconds (reduce4's final subtraction loop at mod.go:450-461 runs with the reciprocal of another modulus), so a stale entry cannot pass unseen.

cleared.check: How often the PoolManager itself can meet the memo with a repeated or a near-equal modulus. Every MULMOD the PoolManager frames execute in sequences a64, a512 and b was traced in the reference interpreter.
cleared.result: a512: 5288 MULMODs, 3328 with a full-width modulus, 257 distinct full-width moduli, 2816 of them 2^256-1, 512 changes of modulus, none to a modulus that shares limb 3 or limb 0 with the one before. Every full-width denominator is preceded by mulmod(a, b, not(0)) (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24), so a one-entry memo holds 2^256-1 whenever a new denominator arrives; the only hits on a denominator are FullMath.sol:48 followed by :112 for the same denominator in mulDivRoundingUp. A memo that keyed on one limb would therefore be exposed by PoolManager swaps only for a denominator whose keyed limb is all ones, and the a512 sequence exposes it 0 times. The memo check rests on the raw sequences of established-l1 (20,000 records on every Polygon endpoint) and on the direct test above; the PoolManager sequences check that the whole path returns the same words.

cleared.check: Base Everest phases (Base Transactions) and transient storage: can a discarded phase or the end of a phased transaction leave an unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency for later code.

The transaction ends in commit_tx, which clears transient storage (inner.rs:141-171), or in discard_tx on error (eip8130.rs:1815-1835). The PoolManager therefore sees the same lifetimes as in a multicall from one sender: Lock, NonzeroDeltaCount and CurrencyReserves (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) live for one transaction, and unlock still checks the delta count before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114).

cleared.check: L-1129, the rule. How the HyperEVM archive client nanoreth (tag nb-20261125-2) decides that a transaction is a system transaction and where it takes the sender from.
cleared.result: A transaction is a system transaction when gas_price() is Some(0) (src/node/primitives/transaction.rs:182-184, src/node/evm/executor.rs:44-49). For such a transaction recover_signer, recover_signer_unchecked and recover_unchecked_with_buf return s_to_address(s): s equal to 1 gives 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, s equal to (1<<160)|1 gives 0x00..01, and any other s gives its low 20 bytes (transaction.rs:49-58 and 77-97). The file header calls this a pseudo signer for system transactions, and address_to_s (transaction.rs:61-69) is the encoder. The system transactions come from the block source as a separate list system_txs with an optional from field (src/node/types/mod.rs:114-128 and 285-290), and the official endpoint serves them under its own method eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber. The synthetic signature is therefore the replica's encoding of what the producer wrote, not a rule that any public endpoint applies to a signed transaction a user submits. If the producer ever put a regular transaction with gas price 0 into a block, the replica would take its sender from s and show state the producer did not compute; that would mislead replica readers and would not change the chain. Under EIP-1559 such a transaction is invalid because the base fee is nonzero in every block read. The cycle 23 census of mined blocks found none below 100,000,000 wei; during verification eth_feeHistory predicted 96,659,059 and 89,439,317 wei for a next block, so 100,000,000 is not a confirmed protocol floor, and any nonzero base fee is enough here. The producer's own admission rule is closed and was not read; no Hyperliquid page that states it was found.

cleared.result: No. The portal sets from to msg.sender only when EOA.isSenderEOA() holds, that is msg.sender == tx.origin, or code of exactly 23 bytes that starts with 0xEF0100 (an EIP-7702 delegation); otherwise from is the L1 to L2 alias (OptimismPortal2.sol:939-943, EOA.sol:9-24 on the develop branch). EIP-3541 forbids deployed code starting with 0xEF, so a contract cannot pass the check, and the first two cases need a key for the L1 address. The PoolManager addresses and their alias preimages have no code and nonce 0 on Ethereum (F-140), and finding a key or CREATE2 input for a chosen 160-bit address costs about 2^160. Only a portal upgrade by its upgrader can emit such a deposit, which F-140 records at governance level.

cleared.check: Tempo type 0x76: can a batch, a Keychain signature, a key authorization, a fee payer, a Tempo authorization list or a configurable account make the PoolManager the sender (tempo v1.19.1-a9d6748 answers on the endpoint; source tree of v1.19.1 read).
cleared.result: No. The sender is the address derived from a secp256k1, P256 or WebAuthn public key (spec, Address Derivation). A Keychain signature names user_address, prepare_keychain rejects it unless it equals the recovered signer, and the access key must be registered for that account in AccountKeychain (crates/evm/src/handler.rs:655-676). A key authorization must be signed by the root key of the account or by an admin access key already registered for it, with account equal to the signer (handler.rs:504-627). A configurable account role is refused when the account has code other than the configurable account code (valid_account_code, crates/precompiles/src/configurable_account/mod.rs:272-279, used in handler/configurable_account/mod.rs:350-356), and without a stored commitment its address must equal the hash derivation of the config (crates/primitives/src/transaction/configurable_account/mod.rs:384-414). The PoolManager has 24,009 bytes of code and no key, so none of these paths can name it. A fee payer pays fees and never becomes a caller, and every call of a batch has the one signer as caller (cycle 21 clearances).

cleared.check: Task 2: what one party of a shared transaction can leave for a later party through the transient state of sync (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36), and whether any of it moves funds.
cleared.result: Only the synced currency and its reserves outlive a call; unlock clears the lock flag and requires every delta to be zero before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Left behind, a synced token makes a later native settle revert with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356), which F-071 records as low. A stale reserve R makes a later settle without its own sync credit balanceOf minus R: if the balance fell since (a take), the subtraction reverts (checked arithmetic, src/PoolManager.sol:360); if it rose, the extra is a payment some account made to the PoolManager after that sync without settling it, which is the first party's own gift or the F-137 pattern. resetCurrency clears only the currency slot (CurrencyReserves.sol:21-25), and sync writes currency and reserves together (CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so no sequence pairs a currency with a reserve from another moment. Nothing moves funds of pools or claim holders. Clearing between transactions was shown on 16 networks with eth_simulateV1 in cycle 21; Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc and HyperEVM still have no eth_simulateV1 today, so they rest on the client readings of earlier cycles.

The public stateless validator recomputes each block's state root with mega-evm (cleared in cycle 19), so such a patch would show as a failed validation on the first block whose transaction met that edge.
